News.title: China’s new invasion target revealed as Xi Jinping builds huge island fortresses in WW3 flashpoint that could test Trump
News.content:
XI Jinping is feared to have found his next target as the Chinese dictator sets his eyes on the Philippines – risking all out war with Donald Trump.

President Xi’s obsession with making China the sole global superpower could see him launch a daring attack and test Washington’s resolve – with a rotting US warship the most likely flashpoint.



China has been trying to grow its dominance in the South China Sea for decades under Xi.

Beijing already claims almost 90 per cent of the waters, but Xi is adamant he should control even more to create a monopoly on trade and naval abilities.





John Hemmings, the director for the National Security Centre at the Henry Jackson Society, told The Sun: “China views the South China Sea as its domain.”

The country with the most to lose if China continues to push for total regional dominance would be the Philippines, experts say.

Manila heavily relies on the South China Sea for national security and economic survival due to it being a key shipping route.

One of the most contentious areas is the sprawling Spratly Islands which is currently claimed by China, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan.



Made up of over 100 reefs, China has been caught building up new military fortresses on a trio of the surrounding islands.

Shocking surveillance footage shows some of the larger reefs sat in the most strategic positions are now flooded with Chinese military gear.

Features include a 10,000ft runway, hardened aircraft shelters, fuel and munitions storage, radar and sensor arrays, and hangars that can accommodate two dozen combat aircraft or several larger planes.

Despite China’s sweeping attempts to seize more territory, the Philippines have become a thorn in Xi’s side.



Manila has spent years standing up to the Chinese – sparking renewed fears Xi could launch an invasion to get rid of the issue entirely.

But attacking Filipino territory could have dire consequences for Beijing.

The Philippines has a firm agreement with the US stating Washington would support the country with its Navy if it ever comes under attack.

The 1951 US–Philippines Mutual Defence Treaty was recently described as being an “ironclad agreement” by Manila.



Dr Philip Shetler-Jones, an expert on Indo-Pacific security at RUSI, said: “Since President Trump visited Beijing, US-China relations are on a very stable level.

“But the reduction of tension in the relationship means it is perfectly logical and normal for China to turn on US allies in the region.

“China has a track record of taking the opportunity to make a move while assuming America and the rest of the world is distracted.

“It’s all related to the longer term objective that Beijing has to reduce the extent to which American presence in the region restricts China’s influence.



“It wants to be the dominant power in the region. The main thing standing in the way of that is currently the US alliance system.”

Terms of the pact apply to any armed attack on the Philippine armed forces, coast guard, public vessels, or aircraft anywhere in the South China Sea.

Filipino President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has already warned Beijing that any deliberate act of aggression would cross a red line.

Manila would formally invoke the treaty and ask Washington for military protection and naval escorts.



US Navy warships escorting Philippine ships would likely anger Xi, who has battled to make China the top global superpower.

A direct standoff between US and Chinese warships would leave the world in a precarious position – with fears a single shot or misfiring could spark war.

China is known to test its limits with enemies, with the Philippine Coast Guard accusing its Chinese counterpart of firing water cannons ‌at government vessels near a disputed shoal last month.



Footage also showed the Chinese Coast Guard and Philippine Navy hitting each other with oars and batons during a heated encounter at Second Thomas Shoal in the South China Sea.

It marked one of three confrontations between the two countries in the South China Sea in just seven days.

China has also been accused of shining military-grade lasers, temporarily blinding Filipino crew members.

These “grey zone” tactics have so far avoided any US response.

A blockade of a key island on the South China Sea would likely be seen as a major escalation, experts say.



Second Thomas Shoal is currently one of the strongest islands in the South China Sea not under Chinese control.

The Philippines currently has a military outpost on the shoal with marines stationed aboard a rotting World War Two-era warship named the BRP Sierra Madre who have strict instructions to protect their patch.

Due to where the warship sits, it currently blocks China’s expansion in the South China Sea – making the Sierra Madre a political signifier of who controls what in the region.



Both John and Dr Shetler-Jones say the worst- case scenario for the region would be Beijing enforcing a total blockade and surrounding the troops.

An attack by the Chinese could provoke a firefight which would see Manila invoke the treaty and call for US backup.

John said: “If China goes into the Sierra Madre and starts killing Philippine Marines, I believe and I think the US has shown itself committed to to sending in its forces to deal with that situation.”

Dr Shetler-Jones added: “One of the flashpoints is the grounded ship, the Sierra Madre, because it is an unsustainable situation.”

A provisional agreement was reportedly made in July 2025 between Beijing and Manila, which saw China promise not to encroach near the sinking vessel.



In return, the Philippines insisted it would only ever sail to the area to provide food, water and supplies to the marines on board.

But Dr Shetler-Jones believes Xi may be waiting for the Sierra Madre to be in dire need of repair so Manila sends in men to fix the ship.

“The Philippines would need to repair that ship to keep it in place to maintain this political status quo,” the expert said.



“But the Chinese would insist the agreement excluded repairs so would give them reason to kick off.”

Experts have feared a Chinese invasion of Taiwan – which forms the eastern boundary of the South China Sea – could trigger World War Three due to the self-governing island’s close ties with the US.

But John believes the Philippines could be the true next target for Xi who may use it to help him gather key intel for a future Taiwan invasion.

John said: “The Philippines is a sort of test case for how China’s going to behave in in the region.

“You already see China testing a lot of things on the Philippines that they will probably want to practice on Taiwan.



“Grey zone operations, triggering the US level of involvement and deterrence to test that resolve.

“So it’s a little bit of a laboratory. What they do to the Philippines is what they could end up doing with Taiwan.”

In recent years, images showed China had amassed vast “floating barriers” – stretching at least 200 miles in the East China Sea between themselves and Taiwan.

China has also held multiple military drills around Taiwan, involving the army, navy and air force.

Dr Shetler-Jones added: “These tactics from the China side are quite familiar, and they’ve had this repertoire for a long time.”



The US has recently bolstered its presence in Asia alongside both the Philippines and Taiwan.

They held joint military drills with Japan and the Philippines in the South China Sea and at Taiwan’s annual training days US weapons and vehicles were clearly on display.

Dr Shetler-Jones said: “When Marco Rubio was in the region, he made quite a robust statement, saying ‘we stand with our allies and we want a good relationship with China, but not if it comes at the expense of US interests or our allies’.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“So I think diplomatically, they’ve been quite firm already, because they can see things escalating and want to draw a line.”

Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS George Washington and its carrier strike group are also providing a military presence in the western Pacific after recent hostile incidents.

News.title: Desperate friend’s plea over death of American killed execution-style at tourist hotspot hours after chilling last text
News.content:
A FRIEND of an American who was killed on a beach in Puerto Rico painfully recalled the paralyzing moment she learned about his execution-style murder.

Tyler Wilkin‘s magnetic energy and upbeat persona were what drew friends like Julie Santiago to the 35-year-old Ohio native, who in January 2024 relocated to San Juan, the island’s capital.



“He loved the island. He fell in love with the people. He fell in love with nature. He fell in love with the beach, the mountains, like everything around the island,” Santiago told The U.S. Sun about her late friend Wilkin.

So when Santiago heard about Wilkin’s gruesome murder on July 10, she froze in shock.



Two days prior, Wilkin was dropped off by his girlfriend near the remote beach of Playa la Selva, a secluded forest area in the northeast corner of the island in Luquillo, where he set up a campsite.

For Wilkin’s friends, it wasn’t uncommon for the adventurous and fearless 35-year-old to pack a backpack and go camping.

“He was fearless. He wanted to be in nature. He didn’t care if it was alone or with a group of friends. And nobody could stop him because that’s who he is or he was,” Santiago said.

Wilkin would stay in contact with a group of friends and his girlfriend, Iva Mo, whom he routinely texted in the mornings.



During his stay, Wilkin began sending unsettling messages about a mysterious man in the area, whom he nicknamed “the howler.”

Wilkin told his friends that he could hear someone howling near his tent along with what sounded like fireworks.

On the night of July 9, the messages became more alarming when Wilkin informed his friends that the unknown individual was back.

“He had messaged that same friend and said, ‘The howler is back.’ And then he messaged two hours later, ‘Oh, this guy is getting rowdy lol,'” Mo told CBS affiliate WKRC.

Wilkin’s final message to friends was sent shortly before 2am.



Hours later, a beachgoer on their morning walk located Wilkin’s body at around 6am about 300 yards from his campsite with a single gunshot wound to the back of the head.

Local police believe Wilkin was shot at close range in an execution-style killing.

Santiago recalled gasping when she first learned about the details surrounding her friend’s murder.



“I just couldn’t believe it. I gasped. I was like, is this a joke? I couldn’t believe it. I froze,” the Puerto Rican native told The U.S. Sun.

“The way he died was not like him running away or anything.

“He was facing the ocean probably with his eyes closed, probably kneeling down, at three feet distance to the back of his head.

“It was an execution. And they took his wallet, so they robbed him for whatever the money he had. They took his life away. I’m just still shocked.”

Nearly a month since Wilkin’s murder, authorities in Puerto Rico have not established any significant leads on a potential suspect or suspects.



Joseph Gonzalez Falcon, the superintendent of the police force in Puerto Rico, said on Tuesday that investigators had still not obtained new information.

“I’ve mentioned that there is a person of interest in that case,” Falcon said in a press conference.

“I’ve been in contact with Tyler’s father and other friends of Tyler. As I’ve said, this, like all investigations, is a priority for us.”

Falcon previously said investigators were looking into a person of interest related to Wilkin’s murder; however, he declined to disclose additional details.

The FBI is now involved in the investigation.



Santiago believes the federal agency’s involvement could help bring Wilkin’s family and friends the closure they’ve been searching for since his body was found on the beach shoreline.

“I think it’s important to get that closure. And the only way we get that closure is to understand who did it and why,” Santiago said.

“I think it’s up to the media and the community to continue to cover Tyler’s story so that it could lead to an arrest.

“I do believe that the media plays a huge part into getting justice and closure for Tyler, and that the more that Tyler is spoken about, the more that the people start understanding what happened.

“The more that the people start understanding that this could have happened to any fisherman.



“This could have happened to anyone’s son. This could have happened to anyone because he was not in a bad route in his life.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“He was not a man to look for conflict. He would not fight anyone. You know, this could have happened to anyone.”

Friends and family of Wilkin have started a GoFundMe to raise donations to hire a private investigator.

News.title: Monk arrested after ‘stabbing fellow preacher, 27, and worker, 53, in monastery’ when asked to leave convent
News.content:
BLADE HORROR Monk arrested after ‘stabbing fellow preacher, 27, and worker, 53, in monastery’ when asked to leave convent

A MONK has been arrested after allegedly stabbing a fellow preacher in a monastery when he was asked to leave the convent.

The 51-year-old Romanian monk allegedly grabbed a box cutter and launched an attack on two men inside a monastery in Cyprus on Friday morning.



He has since been remanded in custody for six days as police investigate the alleged attempted murder.

The violent confrontation reportedly erupted after the monk was told to vacate the monastery cell he had been living in.



The cell had previously been occupied by his later father, according to the information under the investigation.

Abbot Leontios, accompanied by members of the Church committee and a maintenance worker, is understood to have gone to the monk’s cell and demanded the key at the Agios Neophytos Monastery in Paphos.



The religious figure is said to have refused to leave before suddenly grabbing a paper cutter from a desk inside the room.

Police believe he then launched a ferocious attack.

Investigators believe the abbot, who had authority to order the monk’s removal, was the intended target.

But a 53-year-old monastery employee was allegedly struck by the sharp object, suffering gruesome injuries to his neck and hand.



A second monk, aged 27, intervened during the chaos and was also injured in the hand, police said.

The 53-year-old was rushed to Paphos General Hospital, where his wounds were stitched before he was admitted for treatment.

His injuries were not considered life-threatening.

The younger monk was also taken to hospital where he received first aid before being discharged.

Police swooped on the alleged attacker later that day and arrested him.



He is being investigated for a string of serious offences, including attempted murder, acts intended to cause grievous bodily harm, wounding, carrying a knife and the illegal possession and carrying of an offensive weapon.

The case is being treated as a serious violent attack.

News.title: Moment paedo teacher who groomed & sexually assaulted schoolgirl tells cops ‘I’m going to wee my pants,’ during arrest
News.content:
THIS is the moment a paedo teacher who sexually assaulted a schoolgirl tells cops: “I’m going to wee my pants. I’m so sorry.”

David Brown, 35, bombarded the pupil with hundreds of sexual messages during a sickening 18-month grooming campaign.



Brown, who also drove the girl to secluded spots to carry out his crimes, has been jailed for 11 years after admitting a string of child sex offences.

Bodycam footage of the vile teacher’s arrest shows him squirming as he admits he is going to wet himself.



Brown stands at his front door as he is told by officers he is being arrested on suspicion of sexually grooming a child under the age of 16.

The speechless fiend looks from side to side as he is detained by cops.

He then responds: “Can I go for a wee? I’m going to pee my pants. I’m sorry.”

Police said Brown initially targeted the girl, who was a pupil at his school in Lytham St Anne’s, Lancashire, in July 2024.



He initially used his school email account to contact her, before moving their conversations onto social media and video calls.

On one occasion, Brown appeared on a video call wearing just his underwear.

He kissed the teenager in December 2025 before his offending escalated further.

Brown would drive the girl to secluded areas where he engaged in sexual activity with her.

While on other occasions he caused her to engage in sexual activity at a property.



His offending finally came to light when the girl’s parent contacted police in January, with concerns that Brown had been targeting her.

An investigation was quickly launched and officers then searched Brown’s classroom.

It was there they discovered four mobile phones hidden in one of his desk drawers.

Investigators went on to uncover roughly 700 text messages between Brown and the teenager – all of a sexual nature.

Some showed him deliberately attempting to get the girl alone so he could commit his sick offences.



Brown answered “no comment” to every question when interviewed by detectives.

He later pleaded guilty at Preston Crown Court to one count of sexual communication with a child.

The teacher also admitted three counts of sexual activity with a child and one count of causing a child to engage in sexual activity.

Brown, of no fixed address but formerly of St Annes, was jailed for 11 years and ordered to sign the sex offenders register.

Speaking after the verdict, the teen victim’s devastated mum blasted the paedophile for “stealing a year of our lives”.



She said: “This incident has kept me awake night after night for months, with feelings of guilt.

“Guilt that I was not able to do what I consider to be the most important job in the world, protecting my child.”

She added: “I feel that David has stolen a year of our lives…

“A year of childhood memories I should be making for my daughters has been taken away.

“I should be on family holidays and making positive experiences.



“Instead [the years] have been spent having to deal with David’s actions as a family together.”

DS Adam Errington, of West Child Abuse Investigation Team, hailed the victim’s bravery throughout the case.

He said: “Brown is a paedophile who tried to disguise himself as a trusted member of society.

“I can only hope that she now knows that justice has been served, and that Brown has been held accountable for his actions that were so wrong.

“He abused his position as a teacher, as a person with a responsibility for young people’s wellbeing all for his own sordid sexual interests.



“I welcome the custodial sentence against him, and hope that he uses his time behind bars to truly reflect on how reprehensible his actions were.

“I want to send a message to young people out there today who may be a victim of sexual offences, without realising they are.

“It isn’t love – it is manipulation, and it is a crime. If you or someone you know may be a victim of sexual offences, please tell us, or someone you trust.

“We will listen to you, we will believe you, and we will do all we can to get you justice.”

News.title: Twisted revenge plot saw innocent dog walker shot 30 times…how e-bike slip up and duct tape finally snared the killer
News.content:
HUNTED DOWN Twisted revenge plot saw innocent dog walker shot 30 times…how e-bike slip up and duct tape finally snared the killer

WHEN likeable country estate groundsman Brian Low was found dead while out walking his beloved black Labrador, Millie, in the Scottish countryside, it shocked the local community.

Discovered by a fellow dog walker, at a place known as Leafy Lane, police and an ambulance were called.



The first policeman to arrive believed the injuries were consistent with Brian having fallen and even the paramedic thought he had died after a sudden medical event.

Incredibly, it wasn’t until six days later that a medical examination established the injuries were consistent with being fatally shot.



He had around 30-shotgun pellets to his face and body.

When his remains reached the mortuary, shotgun pellets literally fell out of the body bag as it was opened.



“I couldn’t get my head around why somebody would want to murder Brian,” says his partner, Pam Curran.

“I don’t think he had a bad bone in his body.”



With no witnesses to the murder, police looked into who might have had a grudge against Brian.

The spotlight fell on his fellow estate worker, 75-year-old David Campbell who prosecution and several people who knew him, believe held an historic grudge against Brian for over six years.

Proving the case against him was a complex one and is comprehensively detailed in the riveting two-part documentary Murder Trial: Death of a Dog Walker, which focusses on David Cambell’s murder trial and how a bicycle, a hat and some duct tape eventually helped to bring him to justice.

Brian Low and David Campbell had been employed at Edradynate shooting estate near Aberfeldy, Perthshire.

Campbell was head gamekeeper there from May 1984 to February 2018, and Brian was a groundsman from August 2000 to February 2023.



Although accomplished in his work, David Campbell was considered to be arrogant and threatening by many who worked with him.

After he was sacked for poisoning birds of prey on the estate, he is said to have blamed Brian for talking to police and planting evidence on the estate to frame him.

“I knew Dave and Brian had a serious falling out,” says Pam.



“Whatever Brian had said to the police really angered Dave, and they had a right set to.

“Brian wouldn’t tell me the ins and outs of it but he was really upset by it.

“David Campbell’s whole life was his work.

“When it ended, probably sooner than he wanted, he wasn’t happy. But I didn’t think to the extent that he would have killed Brian.”

On the morning of Brian’s shooting, 17 February 2024, David Campbell was captured on footage from his own doorbell camera, covering it with duct tape.



CCTV from the local area, revealed a mysterious figure on an e-bike with a long bag strapped to their back, on the route from the Campbell house to the crime scene.

Was this David Campbell with a shotgun in his bag?

He denied it was him but a similar e-bike was found on his farm by police, that belonged to his wife, Elizabeth.



Further CCTV showed a horse startled in a field near the crime scene around the time Brian Low’s mobile phone stopped moving.

Was it spooked by the fatal gunshot?

Elizabeth Campbell told police that she had not been anywhere near the area for years but later admitted in court that she had cycled there a number of times on her e-bike in late 2023/early 2024.

The day after the shooting, David Campbell took his wife’s bike to have new tyres put on, explaining that his wife was cycling with friends the following weekend through a forest.

Despite the shop owner telling him that the existing ones were not worn and perfectly capable of such an expedition, he had insisted.



Prosecutor Greg Farrell told the court, “The crown case is that he changed the tyres on the bike in order to hide any connection between that bike and the locus [location].

“It’s a muddy path, a good chance that that bike could have left track which could have been matched to those tyres.”

A soil analysis report by Professor Lorna Dawson showed that some traces of soil and vegetation recovered from the pedals did support the proposition that the bike, or its rider, had come into contact with Leafy Lane near Brian’s home in Pitilie.

The CCTV footage of the cyclist shows the man wearing a jacket with a hood.

Elizabeth said that her husband did not have that jacket because he never wore a hat or a hood.



After Greg Farrell showed her a picture of David wearing a woolly hat, she remarked,

“That is very, very unusual.”

A bizarre exchange followed when it was David Campbell’s turn in the dock.

At first he argued that it was not a hat but “a woolly top” before settling on a “beanie” but “not a hat.”

Several witnesses gave evidence of David Campbell’s threatening behaviour.



Leona Forrest, the wife of a groundsman, who both used to live on the estate, recalled when he had shouted in her face that her husband was useless.

Countown to murder Timeline of how killer carried out callous shotgun execution Feb 15

David Campbell fits doorbell camera to back door. Betty Campbell leaves to visit daughter in Dunfermline. Feb 16

7.11am – Campbell leaves home by the front door then walks to the rear where his car is parked. Travels in his blue Peugeot Partner to 22 Dunkeld Street. 7.33am – Leaves Dunkeld Street and returns home in his car. 7.35am – Filmed placing duct tape over doorbell camera on back door before returning inside via the front door. 10.09am – David Campbell manually switches off home CCTV system. 10.13am – Removes tape from doorbell and is heard talking about camera in phone call with daughter Sarah Aitchison. 10.19am – Campbell leaves home with pal Pat Spicer and travels to the bowling club before returning home around one hour later. 11:10am – Campbell places duct tape over the doorbell camera for a second time. 3.41pm – Campbell makes a 14 minute-long call to council planning department. 4:12pm – Hooded cyclist believed to be Campbell first observed on CCTV travelling north on Burnside, Aberfledy, close to Campbell’s home. 4:14pm – Cyclist seen passing Aberfeldy Business Park towards Spirit of Wood delivery track. 4:18pm – Cyclist goes out of view 140 yards before track leading to Leafy Lane. 4.52pm – Activity ceases on Brian Low’s mobile phone at Leafy Lane where his body is later found. 5.01pm – Cyclist reappears 140 metres after the junction for the delivery track. 5.04pm – Cyclist passes Aberfeldy Business Park. 6.41pm – After disappearing from CCTV for more than one and a half hours, cyclist appears at Mill Street close to David Campbell’s home. 7.32pm – First footage recorded on doorbell camera since tape placed over it as door is seen being opened from inside. 7.33pm – David Campbell filmed in boiler suit walking out back door and returning inside two minutes later. Feb 17

At around 9am – Brian Low’s body is found.

“I could feel his spit on my face,” she says.

“And he said was going to kill my husband.”

Former estate worker Richard Wright said that Campbell had once told him, “I’ll f***ing shoot you one of these days.”

Richard added, “He was always threatening somebody.”



Adrian Weber, who had worked on the estate after David Campbell had left, said that Brian had mentioned to him that David had threatened to kill him.

When asked how David Campbell and Brian Low got along, local farmer, Sally Crystal, commented, “At first it wasn’t noticeable, but as time went on, there was a coldness.

“On one occasion I had been talking to Brian in the morning and David walked past me and said, ‘I f***king loathe that man, I hate him.’

I was quite taken aback at that because I couldn’t understand why anybody would loathe Brian.

“He was what I consider a gentle man.”



David Campbell’s defending KC, Tony Lenehan, flipped all of this on its head.

In an interview with the documentary team he reasons, “The Crown led those charges to show that David Campbell was threatening.

“But ironically, those charges supported the conclusion that even if he had ill will towards somebody at some point, he didn’t do anything about it.”

The murder weapon was never recovered.

Police discovered shotgun cartridges in Campbell’s home, the same size as those used to kill Brian, but he was known to use a shotgun at work.



In the witness box David Campbell admitted that he and Brian Low didn’t get on – “He didn’t like me. I didn’t like him,” – but he denied ever threatening to shoot anybody.

The explanation about why he covered over his doorbell with duct tape confused everyone.

He said, “As far as I was aware, somebody stole the front door camera and I phoned my wife to tell her that I’ve taped up the back door camera.

“So, there’s only one camera working, and you’ll be able to see who has it and where it is.”

Greg Farrell remarked, “The whole chapter about the doorbell camera being taped up was quite difficult to understand.



“A common-sense explanation of why he did that was that he wanted to hide his movements.

“As for his explanation, I struggled to follow it.”

Battling the potential of missed forensic opportunities – the crime scene was not cordoned off until six days after the murder – the prosecution led a circumstantial case to build a picture of a decades-old feud between the victim and the accused that led to a pre-meditated murder.

They had put a good case but Brian’s family feared that the jury would accept there was reasonable doubt.

There followed three tense days of deliberation before they came to a verdict.



“That was the longest three days of my life,” says Pam.

“You try to be normal and chat to your friends and say that you’re okay, but you’re really not.

“You’re panicking inside.

“I’ve gone two years through hell waiting on this day to get Brian justice.

“Surely, it’s obvious that he’s guilty.



“I couldn’t go in for the verdict because I didn’t know how I would react.

“That verdict is not going to make it better, but it could make it a hell of a lot worse.”

David Campbell was found guilty.

He received a life sentence with a minimum of 19 years.

Judge Lord Scott, commented, “David Campbell, you’ve been found guilty of the murder of Brian Low.



“It may be that given serious errors in the early stages of police inquiries, you thought initially that you had literally got away with murder.

“If so, you were wrong.”

“You don’t feel happy because you think it’s lives ruined,” says Pam.

“It’s not just my life.

“He’s ruined his own family’s life.”



Like Pam, Brian’s older brother, Douglas, was in court every day.

“Brian meant so much to us,” he says.

“My elder brother John and myself thought we’d be the only two, then my mother became pregnant again.

“She wanted to have a girl but Brian came along.

“She got over the disappointment of him not being a girl, and he was a little bit spoilt.



“He had this cheeky little grin and he was just loved by everybody.

“I went from treating him as my sort of pesky little brother to actually enjoying his company.

“I remember when my father died of a stroke.

“As he was dying, I promised him I would look after Mum and Brian.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Obviously, I didn’t do a very good job of that.”



Murder Trial: Death of a Dog Walker, BBC2, Tuesday and Wednesday 11th August at 9pm.

News.title: Chilling footage shows serial sexual predator Simon Levy leading murder victim to her death and stalking women on street
News.content:
CHILLING footage shows serial sexual predator Simon Levy leading one of his murder victims to her death and stalking women on the street.

Catastrophic blunders in the system left the vile offender free to kill two sex workers after raping a third – while he was on bail for string of sexual assaults.



Levy, 40, embarked on a shocking rampage where he murdered two women, left another for dead and sexually assaulted ten young women on the London Underground weeks after being freed from prison in September 2024.

He was released after serving a three year sentence for molesting two women in public, and subject to a sexual offenders’ order in which he was meant to be watched closely by authorities.



Harrowing footage shows the monster in the streets and on the Tube where he prowled for victims, as well as the moment he led a woman to her death.

CCTV videos also show Levy getting off the bus at High Court road in Tottenham, north London, before he murdered his second victim Sheryl Wilkins on August 24 2025.





A body worn camera videos show the moment the vile attacker is arrested on suspicion of murder – and again for the second and final time five months later.

Levy was jailed in 2021 for sexual assaults, and carried on preying on woman after he was released in 2023.

In a separate trial, he was convicted of 11 counts of sexual assault in which ten of the victims were young women who were using the Tube, and the 11th was a prison officer, assaulted while he was behind bars in 2022.

In January 2025, Levy strangled a woman unconscious before raping her in a car park and leaving her “as good as dead”.

The surviving victim had told cops that she had been raped and knew where her attacker lived, but she was not formally interviewed until after he had killed twice.



In March 2025, he killed Carmenza Valencia Trujillo, 54, before dumping her body in the stairwell of a derelict building in Peckham, South East London – all while still on bail.

Levy – who had a “compulsive or pathological desire to assault women” – was one of seven arrested over her murder, but was released under investigation on April 1 – leaving him free to murder his third victim.

Sheryl Wilkins, 39, was found dead near a B&M store in Tottenham in late August of the same year, just two days after Levy failed to appear at court.



Chilling footage shows Levy and Wilkins walk through the car park where she was murdered.

Yesterday, the “predatory monster” was found guilty of two counts of rape, two of murder, one of GBH and one of intentional suffocation.

Police and prosecutors faced questions for failing to stop the half blind serial attacker in his tracks.

In a shocking “systematic failure”, the court heard Levy had been carrying out daily attacks for years, with dozens more potential victims out there as cops urge them to come forward.

The unemployed loner, who lived with his mum in Tottenham, was separately found guilty earlier this year of sexually assaulting ten women on London’s Tube network over a 19-month period.



Cops have urged more victims of Levy’s to come forward, as London’s victims’ commissioner said a “litany of failures” had allowed him to commit his heinous crimes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Independent Office of Police Conduct (IOPC) confirmed two officers are being investigated over their handling of Levy.

The Metropolitan Police, British Transport Police and Crown Prosecution Service have all admitted to failures in how the brute was monitored between his first conviction and his arrest for murder.

News.title: Meet the Brit dads who were hunted down & now pay for kids they abandoned overseas – as time’s up for rest to be exposed
News.content:
BABIES born to British ‘sex tourists’ and poverty-stricken women in the Philippines are being abandoned by their British fathers – but time is running out for them.

In an exclusive series – Looking for Dad: The Children of Britain’s Sex Tourists – we reveal how errant dads are being hunted down as a revolutionary organisation uses DNA to track them down and make them pay for their desperate children.



READ PART ONE OF OUR EXPLOSIVE NEW SERIES, LOOKING FOR DAD: THE CHILDREN OF BRITAIN’S SEX TOURISTS

READ PART TWO OF OUR EXPLOSIVE NEW SERIES, LOOKING FOR DAD: THE CHILDREN OF BRITAIN’S SEX TOURISTS



But of course, not every British dad fathered a child through a sex worker – or chose to walk away.

Journalist and charity worker Margaret Simons tells how some families made it work.



JUST before Christmas, identical twins Madeline and Melanie delos Santos met their father for the first time in 22 years.

The 25-year-olds had spent decades desperate for a relationship with their British dad, a retired civil engineer.

I head a charity that helped track down their father. But contact was sparse after our investigators tracked him down.

Then, out of the blue, he told them he was coming to Angeles and wanted to see them.



They arranged to meet at his hotel for breakfast. Madeline says she walked into the room, saw her father’s back and recognised him straight away, even though she hadn’t seen him since she was a toddler.

She says: “In that moment I realised I did need him, though I had told myself I didn’t. I realised that I am now complete. And all of the questions, all of my anger and hatred towards him, all of it vanished in a second. It was all gone.”

Why had their dad, who we will name Roy, chosen this moment to visit? The twins don’t know. Says Melanie: “Maybe because he’s old. Maybe he realised it is his responsibility to show up.”

Twenty-five years ago, Roy was working in the Philippines and met Esperanza delos Santos, or Espy as she is known to her family, in a bar on Fields Avenue. He fell for her.

When he was transferred to Bali, Espy moved with him. She returned home when she was seven months pregnant and gave birth to the twins. The family has a faded picture of the Christening, with Roy holding one of the babies.



But then, when the children were still toddlers, the relationship failed, and Roy left.

The family tell me that, to start with, he sent money each month. He provided them with a letter confirming the twins were his children and consenting to them using his family name.

Then, on his retirement, he made one last payment – 1.5 million pesos, (£21,000), with the instruction that it be used to buy a house for his girls.

Roy gave what he thought was fair. It is more than many fathers do. But what he gave is also almost certainly much less than he would have had to give, by law, had his daughters been born in Britain.

The girls were raised by their extended family, and in particular their grandmother, the family matriarch. They were able to attend a private school and gain a decent education, thanks to an uncle sending home remittances from his job as a waiter in Dubai.



But underlying the family say there was a hurt and abandonment.

When the twins were 11, their grandmother allegedly wrote to Roy asking for more money to pay school fees. She says he wrote back that he had no job and no income.

A letter seen by The Sun reads: “We cannot avoid a difficult decision to make about the twins. With both of us without money and still some years to go before they are independent, the only option I can think of is adoption. I hate to say [this] but what else can we do?”



I first met Melanie and Madeline in 2018, just after they turned eighteen. They were gorgeous – smart, thoughtful and kind. But lack of money meant they had to abandon their education and seek work.

All the girls wanted was to know their father. They weren’t after his money.

At the twins’ request, the charity I run tracked down Roy, who was living a middle-class life in the Home Counties, and rang him to tell him about his daughters’ request.

After a few days and some emails, he rang the girls, and they had a good conversation and agreed to keep in touch. But the contact proved sporadic. It was always the girls seeking him, tracking him. He never initiated contact – until last year.

After I wrote about the twins several years ago, Madeline was sponsored by an architect who read my article.



This good samaritan paid her university fees, and last year she graduated as an architect, and now works for an Angeles City architectural firm.

Melanie has a job as a marketing assistant for a motorcycle dealer.

And then their father came to visit. Roy spent three days in Angeles City, and the girls spent as much time with him as they could, sharing every meal.

He met their mother again. That was bittersweet. He did not recognise her.

For the girls, it was a revelation. They noticed mannerisms and habits of thought they had in common. They share his chin. Madeline recognised that “we share a certain way of thinking. A mindset.”



He gave them an explanation, of sorts, for why he had left them behind as tiny children. The girls have asked that the details be kept confidential for their mother’s sake.

Madeline said: “He has a point. I don’t agree with what he did, but I understand better.”

Nevertheless, she has a message for British fathers of Filipino children: “Have a sense of responsibility. Don’t hide your children, because it’s important for them to be proud of themselves and to know who they are.”

And to the many other children of British fathers, she says: “Don’t lose hope. You are worth something just by yourself. And one day you may find your father.”

Thankfully, not all British men who have children in the Philippines abandon them.



David, now 69, who has asked us not to use his surname, first came to the Philippines in 1981 when he was working for a resources trading company.

David did not pay for sex.

He married a Filipino he met while working in South Asia, but they broke up.

Over the years, he travelled back and forth to the Philippines, and when he was in his early 40s met 27 year old Jessica Gutierrez, a waitress at a backpacker restaurant, who became his girlfriend.



He stayed with her for over a year, ending up managing the restaurant in which she worked.

Then she told him she was carrying his child. Their relationship had ended, and she was assuming he would abandon them and go back to London.

David knew that was all too common a scenario, but he wanted to be different.

“I decided I wouldn’t go that route,” he said. “I was in my early 40s. I didn’t have a kid. My brother didn’t have kids.



“There was just something in me that said, ‘I want this. It is the right thing.’”

He asked for and obtained a DNA test to confirm the child was his, and committed to supporting him come what may.

His son William Gutierrez was born in 2000. By now, David was working in the UK, but visited about every eighteen months, and paid to support William.

His mother helped as well and brought birthday and Christmas gifts for the grandchild she had never met in person.

David says: “I didn’t know him very well when he was a young kid, which I think actually was an advantage because, put it this way, women are far better with young children than men are. That’s a biological fact. So I missed the toddler tantrums and the nappies and everything like that.”



But he paid for private schools and medical needs, sending money whenever it was needed – he estimates the cost of around £250 per month.

Then, in 2019, he got a job in Manila running a call centre and began to get to know his son. It was life-affirming.

William, now 25, recently graduated as an electrical engineer. He lives in Cebu, and the two men meet frequently.

David says: “I visit. We go to bars, we drink beer and watch football. We are great friends.”

Now retired, David divides his time between the Philippines and the UK, always trying to avoid the “horrible” British winter.



But the main reason he spends so much time here is his son. “He is a great man, feet on the ground,” David says. “The best thing I ever did. I am very proud of him.

“If it wasn’t for him, I would probably come every couple of years just to see friends for two or three weeks, and that would be it.”

What does he have to say to the many British men who abandon their children, or never stop to wonder if they have fathered one?

He is slow to judge and suspects many of them have wives and children at home.

“The last thing they want is to have to disrupt their family by admitting to this kind of thing,” David says.



“It’s fear of the entanglement, fear of the commitment, of the financial consequences, fear of just the responsibility of having a child.”

And why do so many British men seek sex with Filipinos?

THE LAW By Margaret Simons Supporting your children is not only a moral responsibility, but also a legal one in almost all countries of the world, including the Philippines and the United Kingdom.

Coming to a sensible and amicable agreement between mothers and fathers is usually in everyone’s best interests.

But as a last resort, we find lawyers to act for the children and their mothers and go to court.

The United Kingdom and the Philippines have a reciprocal enforcement maintenance order arrangement. This means the British authorities and courts will enforce a

legitimate child support application from a Philippines-based parent.

The legal obligation to support your children does not depend on whether the mother and father were married, or had a long-term relationship.

If the father is not acknowledged on the birth certificate, then its more complicated and a special application with additional evidence, such as a DNA test, will have to be made.

If the father won’t provide DNA evidence, then an application can be made to the courts to make a declaration of parentage on the basis of any other evidence provided, and taking into account the father’s refusal. The courts can also order a father to do a DNA test if they decide it is in the child’s best interests.

If the British authorities decide a father is due to pay child support, then they use a formula based on the income of both parents to decide the amount. Failure to pay child support can lead to money being deducted direct from wages or pensions, or bailiffs can be sent to collect on the debt.

If a child was born on or after 1 July 2006 to a Filipino mother and a British citizen, then they are automatically British citizens. They can apply to the British Government for a letter to confirm this, and then for a British passport – but would have to provide evidence of parentage. Again, the courts can be asked to order a DNA test.

He says: “In the Philippines, it’s very easy to find a girlfriend, to be honest. If you come for a month, it’s easy to find a girlfriend who will stay with you for a month, and then maybe see you when you come again the next year, and that’s the way it works.

“Sometimes it’s a permanent relationship. Sometimes, as one of my friends put it in a French phrase, it’s ‘wife du jour’ (meaning, wife of the day).”

And what would he say to other British men who father children in the Philippines?



“It’s very difficult,” he says. “It depends on your circumstances.”

It was easy for David, as a middle-aged man without a wife, to stand by his child. It is harder for others.

But, he acknowledges, most British men with children in the Philippines could send even “a little money each month, if they wanted to”.

“Too many of them don’t want to, and that is hardly right,” he adds.

Put simply, William makes him happy. William is in the process of changing his name from Gutierrez. He may soon apply for British citizenship too.



Meanwhile, before he left, Roy agreed that he would help his daughters make an application for British citizenship. Soon, they hope to see him again in Britain and to connect with their half-siblings.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And after years of anger, they don’t hesitate when asked if they love their father. Melanie says: “Yes, I love him. I am now complete.”

News.title: Exact date new heatwave to burn Brits in 36C and set new temperature record
News.content:
Exact date new heatwave to burn Brits in 36C and set new temperature record

Temperatures could soar to a staggering 36C as the extreme summer heat continues with a fifth heatwave about to start - the UKHSA has issued health alerts

View 2 Images Aerial view of runners passing through Clapham Common, in London, on Saturday (Image: Maja Smiejkowska/PA Wire)

The Met Office revealed which day Brits could see temperatures soar to 36C next week, as the fifth heatwave of the year approaches.

‌



Records were broken as for the first time ever, a temperature of 35C was recorded somewhere in the UK on the three consecutive months of May, June and July. This could be broken again in August with some forecast models suggesting that 36C could be recorded in central and south-east England this coming week.

‌



Yellow heat health alerts have been triggered from 9am on Saturday to 9pm on Tuesday and warn that the hot weather is could impact people's health and wellbeing.

‌



View 2 Images Map of yellow heat alerts for England from Saturday to Tuesday (Image: UK Health Security Agency)

The Met Office said temperatures will climb through the weekend as heatwave conditions return, with a high of 36C expected in parts of East Anglia and south-east England by Thursday.

The highest temperature recorded so far this year was 38C at Lingwood in Norfolk, on June 28. There have been 33 days so far in 2026 when temperatures have gone over 30C somewhere in the UK. Yet another worrying record could be broken next week, as 34 days was the record in 1995.

‌



Forecasters have predicted a north-south split in the weather at the weekend, with Scotland and Northern Ireland likely to see spells of heavy rain. England and Wales however will remain largely dry, sunny and increasingly warm. Temperatures could reach 30C on Saturday, before climbing into the low 30s in southern and south-east England on Sunday.

Highs of up to 30C are possible across parts of England and Wales on Tuesday, increasing to 32C to 34C on Wednesday, with the highest temperatures currently expected on Thursday.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued yellow heat health alerts for the East Midlands, West Midlands, South East, South West, East of England, Yorkshire and the Humber and London.

Article continues below

Two record-breaking heatwaves in May and June led to more than 2,800 excess deaths, and two more heatwaves in July have fuelled drought and wildfires.

Several wildfires have broken out across the UK over recent weeks, with large blazes at Dunwich Heath in Suffolk, Headon Warren on the Isle of Wight, Llanwonno in the Rhondda Valleys, South Wales, and the Cairngorms National Park in Scotland.

These blazes are likely to become exceptionally severe on Sunday for almost all of the east and south-east of England, according to the Fire Severity Index. "Exceptional" severity is its highest ranking.

News.title: Solar eclipse to hit this week - Met Office reveals best UK locations to see it
News.content:
Solar eclipse to hit this week - Met Office reveals best UK locations to see it

The Met Office has shared the parts of the UK that Brits will have the best chance to see the solar eclipse next week - an astronomer has shared an important warning for Wednesday night

View 2 Images The skies will darken in days to come as the eclipse takes place (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

The UK is set to experience it's fullest solar eclipse for the next 54 years on Wednesday - with the Met Office revealing the best places to see the cosmic phenomenon.

‌



Over 90% of the sun will be blocked by the moon between 6.17pm and 8.06pm on August 12, the most it has been covered above UK skies since the total eclipse in 1999. The next time the moon will cover this much of the sun will be all the way in 2081, so some Brits will want to make the most of Wednesday's solar eclipse.

‌



The Met Office shared a list of the best locations in the UK for the event.

‌



Perseid Meteor Shower 2026 to peak over UK after solar eclipse - complete guide READ MORE :

Met Office names 25 areas facing downpours on Sunday as weather maps turn blue READ MORE :

View 2 Images People could witness a similar sight to this eclipse in Vermont, in April 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

The places due to see the eclipse at its fullest are Devon, Cornwall and the westernmost parts of Pembrokeshire. From these locations, a range of 94% to 96% of the sun will be obscured by the moon.

Plymouth in particular is forecast to see the moon cover 94.66% of the sun at 7.16pm on Wednesday, according to the Met Office.

‌



Other locations will also see a huge portion of the sun covered, with the rest of Wales, Northern Ireland, parts of the West Midlands and the South West, and the westernmost parts of Scotland expected to see 92% to 94% solar coverage.

In Cardiff, the moon is forecast to obscure 93.24% of the sun at 7.13pm while in Belfast it will cover 93.09% of the sun at 7.08pm.

Skygazers in the rest of the country will not completely miss out as most people will see the moon obscure 90% to 92% of the sun.

‌



Birmingham is expected to seen 91.79% coverage at 7.12pm, 91.41% in London at 7.13pm, 90.74% in Inverness at 7.03pm, 90.71% in Edinburgh at 7.06pm and 90.22% in Newcastle at 7.07pm.

Skygazers really keen to catch a sight of the fullest possible solar eclipse should avoid the easternmost parts of the UK, where only 88% to 90% of coverage is expected. These area include the coasts of Norfolk, Yorkshire and Aberdeenshire, as well as the Orkney and Shetland Islands.

A warning has been put out to the public by the Royal Greenwich Observatory who said regular sunglasses are not a safe enough method to view the cosmic phenomenon. Imo Bell, a planetarium astronomer at the observatory, previously said: "It's not a total eclipse, but over 90% is really exciting. We’re not going to get one this good for a really long time.

Article continues below

"So, it's important not to miss it, and to be prepared. You can't just go out and expect to have a look because it's really dangerous for your eyes.

"So, you can use solar eclipse glasses, which are very, very different from sunglasses – they block out so much light that you can't see anything through them except the sun, because that’s how much light they need to block for the damaging light of the sun to be safe to view."

Bell said solar telescope are ideal but suggested people could also look at whether their local astronomy society is holding any events for the occasion. Bell also advised getting to a vantage point facing west, with minimal buildings around, as the best way to view the eclipse.

News.title: Lionel Messi's father, 68, dies as tragic news confirmed in club statement
News.content:
Lionel Messi's father, 68, dies as tragic news confirmed in club statement

Jorge Messi, a businessman and agent for his superstar footballer son, Lionel, had been ill for a significant period of time and passed away on Friday in his home city of Rosario, Argentina

View 2 Images Jorge Messi has died aged 68 (Image: X)

Lionel Messi's father has died at the age of 68 following a long battle with illness. Jorge Messi passed away in hospital on Friday in his home city of Rosario, Argentina.

‌



His family said during the World Cup in June that Jorge had been dealing with a 'health-related situation'. Lionel's former club, Newell's Old Boys, have now confirmed his passing.

‌



A statement published on Saturday read: "Club Atletico Newell's Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario. Recognised leproso fan, businessman, and father of the Argentine national team captain, Lionel Andres Messi.

‌



"Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini. His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Jorge Messi was his son's agent (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

‌



"Thank you for teaching him to love these colours. The Board of Directors, members, athletes, and the entire leprosa family embrace with affection Celia, Lionel, Rodrigo, Matias, and Maria Sol, and all their loved ones and close ones in this difficult moment."

Speculation about Jorge's health and wellbeing was rife throughout the World Cup, as Argentina reached the final before losing to Spain in extra-time. It was even falsely reported that he had died after his son was seen crying during Argentina's 3-0 win against Algeria in the group stage.

"Why was I crying? It had absolutely nothing to do with football," Lionel said post-match. "I have had a few difficult days."

‌



A subsequent statement read: "The Messi family wishes to inform you that Jorge Messi is currently dealing with health problems. He is currently under medical supervision and is recovering well.

"Given the reports, rumours and speculation that have been circulating in recent hours, the family wishes to express its deep concern about the lack of sensitivity, respect and discretion with which some people have treated a strictly private family matter."

Jorge played an instrumental role in his son's career, serving as his agent from the beginning. He travelled to Barcelona with a 13-year-old Lionel and the rest - such as eight Ballon d'Or awards, four Champions League wins and 13 domestic league titles - is history. He is survived by his wife, Celia Maria, sons Lionel, Rodrigo and Matias, and daughter Maria Sol.

Article continues below

Argentine club Rosario Central also paid tribute by posting on social media: "El Club Atletico Rosario Central deeply regrets the passing of Jorge Messi. We accompany with respect and affection Lionel, his family, and all his loved ones in this painful moment. May he rest in peace."

News.title: Double killer Christopher Halliwell 'is prime suspect and should be quizzed' over unsolved Julie Finley murder
News.content:
Double killer Christopher Halliwell should be quizzed by police over the unsolved murder of a young woman 32 years ago, an ex-detective who worked on the case has said.

Julie Finley, 23, was strangled and dumped naked in a carrot field near a lay-by ten miles outside Liverpool on August 6, 1994. She had screamed "help me, help me, for god's sake help me" to a witness who fled after her killer threatened him near the A570 in Rainford, Lancs.

A Mirror investigation revealed in 2019 that Halliwell was living in Aughton, five miles from the spot at the time of the murder. He was a window fitter and drove a D-reg white Transit van similar to the one spotted at the scene at the time Julie was killed.

Bombshell new evidence puts double killer Christopher Halliwell in frame for third murder READ MORE :

Evidence linking Christopher Halliwell to woman's murder lay untouched by cops for years READ MORE :

View 7 Images Julie was 23 when she as killed (Image: Crimestoppers / SWNS)

‌



We tracked down former Acting Detective Sergeant Ian Clarke who spent years working on the case for Merseyside Police. Speaking at the deposition scene last month, Mr Clarke told the Mirror that he thinks Halliwell should be treated as the prime suspect.

He said: "I think that's good evidence. We would have had no reason to look for somebody like Christopher Halliwell; he wouldn't have ever come into our investigation.

"I don't see why a visit to him in prison couldn't be made. He might make no comment, but you never know he might want to get it off his chest.

View 7 Images Christopher Halliwell was convicted of killing two women - but did he also murder Julie? (Image: SWNS.com)

‌



"I think he's got to be a strong suspect. I would do everything I could to find out the history of Halliwell because I can't believe that a man like him, having done one murder, having admitted another murder, is well capable of having committed this one on Julie Finley. No other suspects ever came in.

"The local people that we interviewed in no way could have been considered as suspects for this and we did interview them."

Julie, who had become a heroin addict in her late teens, was seen at around 10.30pm on Friday, August 5, 1994, near Royal Liverpool Hospital, talking to a white man, of average build, aged in his 20s or 30s.

View 7 Images A BBC Crimewatch reconstruction shows a white van at the spot where Julie's body was dumped

‌



Her body was found the next day. Two witnesses later reported that a man and woman had been seen arguing next to a white Transit van in the lay-by where Julie was dumped. The witness she shouted at was a hitchhiker in his mid-20s with short blond hair, believed to be from St Helens.

Mr Clarke revealed that his team traced the man who was believed to have been a mental health nurse. It is not known if Merseyside Police have gone back to him since Halliwell became a suspect.

Mr Clarke said of the double killer: "I think he's got to be well in the frame in the circumstances of him being in Aughton, which is five miles down the road, having a D-registration Ford Transit, that he's been convicted of murdering young ladies who are similar to Julie Finley.

View 7 Images An e-fit of the hitchhiker who was later traced

‌



"So it's a lot of coincidences to work on and I would think that had we known that at the time he would certainly have been interviewed."

Sending a message to Halliwell, Julie's mum Pat, 81, said: "Could you please let us know if you're the one that murdered Julie? I want to know, I want justice for her. I've waited long enough and it's not fair on the family. It's thirty-odd years now and she could be married and have got herself a good job."

View 7 Images Pat with a picture of Julie (Image: PP.)

Pat, from Liverpool, also urged the police to quiz the killer, saying: "Go down and speak to Halliwell. I want closure for Julie."

‌



Like Halliwell's known victims, Julie was in her early 20s when lured into a vehicle, killed and dumped in a rural spot. There was no sign of an overt sex attack and a solid object had been thrust in her neck.

Swindon taxi driver Halliwell, 62, is serving a whole life term for killing Becky Godden-Edwards, 20, and Sian O'Callaghan, 22. It comes after a Mirror investigation this year found fresh evidence linking Halliwell to the unsolved murder of Melanie Hall, 25, who vanished from a nightclub in Bath two years after Julie was murdered.

View 7 Images Police at the spot where Julie was found in 1994 (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Det Chief Insp Ben Lavender, of Avon and Somerset Police, said in January that one theory was that the killer had links to Dursley, five miles from where Melanie's body was found.

‌



We uncovered electoral roll records which show Halliwell's sister, Sarah, lived in the small Gloucestershire town. They also show the double killer's mother, Sofia, and stepfather John, lived in neighbouring Nailsworth.

Melanie's remains were discovered in October 2009 on the northbound M5 at junction 14, 28 miles north of where she vanished.

One of Halliwell's former friends told the Mirror they would use the Michaelwood service station, a mile up the road.

News.title: How Madonna’s favourite’s pint became UK’s best beer - tragic beginning to closely-guarded ingredient
News.content:
From miners to movie stars, monarchs to Madonna, Timothy Taylor's bitter is the pint that has taken the world by storm. From humble beginnings in a rented Keighley barn, it now sells more than 18 million pints a year, worth £81.8million, to stand as the best selling cask ale in Britain.

The endorsement that no marketing budget could ever buy came in May 2003, when Madonna sat down on Jonathan Ross's sofa and named Landlord the best real ale going. She had been introduced to it by her then husband Guy Ritchie at the Dog and Duck in Soho, and cheerfully admitted that half a pint was enough to finish her off.

The Queen of Pop was talking about Landlord, the bitter first brewed in 1952 to slake the thirst of Yorkshire miners and see off the mighty Barnsley Bitter. After her first intervention - she doubled down a couple of years later on Parkinson, calling Landlord "The Champagne of Ales" - the brewery's phone rang for months, and Landlord became the talk of every pub in the land.

View 7 Images Timothy Taylor Landlord beer - an old truck circa 1930 (Image: Supplied)

‌



Hugh Grant joined in at a London gallery opening owned by the Duke and Duchess of Kent's son-in-law, another Timothy Taylor and no relation. Asked for his view on the art, he said: "Art, what art? I'm only here for this marvellous beer!"

Royalty came calling too. The Prince of Wales toured Knowle Spring on 12th February 2001 and was photographed sampling a pint of Landlord. The brewery marked the day with a beer it named Royal Ale, and brought it back as Celebration Ale for the 150th anniversary in 2008.

It returned a third time in May 2023, brewed to the original recipe, when the man who had sipped Landlord in Keighley was crowned King Charles III.

Chief executive Andrew Carter said: "It is always flattering, although we're just as pleased whenever anyone chooses a pint of Landlord. Madonna's endorsement remains the most memorable because it was so unexpected, but every genuine recommendation means something to us."

‌



View 7 Images Timothy Taylor, pictured circa 1870. This week marked 200 years since he was born (Image: Supplied)

The man who started it all was a Keighley tailor called Timothy Taylor, and this week marked 200 years since he was born. He was born in Bingley on 6th August 1826, the eldest son of a family of tailors.

He entered the business in 1841 after leaving school and went on to work as a travelling salesman for the firm. In 1857 he married Charlotte Aked at Keighley Parish Church - a union that shaped everything that followed.

A year later, Charlotte's brother Charles died of typhoid, caught from drinking contaminated water. It was from that point, the brewery's own history records, that Timothy's interest in beer began.

‌



Andrew said the family cannot be certain what drove him, adding: "It is an important part of our history, but we cannot know exactly what was in Timothy's mind. Charles's death appears to have sparked his interest in brewing, possibly because beer offered a safer alternative to contaminated water, but we believe his primary passion was simply to create great beer."

View 7 Images Barry Eye Barrel making circa 1950 (Image: Supplied)

In 1858 he took a barn and stable in Cook Lane, Keighley, and turned the building into a brewery. Keighley was booming on the back of the Industrial Revolution, and beer was a commodity the town would always buy.

His first pubs came in 1859, among them The Volunteers in Keighley, and that little bar still pours his beer today. Several of the premises he went on to own were called hotels, a ploy used by Taylor's and other brewers to sidestep the licensing laws of the day.

‌



By 1863, Timothy wanted out of the town centre, so he moved half a mile up the hill to Knowle Spring. The draw was a pure supply of the soft water that brewers call liquor, and the brewery has never left the site since.

For its first 130 years its mainstay was mild, the low-strength ale that mill and foundry men drank to replace what heavy work sweated out of them. Timothy died in January 1898, aged 71, and left an estate worth £50,000, a considerable fortune for the time.

View 7 Images Timothy Taylor Landlord beer van circa 1977 (Image: Supplied)

His sons Robert and Percy took the firm on, and the family has held it ever since. Survival was never a certainty. In 1922 the brothers put the business up for sale, and Samuel Allsopp and Sons of Burton upon Trent tabled a bid of £112,000.

‌



The buyer then walked away, and Taylor's stayed in family hands almost by luck. The beer that made the name arrived almost by accident when, in 1952, Chairman Philip Taylor and his brewers created a strong pale ale.

It was launched the next year as Competition Ale, the competition being a contest to name it. A steward from the Keighley Drill Hall Club won a £500 prize for the winning suggestion, Landlord.

Philip's daughter Roberta, an art student, drew the jovial Landlord that still sits on the pump clip today. John Aked Taylor, later Lord Ingrow, took charge in 1954 and built the financial discipline that kept the brewery independent, while rivals were swallowed up around it.

View 7 Images King - then Prince - Charles at the Timothy Taylor Brewery in Yorkshire (Image: Tim Rooke/Shutterstock)

‌



Known to his staff as "The Boss", John refused to scrimp on the ingredients, whatever the cost. He said of the brewer's craft: "You can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear."

When keg beer swept the trade in the 1960s, John held the line and carried on brewing cask ale the way his forebears had. The brewery still uses whole hops and Golden Promise barley, a variety far more commonly sent to whisky distillers than to brewers.

That obsession filled a trophy cabinet. Landlord has won more awards than any other English ale. In 1999 and 2000 it became the first beer to hold the CAMRA Champion Beer of Britain and the Brewing Industry International titles at the same time.

It had already taken Beer of the Year at the Great British Beer Festival in 1982 and again in 1983. In November 2024, it was named the top-selling cask ale in the country by value, and a year later it took the volume crown too, finally displacing Sharp's Doom Bar.

‌



View 7 Images The Queen of Pop, Madonna, is a fan of Timothy Taylor bitter (Image: GETTY)

Sales rose 3.6 per cent last year, at a time when real ale is falling sharply elsewhere. Through all of it, the beer has stayed stubbornly the same, and the man responsible knows exactly how unusual that is.

Andy Leman became head brewer in 2015, after 28 years at Knowle Spring, learning the job from his predecessor Peter Eells. He is only the sixth head brewer the company has had since 1858.

The single most closely guarded thing in the building is not a recipe ,but a living culture. Andy said: "The yeast is the same culture we've been using for 40 years which we harvest each week." Andrew said: "We look after it extremely carefully and, yes, we maintain protected backup cultures."

‌



The birthday itself was marked in the way the founder would have understood best. Andrew said: "We're marking the occasion by giving away 200 pints of Landlord across our Keighley pubs, Taylor's on the Green and the Boltmakers Arms."

The Boltmakers Arms sits a short walk from the streets where Timothy once cut cloth for a living. Two hundred years after his birth, the tailor's descendants still sit on the board of the company he founded.

Andrew said: "Timothy would still recognise the Knowle Spring, our spring water and the same uncompromising commitment to quality. He would also be proud that we remain independent and family-owned, with fifth-generation Taylor family members still on our Board. The investment in the brewery, scale and nationwide reach might take him aback slightly though."

News.title: Rugby star, 26, dies from suspected heatstroke after training session
News.content:
Rugby star, 26, dies from suspected heatstroke after training session

Japanese rugby club Kyuden Voltex have confirmed the tragic death of forward Saimoni Vuilagi at the age of just 26

View Image A rugby player in Japan has died (Image: Tony Marshall)

Japanese rugby club Kyuden Voltex said they were “devastated” following the death of Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi from suspected heatstroke.

‌



Kyuden Voltex, who play in the Japanese league’s second tier, announced Vunilagi, 26, died on Friday morning, having been taken to hospital on Monday after a training session.

‌



A club statement read: “After team practice on Monday, August 3, 2026, Saimoni displayed symptoms consistent with severe heatstroke.

‌



“He was transported to a medical facility for treatment, but despite the best efforts of the medical team, he sadly passed away.

Lewis Moody health latest as star arrives at Wimbledon after MND diagnosis READ MORE :

“The players, staff, and all team associates are devastated by this sudden news.

‌



“Although Saimoni had only recently joined Kyushu KV, his generous spirit and powerful style of play had raised high hopes for his contributions in the upcoming season.

“We humbly pray for the repose of his soul and extend our heartfelt condolences to his bereaved family.”

Vunilagi attended university in Japan and joined Kyuden Voltex last month from Japan Rugby League One side Tokyo Sungoliath.

Article continues below

"We express our heartfelt condolences upon receiving the news of the passing of Saimoni. We offer our deepest condolences to the bereaved family and all those involved," a statement from Japan Rugby League One read.

News.title: Met Office names 25 areas facing downpours on Sunday as weather maps turn blue
News.content:
Met Office names 25 areas facing downpours on Sunday as weather maps turn blue

A giant belt of rain is forecast to move across the UK on Sunday with more downpours to come next week

View 3 Images The rain will move across the UK on Sunday (Image: Getty Images)

Weather maps have turned blue across parts of the country on Sunday as the UK braces for a battering of rain next week.

‌



The Met Office has identified 25 areas will see showers tomorrow (August 9) while at least four will see heavy downpours as the hot summer spell gives way to rain.

‌



Forecasters predict a belt of rain will sweep across Scotland and Northern Ireland, which are expected to bear the brunt of the heavier downpours. Maps turn yellow in some areas, indicating higher rainfall rates per hour. These include Fort William, Stranraer and Aberdeen in Scotland, as well as Belfast in Northern Ireland.

‌



View 3 Images Weather maps show rain will hit mostly Scotland and Northern Ireland on Sunday

Rain is forecast to spread across both countries later tonight and into the early hours, with showers expected from midnight through to around 10am.

Northern England will then see patches of rain moving in from Sunday morning, hitting Kendal and Newcastle first before spreading into Lancashire, Greater Manchester.

‌



Meanwhile, Caernarfon in Wales can brace for rain later in the night from around 10pm.

Showers arrive ahead of further unsettled weather on Monday, when the Met Office forecasts more rain across as many as 12 areas of the UK.

View 3 Images Some patches turn yellow - where there is heavier downpours of rain

‌



Met Office meteorologist Honor Criswick said: "As we head into Monday, northerly winds will drag some cloud southwards, bringing rain across the far north of Scotland.

"We could also see a little bit of rain around the east coast of England, but the best of the brightness is likely going to be across southern parts of Wales and southern England. This is where we'll see the highest temperatures as well, reaching around 25C to 26C."
