Sports.title: Lionel Messi’s dad Jorge dies aged 68 after battle with illness that reduced Argentina star to tears at World Cup
Sports.content:
LIONEL MESSI’S father Jorge has died aged 68 after a long illness.

Jorge passed away at around 10pm yesterday at a clinic in Rosario, where he had been receiving medical treatment.



The news will come as a devastating blow to Messi, who has always maintained a close relationship with his father and agent.

Jorge played a huge role in his unprecedented football career, guiding him from his childhood days at Newell’s Old Boys to becoming the greatest player in history.



Newell’s Old Boys said in a statement: “Club Atlético Newell’s Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario.

“Recognized leproso fan, businessman, and father of the Argentine national team captain, Lionel Andrés Messi.



“Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.

“His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“Thank you for teaching him to love these colours.



“The Board of Directors, members, athletes, and the entire leprosa family embrace with affection Celia, Lionel, Rodrigo, Matías, and María Sol, and all their loved ones and close ones in this difficult moment.

“Farewell forever, leproso ❤️🖤”

Jorge was the driving force behind getting Lionel the growth hormone treatment he needed as a youngster after the family struggled to secure the necessary support in Argentina.

When Barcelona offered Messi the chance to move to Spain as a 13-year-old, Jorge stayed with his son as he began his remarkable journey at the Catalan giants.

The pair endured difficult early days as Lionel adjusted to life away from his family and fought to establish himself at one of the world’s biggest clubs.



Messi once recalled the sacrifices they made together, saying: “My dad was always by my side. We went through a lot of bad things.”

“My dad asked me what I wanted to do, did I want to keep going or should we go back? I wanted to keep going and he stayed with me.”

Jorge remained at his son’s side as Messi’s career exploded, eventually taking responsibility for his commercial negotiations and becoming a key figure behind the global Messi brand.

The relationship between father and son was not simply professional, with Jorge remaining a central figure in the Messi family – regularly accompanying Lionel during major moments in his career.

He also had football ambitions of his own, having played as a midfielder in the Newell’s youth system before being called up for military service.



Jorge later worked at the Acindar factory, rising to become a manager before his son’s extraordinary rise transformed the family’s life.

The 2026 World Cup provided a recent glimpse into the difficult period surrounding the Messi family.

After scoring in Argentina’s opening match against Algeria, Messi was visibly emotional and later explained that his tears were linked to matters away from football.

He said: “It’s for a reason completely unrelated to sports; I’ve had some difficult, complicated days. I’m grateful to the entire team, as always, for being by my side.”

Asked about his family, Messi later added: “The truth is, it’s mostly for my family. Because, well, they’re always there, always supporting me. We’re going through a difficult time right now.”



The Messi family subsequently said Jorge was “under medical supervision, recovering and progressing favorably within the context of his condition.”

Jorge’s influence stretched far beyond helping Lionel become a professional footballer, with the pair remaining closely connected throughout his son’s trophy-filled career.

Messi is the most decorated footballer of all-time, with 47 team trophies to his name – not to mention his individual honours including EIGHT Ballon d’Or‘s.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

From those uncertain days at Newell’s, to his second home in Barcelona, to the glitz and glamour of Paris and later Miami – all while representing Argentina on the biggest stage throughout, Jorge was one of the constants in Messi’s life.

Football will now mourn the loss of a man who played a crucial role in helping one of the sport’s greatest talents reach the top.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero OPEN to controversial Arsenal transfer and become first Tottenham ace to join fierce rivals in 25 years
Sports.content:
CRISTIAN ROMERO wants to sign for Arsenal – but Tottenham have NO intention of selling to their bitter rivals.

World Cup finalist Romero, 28, is set to leave Spurs this summer after five seasons in N17.



Arch enemies Arsenal are understood to be interested in the Argentine, along with Atletico Madrid and Inter Milan.

But a deal with the Gunners will be totally unpalatable for Spurs.



A move across North London would be a truly eyebrow-raising transfer and have the hallmarks of Sol Campbell leaving Spurs for Arsenal in 2001.

The difference with that switch though was that Campbell was a free agent, meaning Spurs could not prevent the centre-back from crossing into enemy territory.



Former England star Campbell was the last player to move directly from Spurs to Arsenal – and he was labelled a “Judas” by fans at White Hart Lane for the move.

Nobody has made the switch at all since 2010, when William Gallas controversially went in the opposite direction at the end of his Gunners contract.

Romero still has another three years left on his contract meaning Tottenham hold the cards over his future.

SunSport has been told by a high-level source at Spurs that they would not entertain the prospect of selling a player to the Gunners.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

It appears to rule out what would be the most contentious move of the summer.

But Romero is still expected to leave Spurs before the end of the transfer window.

Boss Roberto De Zerbi has already signed Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton for £52million as his replacement.

Atletico have a long-standing interest, with head coach Diego Simeone a huge fan of his compatriot, and seem a much more likely destination.



The Spanish giants tried to sign Romero last summer before then boss Thomas Frank convinced the defender to sign a bumper new contract and made him skipper.

Atletico are believed to be readying a fresh bid for £40million-rated Romero, financed by sales of a number of three other players.

Sports.title: Former England star puts £3.3million Cheshire mansion with golf simulator, home cinema, gym and steam room up for sale
Sports.content:
EVERTON ace Michael Keane has put in a transfer request at home by putting his £3.3million Cheshire mansion up for sale – complete with a golf simulator.

The Toffees’ defender’s luxury six-bed pad boasts a stunning split-level cinema with raised seating, gym, steam room and games room.



There’s also a huge entertaining room and party terraces, children’s play area and an astroturf pitch for a kick about, of course.

Other features include a grand galleried entrance hall, five reception rooms, an open-plan kitchen and decorative fireplace.



Keane, 33, bought the 6,500 sq.ft pad from Everton legend Phil Jagielka in 2021 for £2.9million but now wants to sell it, and has slashed £200,000 off the original asking price.



Planners gave him the go-ahead for a gym extension in 2020 despite objections from his next door neighbour but building work never started.

The pad is described by estate agents as an “immaculate, beautifully presented contemporary house in one of the area’s most sought after roads”.

They add: “The master suite is incredibly impressive, beautifully remodelled with a large bedroom area, built-in TV recess, French doors and dummy balcony to the front and several walk-in fully fitted dressing room areas for him and her.

“To the rear of the house is a huge, entertaining sun terrace which flows around the whole of the outside space and is lit at night.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“There’s a formal astroturf section of the garden beyond which a larger lawn with children’s play area and an outdoor recreation building currently housing the golf simulator.”

Other footballers who live nearby include team-mate Jordan Pickford, former Manchester City star John Stones, and Manchester United goalkeeper Tom Heaton.

It was at United where Keane started his career, starring as part of their iconic 2011 FA Youth Cup winning team alongside the likes of Paul Pogba, Jesse Lingard and Ravel Morrison.

Loan spells at Leicester, Derby, Blackburn and Burnley followed before the Clarets snapped him up permanently in 2015 when it became clear that he would struggle for first-team football at United.



An impressive two-year spell at Turf Moor led to Everton signing him in 2017, where he has been a good servant to the club – making 265 appearances.

Keane signed a new one-year contract at Everton in April, keeping him at the club until next summer.

Sports.title: Huddersfield Giants to leave home for Dewsbury amid major investment
Sports.content:
Betfred Super League side Huddersfield Giants have announced they are to leave the town and move to Dewsbury for the 2027 season onwards.

The Giants' intention is to move into Dewsbury's Flair Stadium, subject to RFL board approval, investing a projected £10m-plus in developing the ground.

The investment will deliver a transformational upgrade of the venue, including the construction of a new stand that will increase capacity from 5,000 to around 8,000 spectators, creating a viewing area on all four sides of the pitch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants director of rugby Andy Kelly reflects on what he's described as the 'most challenging' period of time in charge of the club

The redevelopment will also feature refurbishment of the fan concourses, significant upgrades to existing and new hospitality suites, new bars and food areas, both male and female player dressing rooms, and press facilities elevating the stadium to Super League standards.

An agreement has been reached following extensive and amicable negotiations with Betfred Championship team, Dewsbury Rams, and a strong partnership between the two clubs has been forged. The Flair will continue to host the Rams in the newly-upgraded and dual-branded facility.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Huddersfield Giants prop Tom Burgess joins Jenna, Jon and Sam Tomkins on The Bench

This comes following a period of uncertainty for the Giants after seeking a permanent location in the Huddersfield area.

Owner of the club, Ken Davy OBE, has explored several alternative sites, including The Shay Stadium in Halifax.

Speaking of the decision, Davy said: "It's no secret that as a club, we have fought to find a home in Huddersfield. We had to move from Fartown, from Leeds Road, and now from the Accu Stadium. But the Huddersfield Giants will not retreat. We will not compromise or quietly shuffle into the shadows.

"While we remain the Huddersfield Giants, I am proud to announce that our stage for the 2027 season and beyond is Dewsbury.

"The Flair Stadium is the perfect location for us, it will have the right capacity and facilities for the Giants and its fans to thrive while we continue the search for our permanent home. Our one giant future starts now.

"My overriding aim is to create a purpose-built stadium within Huddersfield for the Giants to call home. My commitment on that has not wavered. However, that was not feasible for the 2027 season."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Huddersfield Giants against Hull FC from the Super League

Ralph Rimmer OBE, executive chairman of the Huddersfield Giants, added: "The Giants' future is bright, and we are excited to lead the club into this new era.

"For fans, the matchday experience will be our focus. A smaller, more intimate ground means the crowd is closer to the action, letting the atmosphere grow and support the team out on the pitch.

"The Flair Stadium offers everything that supporters need from parking and accessibility to corporate hospitality and function rooms.

"We can't wait to welcome you for the 2027 season and beyond to be a part of the Giant future we have in store."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Nicholls pays tribute as Big Buck's dies aged 23
Sports.content:
Big Buck’s, one of the greatest staying hurdlers of all time, has died at the age of 23.

Owned by the late Andy Stewart, he was part of a golden age for trainer Paul Nicholls as he counted Kauto Star, Denman, Master Minded and Neptune Collonges among his stablemates.

Big Buck's had always been viewed by connections as a potential top-class chaser, however, a fall at the final fence in the 2008 Hennessy Gold Cup saw him revert back to hurdles and he never looked back.

He won what is now the Stayers' Hurdle a record four times, the Liverpool Hurdle four times and three times he came home in front in the Long Walk Hurdle.

Big Buck's, who struck up a great relationship with Ruby Walsh, was a fan favourite as he would often hit a flat spot in his races before powering to victory.

Nicholls told the Press Association: "Ability-wise he was probably as good as anything I've ever trained, it's just a shame he couldn't jump a chase fence.

"He was a wonderful horse for a wonderful owner who deserved to own a great horse like that. Andy enjoyed the whole journey and shared it with everybody.

"The horse had a brilliant life and had a great time with us and then a great time with Mike and Lucy Felton in retirement, but sadly time caught up with him.

"I was very lucky to have him at the same time as Kauto Star, Neptune Collonges, Master Minded and Denman. He was definitely as good as any of them."

Image: Big Buck's and Ruby Walsh formed a formidable partnership

One of the last surviving members of that halcyon period for the Ditcheat handler, Big Buck's would go on to pass Sir Ken and win a then record 18 straight National Hunt races when reverting to hurdles, an achievement only eclipsed by Altior since.

However, for Nicholls there will always be the question of how high he could have climbed if remaining over the larger obstacles.

"He won the Graded race at Aintree over fences, jumped 18 fences and jumped them 18 different ways and still won," said Nicholls.

"It made me think he was a certainty in the Hennessy and he was unlucky that day, but he just wasn't a natural jumper of a fence.

"If Kauto Star hadn't been about at that time then we probably would persevered over fences and he had the ability to win a Gold Cup. If he had won the Hennessy that day it would have definitely given us a headache and it would have been interesting where he would have ended up.

"But over hurdles he was invincible. Andy said I was bonkers, but going back over hurdles was the best thing we ever did. History tells you how good he was and Cheltenham, Aintree, Newbury, Ascot - if there was a big staying hurdle race, he won them all - all those Grade Ones on the trot, what a horse."

Big Bucks would become a standing dish on Thursdays at the Cheltenham Festival, with his famous flat spot often sparking nervous gasps from supporters before hitting top gear and surging up the Cheltenham hill under Walsh.

When asked to nominate just one race in Big Bucks' decorated career littered with so many great triumphs it was his fourth-straight success in the day three feature, when seeing off arguably the deepest field he met, edging out Irish raider Voler La Vedette, that Nicholls remembers most fondly.

"His fourth World Hurdle was the one that sticks out as being very special," said Nicholls.

"But we had so many great days with such a brilliant horse and we were all very lucky to be associated with him."

Sports.title: Rockets clinch qualification for women's knockouts in The Hundred
Sports.content:
Trent Rockets booked a place in the knockouts of The Hundred women's competition with a thumping nine-wicket win over already-eliminated MI London.

Nat Sciver-Brunt (67no off 36 balls) and Beth Mooney (54no off 44) struck sublime half-centuries as Rockets eased to their 122-run target with 18 balls to spare to claim a fifth-straight win.

Earlier, Australian left-arm spinner Sam Bates claimed 3-13 to move joint-top of the wicket-taking charts as MI London struggled to 121-5.

The Rockets then strolled to their target, despite Sophia Dunkley being dismissed for a three-ball duck. Sciver-Brunt and Mooney's subsequent 118-run stand is the second-highest partnership in the history of the women's competition.

MI London had made a steady enough start after being asked to bat, reaching 28-0, but the innings fell away after Bates took the key wicket of Hayley Matthews (10), trapped lbw.

Hollie Armitage (4) fell cheaply to Charley Phillips, before Bates struck twice off consecutive deliveries - dismissing Kira Chathli (31 from 27) lbw before Nicola Carey fell to a smart stumping by Mooney - as the hosts slumped to 49-4, with only an MI London review denying her the wicket of Alice Monaghan and a hat-trick.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Trent Rockets' Sam Bates was denied a hat-trick after MI London's Alice Monaghan reviewed the umpire's original decision of out lbw on Bates' hat-trick ball which proved to be agonisingly missing the wickets

Monaghan (27no off 21) and Melie Kerr (17 off 14) rebuilt, before Chinelle Henry (27no off 21) struck a flurry of boundaries late on, but their total looked well below-bar on a good deck against a rampant Rockets outfit. And so it proved.

What is happening in The Hundred on Sunday?

It's another four-match day, with two games apiece at Headingley and Lord's.

SunRisers Leeds first host Welsh Fire (women's game 11am, men's 2.30pm), the two teams jostling for position in the latter stages of both the women's and men's tournaments.

London Spirit then take on Birmingham Phoenix (women's game 2.30pm, men's 6pm), both battling for pride as they've already been eliminated from the women's and men's competitions.

Sports.title: 'I'm your warrior' - Guimaraes moves to Arsenal from Newcastle for £75m
Sports.content:
Arsenal have signed midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in a £75m transfer.

The 28-year-old has put pen to paper on a four-year deal with a further one-year option.

On the move to Arsenal, Guimaraes, who will wear the no. 39 shirt with the Gunners, said: "I feel amazing. I'm glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to [Andrea] Berta and Mikel [Arteta], I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

"I'm so excited to join you. I will give you my best, I promise. I'm your warrior, I'll never give up. Hopefully we can create many, many good memories together."

Newcastle had been keen to ensure the Brazil international, who had two years left on his contract plus a club-held option for a third, stayed at St James' Park, but his departure means they have now sold more than £240m worth of talent this summer.

Anthony Gordon joined Barcelona in a £69.3m deal and Spurs signed Sandro Tonali for £100m, while head coach Eddie Howe also left in what has been a turbulent few months at the club.

A Newcastle statement said: "The agreed fee represents one of the top-10 highest transfer fees ever received for a player aged 28 or over, and a record fee for a player of his age and position combined."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News takes a closer look at how Guimaraes stacks up against Arsenal's current midfield

Guimaraes told Newcastle bosses earlier this summer that he wanted to join Arsenal if a suitable offer arrived. Their opening bid was rejected before the deal was agreed.

He joined the Magpies in 2022 from Lyon for £40m and made 195 appearances for the club, scoring 31 goals and winning the Carabao Cup.

'One of the toughest decisions of my life'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Guimaraes' best Premier League goals for Newcastle

On his Newcastle departure, Guimaraes said: "This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together.

"I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my team-mates, Eddie (Howe) and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

"I thank PIF, our chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club. I also want to say thank you to David (Hopkinson) and Ross (Wilson) for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.

"This move is very tough because Newcastle means so much to me, but I wanted to experience something new in my life. I feel ready for a new challenge for myself and my family. I had a very positive conversation with Matthias Jaissle, and I leave knowing the club is in very good hands.

"To the supporters, thank you will never be enough, but I say it with all my heart. I will always be proud to have been part of this club's journey. Thank you for everything."

'A statement signing for Arsenal'

Sky Sports' Oliver Yew:

Guimaraes is one of the best midfielders in the Premier League, if not the world, and from a position of strength, Arsenal have taken him from Newcastle.

Midfield is already an area of the pitch where Arsenal are strong but Guimaraes' arrival is certainly an upgrade on Christian Norgaard, who has joined Everton. Myles Lewis-Skelly was playing incredibly well at the end of last season and started the Champions League final. Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino are World Cup winners and after some rest will be ready to go. There is Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze for the No 10 position alongside the two potential starters in Declan Rice and Guimaraes.

I'm so excited to join you. I will give you my best, I promise. I'm your warrior, I'll never give up. Hopefully we can create many, many good memories together.

The Brazilian gives Arteta even more options and it also allows for the possibility for Rice to get a breather in certain games after his exploits last season.

It is a world-class midfield and if Arsenal were not favourites for the title already, they are now.

Question marks were being raised over the fee Newcastle wanted for a player who will be 29 in November but the deal has been done nowhere near the reported £100m fee that was wanted. At the start of the transfer window, you would have probably said this is a fair fee, but with the last few weeks we have had in the window, with big money spent on midfielders Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers, anything under £100m looks good value.

Guimaraes is a little older but this is Arsenal's strategy, they want to win now. They have signed some younger players but last summer's deal to sign Viktor Gyokeres was to win now. He will not need any time to settle in. He is one of the most consistent Premier League midfielders.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd thinks Guimaraes is an upgrade for Arsenal's midfield and will play alongside or fill in for Declan Rice

Arsenal will not necessarily make money on him in the future but his arrival should get them closer to winning a first Champions League and he may help them retain the Premier League title.

If they can add a left winger and some star quality in that position, which looks like the last piece of the puzzle, it could be bad news for their title rivals.

'Newcastle were desperate to keep Guimaraes'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Keith Downie explains the three reasons why Newcastle have allowed Guimaraes to leave the club for Premier League champions Arsenal

Sky Sports News reporter Keith Downie:

Newcastle were desperate to keep Guimaraes and if he had said he wanted to stay, Newcastle would have refused any offer from Arsenal or any other club.

Attempts to persuade Guimaraes otherwise were made and positive conversations were held, but he was insistent he wanted to leave because he felt this was his last big opportunity to win titles.

The deal could only go ahead if two things happened: Guimaraes said he wanted to leave (which he has respectfully) and Newcastle sold on their terms, similar to Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.

Newcastle insisted it was their valuation or no deal. They would only sell Guimaraes at a fee that would become one of the highest paid for a player aged 28 or over.

In addition, a deal would only be sanctioned if the situation was handled properly - for example, Guimaraes attending Newcastle's training camp in Spain, which he reported to on Monday.

Newcastle feel Guimaraes has complied with their demands immaculately. They did not want a repeat of the Alexander Isak situation, where he refused to train before joining Liverpool last summer.

Agents were in between the clubs from the outset but Newcastle refused all pushes, which had began with mentions of a deal worth £40-£45m in June.

Newcastle were left frustrated because they felt Arsenal elongated the transfer by refusing to contact them for weeks.

Newcastle insist there have been no fall outs and good relations remain between player and club.

Sports.title: 'I'd rather fight Aaron for world title' - Walsh dismisses Stevie McKenna call-out
Sports.content:
Callum Walsh would entertain a fight against Aaron McKenna over Stephen McKenna, insisting all-Irish clashes only make sense with the world title on the line.

Walsh (16-0, 11 KOs) fights former European champion Tyler Denny on the undercard of Aaron McKenna's IBF world middleweight title showdown with Etinosa Oliha at Dublin's 3Arena this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

It's the headline act of six middleweight bouts on a stacked card that also sees Stephen McKenna face Owen O'Neill over eight rounds before assuming corner duties for his younger, world title-chasing brother.

Walsh has been identified as a potential future opponent by Stephen McKenna (16-1, 15 KOs), but the unbeaten 25-year-old believes he's already at another level.

Responding to McKenna's challenge, Walsh told Sky Sports: "If there's anyone that I'm looking at, it would be the fella with the world title, not the fella with the loss.

"In my mind, it doesn't make sense unless it's for a world title. There are bigger names than Stevie McKenna calling me out.

"Shane Mosley Jr is a bigger fight than Stevie McKenna. His brother Aaron is fighting for the world title. If I was going to fight either of them, I'd fight Aaron for the world title."

Image: Walsh on the scales ahead of his middleweight fight against Denny (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa Boxing)

'It makes sense for him, not for me'

Walsh believes an all-Irish fight without a world title on the line could needlessly jeopardise the momentum middleweights are currently generating in Ireland.

"It's a big time for Irish boxing," he added. "As an Irish fighter from such a small place, there are three of us now in Zuffa Boxing. Why would we want to eliminate each other unless it's for a world title?

"If it's for a world title, at least you can get paid for it. You're going to be able to sell out an arena and put on a big show for everyone involved. Why have an all-Irish fight on an undercard somewhere when it doesn't make sense?

"It makes sense for him. It makes no sense at all for me. His brother's fighting for the world title. There are bigger names calling me out. I've had bigger fights. It doesn't make any sense."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stevie McKenna is determined to have an all-Ireland clash against Walsh should both of them emerge victorious at Zuffa Boxing 10 this weekend

Walsh believes Stephen McKenna would be better served avenging his sole loss as a professional, a majority-decision defeat to Lee Cutler in 2024.

"He doesn't even want to fight the fella who beat him," he said. "He was asked if he wanted a rematch and he said no.

"Go back and fight the fella who beat you. That's the one I'd be looking at if I was him. He's in the same division, the same league, and he's begging for the rematch."

'I'll fight Aaron or the other fella'

Walsh, who fights in Dublin for the first time since knocking out Przemyslaw Runowski in two rounds in 2024, is confident he can overcome Denny and believes Aaron McKenna will become Ireland's newest world champion.

Victory for both men would set up the mouth-watering prospect of an all-Irish world title fight, and Walsh insists he would have no problem facing Aaron should he emerge as champion.

"I don't know much about his opponent, to be honest," Walsh added. "I'm sure Aaron will win. I presume he will.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Walsh insists he's not complacent ahead of Saturday's fight with Denny, while the former European champion is confident he can cause the upset in Dublin

Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged ‘lover’
Sports.content:
Uefa has confirmed a “departure payment” was made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Gianni Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary, allegations Fifa has dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum following the alleged relationship with Infantino. In a statement, Uefa confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, which it said was “in line” with regulations at the time.

However, Fifa has responded to the reports. “Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory,” a Fifa spokesman told the Telegraph. “No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.”

The report comes as pressure mounts on Infantino following his plan to seek private investment in a company which would run Fifa’s competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups. Infantino worked at Uefa for 16 years and was its general secretary from 2009 before being elected as Fifa president in February 2016.

A Uefa spokesperson said: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for a MBA course at a local business school.”

The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time. “Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all Uefa employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

Infantino has found himself at the centre of a storm for two weeks following his controversial plan to sell stakes to private investors in a company to run the World Cup. The plan was rejected by Uefa and two other continental confederations. On Wednesday, Infantino was backed by Fifa’s management board following a meeting in Morocco and issued an apology over the process.

Uefa’s threat for its 55 member countries to boycott Fifa competitions until the plan was scrapped remains, with the European confederation saying on Thursday that Wednesday’s announcement “changes nothing”.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimarães completes £75m Arsenal move: ‘I needed a new challenge’
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimarães says he “needed a new challenge in my life” after joining Arsenal from Newcastle for £75m and has targeted winning trophies. Guimarães is understood to have signed a four-year contract that contains a further one-year option after Newcastle reluctantly agreed to sell their captain.

The 29-year-old, who captained Newcastle to their first trophy since 1955 when they won the Carabao Cup last year, had made it clear that he wanted to join the Premier League champions after meeting the club’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, this week.

Arsenal have previously shown an interest in signing Guimarães on two occasions – in 2020 when he was playing for Athletico Paranaense in Brazil and then 18 months later when he was at Lyon and went on to move to the north-east. But the Brazil midfielder said he wanted to join Arsenal after his first meeting with Mikel Arerta and the sporting director, Andrea Berta.

“I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life,” he told Arsenal’s website. “After playing two World Cups, I’m at the point of my life, I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I’m in the right place to do it.

“I’m so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I’m hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

The arrival of Guimarães significantly boosts the midfield options available to Arteta, who now has a formidable squad that contains Declan Rice, Martin Ødegaard, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

“We are further strengthening the heart of our team,” said Berta. “As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity and has provided goals and assists for his team every year. Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.”

Guimarães revealed he has already received a message from Rice welcoming him to Arsenal that said “come here and please no more fights, now we’re friends”. “I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, is one of the best in Europe,” said Guimarães. “Everyone is an amazing player. I’m so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well,”

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães said leaving Tyneside was ‘one of the toughest decisions of my life’. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

Guimarães also released a statement to Newcastle. He said: “I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my teammates, Eddie [Howe] and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

“This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together. I thank PIF, our chair, Yasir Al-Rumayyan, and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club. I also want to say thank you to David [Hopkinson, the Newcastle CEO] and Ross [Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director] for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.”

On Friday, Wilson said they had no option but to allow Guimarães to leave. “What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave,” he said.

“That doesn’t mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. There’s no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer – it wasn’t. But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen.”

Sports.title: Liverpool agree to sign Barcelona’s Ronald Araújo on loan as Jacquet cover
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed to sign Ronald Araújo on a season-long loan from Barcelona after Andoni Iraola was faced with lack of defensive options for the start of the new season.

Concerns over Jérémy Jacquet – the France Under -21 defender who arrived last season for more than £50m – and injuries to Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni have left Liverpool short of options at the back after the departure of Ibrahima Konaté on a free transfer to Real Madrid.

Araújo, who was part of the Barça side that won La Liga last season, will add much-needed cover in the short-term. The Uruguay defender is expected to complete his medical on Sunday.

The deal for the 27-year-old is believed to contain an option to buy at the end of the season. Araújo has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona, but only made 11 league starts last season.

Liverpool have shown an interest in Aston Villa’s Ezri Konsa, but were put off by the £60m valuation of the England defender. Arsenal have had an initial approach for Konsa rejected.

Jacquet, who signed from Rennes in February, has not made a competitive appearance after picking up a serious shoulder injury last season and did not feature during Liverpool’s three-match tour of the United States. Iraola said last week that he has been feeling “some discomfort, so we don’t want to rush him”.

The Liverpool manager added: “He comes from a lot of months without playing. And obviously I would like to try with him with Virgil [van Dijk] when he recovers, because with the injury of Joe we’ve been without senior centre-backs. But we have to be careful with Jeremy.”

Sports.title: Why Super Furry Animals joined music’s dash to cross over football’s vinyl frontier | Emma John
Sports.content:
As someone born on the cusp of the gen X-millennial divide, I am the perfect target for today’s 90s nostalgia. I played my modest, teenage part in the Battle of Britpop (verbal skirmisher, Blur division); I fervently sang – and, God help me, believed – that Things Can Only Get Better. Super Furry Animals were a band I knew only distantly, via the transgressive thrill of that song they had with all the swearing in. And yet the news they’ll be shirt sponsor for a Welsh football club this season has managed to whisk me straight back to a time when things seemed simpler, kinder and more hopeful.

Nearly three decades have passed since Super Furry Animals last had their logo on a football kit. Back in 1999, their frontman Gruff Rhys and bassist Guto Pryce, both Cardiff City fans, persuaded their Bangor-born bandmates to lay down their north Wales allegiances for the duration of the Bluebirds’ Welsh Cup run – which was, incidentally, all they could afford. The cup shirts cost them £2,000 and were, according to Rhys, knock-offs made for ice hockey. This year’s beneficiaries are a more modest outfit: Cwmbran Celtic, just relegated from Wales’s second tier. Cwmbran is the town where the band send their stage props for repair, and given the props in question are giant inflatable bears, you wonder whether they could get one installed in goal.

Super Furry Animals aren’t the only 90s band involved: Scottish post-rockers Mogwai have sponsored the men’s away strip, with 10% of the profits from all shirt sales going to a grassroots music charity.

There has traditionally been an element of patronage when famous musicians do football, from Elton John’s time as chair of Watford, to Robbie Williams’s 2024 elevation to Port Vale club president. The pattern is a repeating one: local lads (they’re usually lads) make good, and want to give back to the team they’ve followed since they were little. Wet Wet Wet were the first to go down the shirt-sponsorship route with Clydebank in 1993. The team’s shirts turned out to be a more timeless design than the loud, oversized suits that Marti Pellow’s crew wore the day they unveiled them.

Slapping your logo on your home side’s shirt was a charitable endeavour, rather than an investment. Nothing underscored this point better than Fatboy Slim’s relationship with Brighton & Hove Albion. The DJ’s record label first sponsored their shirts in the late 90s, back when the team’s financial straits had left them flirting with extinction, and Tony Bloom’s billions were still waiting to be won. It was particularly appropriate back then that Micky Adams’s men should run out on to the field with their chests declaring them SKINT.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Zamora in Brighton’s home kit sponsored by Fatboy Slim. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

Musical match-ups have tended, therefore, towards the endearing, not the cool. Jake Bugg sponsored Notts County not to market his own music, but to evangelise the Midlands team on his global tours. And it’s even cuter when bands have sponsored kids’ teams. The late Lemmy of Motörhead was tickled by the thought of a Lincolnshire under-10s team sporting his Snaggletooth skull mascot on their fronts; unfortunately the resultant all-black kit too closely resembled referees’ uniforms and the children were banned from wearing it in league matches. Still, the idea had an enduring appeal: the Prodigy, Biffy Clyro, Sleaford Mods and Franz Ferdinand have all paid for youth kits.

In the last couple of years, though, the relationship between bands and football teams has turned serious. The move to monetise the “adjacent audiences” of pop and sporting fandom means shirt sponsorship is no longer a way of artists showing their support, but a marketing and merchandising opportunity in its own right.

Spotify’s deal with Barcelona got the ball rolling, with Coldplay, Karol G, Rosalía and Travis Scott each briefly appearing on the shirtfront, and limited-edition replicas costing more than £340 a pop. The footie-kit-as-streetwear trend means bands aren’t “sponsors” any more, they’re “collaborators”. Hence Manchester United’s pre-match shirts don’t bear the name of the Stone Roses, just their album artwork. And while that may have baffled a few younger fans – the club’s website ran a post explaining who the Madchester group were for the gen Z-ers – it still reflects a genuine connection. Ian Brown is a lifelong Red, and the team has walked out to This Is the One since Gary Neville first requested it two decades ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Coldplay show off their Barcelona shirts. Photograph: Fc Barcelona Handout/EPA

Whereas a year ago, if you’d been asked at a pub quiz what Paris Saint-Germain had in common with a K-pop band, or what Pink Floyd had to do with a Serie A team, you’d have been within your rights to say “nothing”. The answer, now, is clothing ranges – PSG teamed up with the girl group Blackpink to optimise fan engagement in Asia, while Inter marked the 50th anniversary of the album release of Wish You Were Here.

All this can be confusing for the simple-minded sports lover like me. What is a culture-forward lifestyle capsule, anyway? It sounds like something Musk and Bezos want to blast to Mars in. Creating a sporting look now involves an advanced understanding of fashion arithmetic: at last year’s Euros it was Admiral x Spice Girls, now it’s the Rolling Stones x England Cricket x Castore. These are powerful equations, as when a 2025 Bohemian FC x Fontaines DC shirt (raised to the power of Greta Thunberg when she wore it on her flotilla to Gaza) = £££££ for charity. Maybe Ed Sheeran’s Mathematics tour top for Ipswich was an omen. Or perhaps this is a fad, and the music industry will soon move on to something new. GQ, which has declared “blokecore” over, says we’ll be wearing classic rugby tops by autumn/winter. Sounds delightfully 90s to me.

Sports.title: Will Lankshear starts off in style to see Middlesbrough past Wrexham
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear’s debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round. Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener but when Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter’s cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle’s cross and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt. Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento’s cross into Lankshear’s path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining but Morgan Whittaker’s low strike rebounded off the post.

After the match the Middlesbrough manager, Kim Hellberg, expressed his delight with the instant impact Will Lankshear has made since joining the club. “He was very impressive and the most impressive thing has been seeing how well he has worked on the training ground,” Hellberg said. “How hard he works on the training ground and how much he wants to learn.

“It’s a joy to watch and when you add the person he is to the quality he has as a footballer on the pitch, you have a very good striker. I’m happy to have him here.”

Wrexham’s manager, Phil Parkinson, felt his side had given a decent account of themselves just four days after returning from a pre-season tour of the US. Parkinson said: “I thought we had enough half-chances, particularly in the first half, to have progressed in the competition. The game really separated from one quality finish from their lad. We had some good build-up play, but just didn’t quite have that clinical edge.

“It was a big ask in terms of coming back from America on Monday and you’ve got to give the lads credit for going close. There were a lot of positives in the performance.”

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho in December last year.

Scotland Yard said the striker had been charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm. Toney, who plays for the Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, is due to appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported in December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt. It claimed a fan recognised the footballer and grabbed at him while seeking a photograph with him before the incident.

On Friday the Metropolitan police said the charges related to an incident on 6 December at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London, reportedly the now-closed 100 Wardour Street.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was at the centre of one of the most curious transfers on deadline day in August 2024 when he completed a late move from Brentford to Al-Ahli worth a reported £40m. He has also played for Newcastle United and his home town club Northampton Town, as well as several others on loan as he looked to establish himself.

Seen as a late bloomer in football terms, he had made only two Premier League appearances before his 25th birthday, but went on to score 67 goals in 128 appearances over the next three seasons at the top level.

He has played 10 times for England, scoring once in a friendly match against Belgium in 2024, and was part of the 2026 World Cup squad, making appearances against Argentina in the semi-final and in the win over France as England finished third.

Sports.title: Jay-Z’s Roc Nation Sports making waves in European football transfer market
Sports.content:
In the end there was a clear winner. And Jay-Z’s latest victory came only 24 hours after the first record featuring him actually rapping for four years had been released by his wife, Beyoncé, on an extended remix pack of Morning Dew (Donk).

These days, the man who remains one of the most influential artists in hip-hop has his fingers in many pies, from the streaming service Tidal and his own streetwear brand, to champagne and cognac. But it is Roc Nation Sports – an offshoot of his entertainment company of the same name founded in 2008 – making headlines in the summer transfer window.

Established five years later in partnership with Creative Artists Agency, it began mainly representing players from the NBA, NFL and MLB, including Kevin Durant. Bayern Munich’s Jérôme Boateng was the first football client, in 2015, before Roc Nation Sports International (RNSI) was established four years later with a focus on stars at big European clubs.

Based in London, it now has more than 100 players on its books, including Vinícius Júnior – the Brazil forward who signed a lucrative new contract with Real Madrid this week believed to be worth around €25m. That came after Arsenal had been linked with a blockbuster move for the 26-year-old.

In July 2023 RNSI took over the successful Brazilian agents TFM – who already represented Vinícius, Gabriel Martinelli, and Endrick – and renamed it Roc Nation Sports Brazil.

In negotiations that have lasted two years, it had hoped to persuade Real to increase their star asset’s salary to €30m a year to match Kylian Mbappé, and allowed his contract to enter its final 12 months in an effort to drum up interest elsewhere. While Arsenal – now exploring other attacking options including Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye – are believed to have been willing to pay a big fee for Vinícius, it is understood that they thought signing him on a free transfer next season was more likely.

Nonetheless, Real upped their offer and Vinícius stayed. It is a decision that looks likely to cost them the chance to sign Rodri from Manchester City after Barcelona stole a march on their great rivals.

View image in fullscreen A phonecall from Vinícius Júnior reportedly led to Yan Diomande signing with Roc Nation Sports. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP

On the same day as the new six-year contract for Vinícius was announced, Yan Diomande flew to the Spanish capital to complete his record £115m transfer from RB Leipzig. The 19-year-old – who has made only 46 appearances at senior level for the German club and for Leganés in the Spanish second division but is already the most expensive African player in history – was pictured with his agents, Nathan Campbell and Kareem Gbaja on a private jet. RNSI has been reported to have been paid up to £17m in commission and fees.

A long-running saga that began when Liverpool had a £70m bid rejected by Leipzig in June ended with Diomande signing a seven-year deal at the Bernabéu on Thursday. It has provided a telling insight into the mechanisms of a modern transfer, with every week bringing a fresh twist. Having been told they must pay in excess of £100m to sign Diomande, Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the race at the end of July after releasing a statement that said the European champions “will not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents”.

RNSI has also had to fend off two legal challenges, including one from the former Bournemouth winger Max Gradel who claims that his agency, Maxidel Management, had an existing agreement with Diomande. Gradel has filed a complaint with Fifa, although world football’s governing body did not block the player’s move to Real. Dez Bamba – who is president of Diomande’s first club, AFI Sud Comoé in Côte d’Ivoire – has said that the winger was persuaded to join RNSI after receiving a call from Vinícius. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Meanwhile, the Rainbow World Group instigated proceedings at the high court in London and the British Virgin Islands against Diomande in mid-June “to enforce binding image rights and intellectual property agreements tied to his early career development”. It is claimed Rainbow invested significant resources in the winger, including taking him for trials at Chelsea, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Newcastle before he was signed by Leganés. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Given Diomande’s meteoric rise, perhaps it is no surprise that clubs are flocking to invest in African academies.

Jeff Luhnow – the former general manager of the Astros and St Louis Cardinals who won three World Series baseball titles and was chief executive of Blue Crow, the ex-owner of Leganes, until the club was sold to 885 capital in June - told the Guardian last year Diomande was expected to be the first of many after they set up recruitment and development programmes in several African countries, including Ghana and Zambia, in the past several years. “We’ve got more players like that in our pipeline,” said Luhnow.

RNSI announced in November that it has signed eight young African stars, including the Ghana Under-17 midfielder Joseph Narbi and Francis Gomez, a Gambian winger currently at AC Horsens in Denmark. “We believe Africa is a hotbed of untapped footballing potential, and our expansion here is a natural progression of our global vision,” said Campbell.

In the dog-eat-dog world of football agents Jay Z’s new kids on the block are certainly making their presence felt.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi suffers tragic loss of father as Jorge Messi dies aged 68
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's father, Jorge Messi, has passed away at the age of 68 after battling illness.

The father of the Argentine football icon had been experiencing health issues recently, which the Messi family confirmed during the World Cup.

3 Jorge was the father of Argentina superstar Lionel Messi Credit: Getty

Jorge was a central figure in Messi's career, having acted as his son's agent since the age of 14.

Messi's first club, Newell's Old Boys, paid tribute in a statement.

It read: “Club Atlético Newell’s Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario.

“Recognized leproso fan, businessman, and father of the Argentine national team captain, Lionel Andrés Messi.

“Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.

“His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory.

“Thank you for teaching him to love these colours.

“The Board of Directors, members, athletes, and the entire leprosa family embrace with affection Celia, Lionel, Rodrigo, Matías, and María Sol, and all their loved ones and close ones in this difficult moment.

“Farewell forever, leproso."

His death comes less than a month after it was revealed that Jorge had been 'under medical supervision' for an unspecified health issue.

3 Jorge Messi has passed away following a battle with illness Credit: Getty

With this occurring at the start of the World Cup, Messi was in tears after scoring his first goal of the tournament against Algeria, and later revealed he had been struggling with issues off the pitch.

Speaking post-match, he said: “My tears after the first goal? I’ve had some tough days, it wasn’t related to football, and those feelings were because of that.

"I thank my teammates, the technical staff, and the delegation for helping me.”

As well as acting as his agent, Jorge was the driving force behind Messi's career.

He travelled with his son to Barcelona when he first joined the Spanish giants' La Masia academy as a 13-year-old.

Jorge remained at Messi's side throughout his unprecedented career, which has seen him win a staggering 13 Ballon d'Or awards, four Champions League titles, and the 2022 World Cup.

3 Jorge Messi was in the ground to watch his son lift the 2022 World Cup trophy in Qatar Credit: Getty

Messi's father was in attendance to watch him lift the Jules Rimet trophy in Qatar, a moment which many felt cemented his status as football's greatest-ever player.
