Sports.title: Police swarm to intervene in wild EFL Cup fan fight as club release statement
Sports.content:
Port Vale have released a statement in response to a violent brawl among the club’s supporters in Friday’s Carabao Cup clash against Wolves.

Police were forced to intervene midway through the match at Molineux with punches exchanged between Vale fans in the away end.



1 Wolves booked their spot in the Carabao Cup second round with a convincing win over Port Vale Credit: Getty

A number of fans were caught up in the melee with others – including children – making a desperate attempt to get out of the way.

The incident appeared to start from a punch by a supporter which sparked a flurry of violent exchanges as fans weighed into the skirmish.

Police were able to quickly break up the violence although those involved continued to hurl verbal abuse at one another.



In a statement released on Saturday morning, the League Two club vowed to investigate the incident with the help of the Championship club.

It read: "We’re aware of an incident in the stands at last night’s game and will be working closely with Wolverhampton Wanderers and the relevant authorities to establish the facts surrounding it.



"We take matters of this nature seriously and will consider any appropriate action once the facts have been established."

Wolves booked their spot in the Carabao Cup second round with a 3-0 win over Port Vale on the night.



The Championship side netted all three goals before the interval with Adam Armstrong, Andre and Ferran Lopez all on the scoresheet.

Port Vale boss Jon Brady admitted he was pleased with the showing at Molineux but rued his side’s failure to find the net.

"I thought in the first 15 minutes we had two of the best efforts," Brady said. "Jammo (Jaheim Headley) hits the bar, if it goes in, it could have been a different story, maybe. Three big chances we had.

"I could have come here and play 5-4-1 but I wanted us to go brave as a team and we went after them at times. I was really pleased with some of our play. We just didn’t put the ball into the back of the net.



"You’re playing a team that is expected to go back into the PL with top-class players.

"We pushed and I feel we showed a very determined side to us. But some of the play from them was fantastic. I’m really pleased and proud of the boys tonight."

Meanwhile, Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto said: "I'm happy for sure. A first victory is important to bring confidence.

"A lot of things still to improve, that is normal. But we want to stay at a good level to start the season.



"We still need to bring in players that can improve the level of the team. I want things done as soon as possible but the market is delayed because of the World Cup."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi subjected to World Cup murder threat, US authorities reveal
Sports.content:
A US police report has revealed that Lionel Messi was the subject of a suicide bomb threat during the World Cup.

Spanish newspaper Marca has disclosed details from a chilling American police report, which lists all the security threats faced by the FBI and the International Police Cooperation Center (IPCC) this summer.



3 Lionel Messi was reportedly the target of several terror threats during the World Cup Credit: Getty

According to the news outlet, Argentina superstar Messi received more threats than any other player throughout the tournament.

The risk extended to his national teammates, with the report revealing one plot during their final group game against Jordan.

One man is said to have rung up Dallas Airport and warned that he and two others would storm the stadium with "homemade bombs and an AR-15 [rifle]."



Messi was named as a specific target, with the suspected bomber making explicit mention of him, as well as vowing to attack 'police officers and players from both teams'.

This was repeated again in Argentina's round of 16 clash with Egypt, where their captain was targeted by a bomb threat.



One of the suspects wrote on their social media: "I’m going to enter Atlanta Stadium and blow up Messi with four bombs strapped to my body."

During that same match, the police received a call from another man claiming he had left “three bombs” inside bins across the stands.



This caused the entire stadium to be searched with explosive-detection dogs, but ultimately turned out to be a false alarm.

Ronaldo also targeted

Messi’s rival Cristiano Ronaldo was also an alleged victim of World Cup attack fears.

According to the police report, a FIFA employee reported the presence of a 'suspicious man' to the FBI, who had asked for details about the Portugal icon's accommodation.

3 Cristiano Ronaldo was subjected to worrying fan behaviour during the World Cup Credit: Getty



Two days later, Houston police are said to have tracked down the same man and located him in the hotel where the Portugal team were staying.

Another individual was then arrested in Toronto over a similar incident, having tried to get in a lift with Ronaldo, later claiming they only wanted to take selfie with him.

Referee abuse

As well as dealing with major threats towards players, the report also revealed referees were targeted with hate.

French referee Francois Letexier received more than 6,000 hate messages on his personal WhatsApp after officiating Argentina's controversial last-16 win over Egypt.



With Egypt manager Hossam Hassan later accusing FIFA of bias towards Argentina after being left furious with refereeing decisions, fans followed suit.

Egyptian supporters hounded the official, as well as aiming furious messages at VAR referee Willy Delajod, including death threats.

3 Referee Francois Letexier was mobbed by Egypt's players during their World Cup exit to Argentina, before suffering further onslaught online Credit: Getty

The police report disclosed that the French pair had to reinforce the security of their homes and families in France after the incident.



As well as players requiring police intervention out in the US, other national teams received protection on home soil.

The South Korea national team were given a police escort as they returned home from the World Cup, after crashing out in the group stage in North America.

Around 160 airport and riot police were reportedly deployed as the players were met by fans hurling abuse at manager Hong Myung-bo, who stepped down from his role after the tournament.

Sports.title: Five Premier League stars who face make-or-break season in battle to prove themselves
Sports.content:
Five Premier League stars who face make-or-break season in battle to prove themselves

A huge season awaits for five high-profile Premier League stars.

With a little under two weeks until the big kick off, the moment for redemption is fast approaching.

7 The Premier League's big boys are plotting a way to knock champions Arsenal off their perch Credit: Getty

Whopping transfer fees and reputations are on the line with hope and expectation likely to be ramped up on last season’s underachievers.

One club hoping for a stronger return on their investment is Liverpool.

The Reds’ mammoth shopping spree 12 months ago failed to yield the required results proving that cherry picking Europe's top talents doesn’t necessarily guarantee success.

The same can be said of Chelsea who will be hoping their most recent nine-figure signing Morgan Rogers can hit the ground running.

Meanwhile, the Blues will be looking to a familiar face to find his groove again after a below-par campaign last time around.

There are also those who are yet to hit top form due to injury or a loss of form sparking questions of whether they can turn around their fortunes.

Discussing the importance of the upcoming season for five Premier League talents, talkSPORT’s Shebahn Aherne and Tony Cascarino looked at who fell below expectations last season and how they can turn their fortunes around.

Liverpool: Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz & Mikos Kirkez

The trio arrived at Anfield last season for a combined £265million in the hope of propelling the Reds into a period of domestic dominance.

However, nothing could have prepared Liverpool for what was to come with Isak suffering a leg fracture, while Wirtz and Kerkez struggled to impose themselves on Arne Slot's team.

Former Chelsea striker Cascarino believes all three must step up this season if Liverpool are to get themselves back among the title contenders.

7 Florian Wirtz found the going tough during his first season at Anfield Credit: AFP

7 More will be expected of £125m signing Alexander Isak this season Credit: Getty

7 Kerkez struggled at times last season but will be hopeful of an improved campaign this time round Credit: Getty

“The obvious ones are Isak and even more so Florian Wirtz,” he said.

“I think you could put Kerkez in that bracket as well being a left back but for me the outstanding one that’s got to play better than last year is Wirtz and I’m giving the benefit of the doubt to Isak due to injury.

“They invested a lot of money in Wirtz. I think he has to make things happen for Liverpool.

“He’s a quick footballer and last year I thought he was guilty of too many flicks where he was giving the ball away.

“The very best teams keep the ball and the flicks made them lose possession. When they lost possession, they were in trouble. That was the reason Liverpool conceded goals.”

Manchester United: Mason Mount

Liverpool’s bitter rivals Manchester United enjoyed a return to form last term under the guidance of former midfielder Michael Carrick.

7 Mason Mount has shown promising signs so far in pre-season as he looks to get his United career on track Credit: Getty

United secured third spot and a much-needed return to the riches of Champions League football.

Like Liverpool, the Red Devils were forced to contend with injuries of their own, one of which being Mason Mount.

The midfielder has been blighted by injury since joining the club from Chelsea in 2023.

His time in the treatment room has seen him miss out on Euro 2024 and this summer’s World Cup with England.

Mount has spent a total of 394 days on the sidelines since arriving at Old Trafford and Aherne believes he should look no further than his Manchester United teammate for inspiration.

“He needs to have a strong season,” Aherne said of Mount.

7 Luke Shaw played nearly every minute under Carrick after overcoming his injury owes Credit: Getty

“Luke Shaw played every game last season and really got his season back on track, sorted out the injury issues and he was brilliant.

“But Mason Mount, you always hear that he’s the perfect pupil. He’s a very smart and intelligent player and when he’s on his game. He’s brilliant.

“You just hope that this season he will come good.”

Cascarino is also hopeful the 27-year-old could find his level again and highlighted one of his key attributes.

“They paid £55m for him. He was injured at Chelsea before he got to Old Trafford and he was a terrific player for Chelsea,” Cascarino said.

“He can play in that floating position like Wirtz and he can get a goal.

“Manchester United need a really fit Mason Mount, if not to start, then to challenge for other player’s spots in the team.

“He’s a good finisher, get him in goalscoring positions and he will finish. It would be like a new signing.”

Chelsea: Cole Palmer

Another player hoping for a renaissance this season is Chelsea’s Cole Palmer.

7 Cole Palmer is hoping for better fortunes this season Credit: Getty

The midfielder struggled to emulate his superb 2024/25 campaign last time out having struggled with injury and poor form.

After scoring for England in the Euro 2024 finals against Spain, Palmer was left out of the England squad for the World Cup.

His omission summed up his season at Stamford Bridge, however Cascarino expects it to merely be a blip as he prepares for life under Xabi Alonso.

“Cole Palmer didn't play as well as he did before,” he added. “I’d imagine he’ll come back to his best and by the set-up they’ve done this year and the experience they’ve brought in, I think Chelsea will be a better team.”

Sports.title: Arsenal told to raid Premier League rivals for star player in hunt for Vinicius Jr alternative
Sports.content:
Arsenal told to raid Premier League rivals for star player in hunt for Vinicius Jr alternative

Arsenal have been tipped to try and sign Brighton star Kaoru Mitoma after missing out on Vinicius Junior.

The Gunners saw their hopes of signing Real Madrid superstar Vinicius end on Thursday, as it was announced he had signed a new six-year deal with the Spanish giants.



5 Arsenal have been forced back to the drawing board after missing out on Vinicius Credit: Getty

But before that, the Brazilian was heavily linked with a move to the Emirates, amid reports of a stand-off over a new contract.

Vinicius had entered the final year of his previous contract this summer, leading Arsenal to weigh up an approach for him in the hope of a blockbuster transfer.

However, their dreams soon ended as the forward then agreed fresh terms on a new long-term deal at the Santiago Bernabeu.



What next for Arsenal?

Arsenal will now begin their search for alternative attacking targets, with Mikel Arteta keen to strengthen his left-wing options after the club announced Bruno Guimaraes' £75million arrival in midfield.

The Gunners have already secured the signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge after Leandro Trossard left to join Besiktas, but have been continually linked with a more high-profile move this summer.



After missing out on Vinicius, talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs revealed that Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez is now a 'dream target', while Everton star Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola - who is being pursued by Liverpool - were other potential options.

'Scarily good'

talkSPORT pundit Tony Cascarino believes Brighton and Japan forward Mitoma could be exactly what Arsenal need on the left wing.



Mitoma has earned a strong reputation since joining the Seagulls in 2021, and has just a year left on his current contract at the Amex, meaning he could likely be bought for a cut price.

Speaking on the Weekend Sports Breakfast, Cascarino said: “If he was a tad younger and hadn't had so many injuries, I'd really look at him.

"I thought Mitoma, when he's been Brighton's best player, he's scarily good.

5 Mitoma signed for Brighton for a reported fee of just £2.7million in 2021 Credit: Getty



5 Julian Alvarez is wanted by Arsenal and has a £432m release clause in his Atletico Madrid contract Credit: Getty

“He had a poor season last year, and a number of injuries. I think he scored three goals in the league for Brighton last year.

"But he's a dangerous winger - he wants to take people on all the time. And Arsenal have got cover there, so, yeah [I'd go for him].”

Mitoma struggled for fitness in the 2025/26 campaign, and ultimately missed out on Japan's World Cup squad after suffering a hamstring injury against Wolves in May.



However, he has carved out a strong reputation over the last four years in the Premier League with Brighton.

The Japanese star marked his debut season in English football in the 2022/23 campaign by scoring seven league goals, helping the Seagulls to a best-ever sixth-place finish and sealing Europa League football.

His best-scoring season came in 2024/25, where he netted 10 times in the Premier League, before turning down interest from European giants Bayern Munich in the subsequent transfer window.

5 Mikel Arteta has a host of left-wing options to explore after missing out on Vinicius Jr Credit: Getty



Rashford option explored

Mitoma wasn't the only familiar name suggested as an option for Arsenal, with host Shebahn Aherne also highlighting Marcus Rashford's availability.

The England star's future remains unclear as he prepares to return to Manchester United after Barcelona chose not sign him permanently.

Rashford has long been tipped for a move to the Gunners, although no attempt to sign him has been made this summer, while bitter rivals Tottenham have even been touted as a potential destination.

But Cascarino was less sold on Arsenal snapping him up, admitting his up-and-down career raises questions marks over his suitability.



On Rashford, he said: "It's such a hard call on Marcus Rashford, because there's a part of you that thinks, absolutely, he could go and [shine at a big club].

"At his very best, he can really hurt teams. But everyone's the same thing - they're not sure.

5 Marcus Rashford hasn't played for Man United since 2024, after two loan spells away from Old Trafford Credit: Getty

"Everybody I spoke to about Marcus Rashford is not sure whether he could go and do it for a club, whether he could do it and stay at Manchester United. I just don't know."



With new Red Devils boss Michael Carrick previously leaving the door open for Rashford to be reintegrated into the squad, Cascarino admitted his future could still lie at Old Trafford.

He added: “It's a coin flip, but I think Man United are in a perfect position to go, 'We'll have a look'. Michael Carrick [is] managing him now, new one. I don't know, it's a real tough one.”

Sports.title: Ashley Young ‘gutted’ Man United did not hijack Premier League rivals’ transfer
Sports.content:
Ashley Young is the latest Manchester United legend to express his disappointment at Danny Welbeck’s move to Chelsea.

The striker signed a two-year deal at Stamford Bridge last month after enjoying a superb season at Brighton.



4 Danny Welbeck's sparkling form last season earned him a surprise move to Chelsea Credit: AFP

Young and Welbeck shared the Old Trafford dressing room for three seasons towards the end of Alex Ferguson’s reign in charge before the striker was eventually sold to Arsenal.

Welbeck has gone on to enjoy a fruitful career with spells at the Emirates Stadium before stints at Sunderland, Watford and more recently, Brighton.

The 35-year-old posted arguably his best season at the Amex Stadium last season, netting 14 goals, sparking calls for him to be included in England’s World Cup squad.



Welbeck was unable to do enough to break into Thomas Tuchel’s 26-man squad; however, his efforts were hugely appreciated by new Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso.

And while Young is pleased for his former teammate, he expressed some regret that Welbeck was unable to secure a move back to the Red Devils.



“They’ve (Chelsea) made some good signings and they need some experience in that squad,” Young told talkSPORT at the launch of the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 set.

“He’s a really good friend of mine, Welbs is. I’ve been speaking to him the last couple of weeks."



Asked whether Welbeck was excited ahead of the new season at Stamford Bridge, Young said: “Yeah, of course he is. He’s delighted to be signing for Chelsea, especially at this stage of his career.

“He’s proved himself time and time again.

"Could he have been on the plane going to the World Cup? For me, I’m probably being biased in saying he should have, but he wasn’t.

4 Ashley Young spoke to talkSPORT at the launch of the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 set Credit: Topps

“He’s been fantastic and I’m gutted he hasn’t gone back to United, to be honest.”



Prior to his switch to west London, former United defender Rio Ferdinand sent out a desperate plea for the star to return to Old Trafford.

Posting on X, Ferdinand wrote: "Welbs…. Ignore + come back home! Champions League football next season in Manchester."

The sentiment was echoed by ex-Manchester United captain Gary Neville, who claimed the club should never have sold him to Arsenal in 2014.

“I said ten years ago that Manchester United should never have sold Danny Welbeck. He’s gone away and done brilliantly well,” Neville told Sky Sports.



“He’s coming into a little cameo at the end of his career, but he’s a fantastic player. I worked with him, obviously, as a team-mate, I worked with him with England as a coach, and he was fantastic for England.

4 Young and Welbeck were key players under Ferguson at Man United

4 Welbeck is already up and running with his new teammates Credit: Getty

“And he’s been good in the Premier League as well. It’s a good move for Chelsea, and it gives them a real option up front.”



After breaking through from the club’s academy under Ferguson, Welbeck quickly became disillusioned under David Moyes in the 2013/14 season.

Part of that frustration came from being played on the left wing, where he was unable to show his true qualities.

Opportunities as a central striker were further restricted under Louis van Gaal, and Welbeck was banished to the bench for the Dutchman's first three matches in charge.

That led to his eventual move to Arsenal, where he went on to score 32 goals, helping Arsene Wenger’s side lift the FA Cup twice.

Sports.title: ‘Toughest decision’ – Bruno Guimaraes releases emotional statement as Arsenal move announced
Sports.content:
Arsenal have officially confirmed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle.

Guimaraes joins the Gunners on a four-year contract, leaving St. James' Park after four years at the club.

3 Arsenal have completed one of the most high-profile signings of the summer Credit: Getty

The announcement of the move comes after a long transfer saga, with the Brazilian heavily linked all summer.

He had agreed personal terms with Arsenal at the start of July and by the end of the month, he asked to delay his travel to Newcastle's pre-season camp as talks with the Gunners progressed.

Now, he has completed his switch, becoming the Premier League champions' fourth signing of the transfer window, and the most expensive midfielder over 28 in football history.

Speaking after his Newcastle exit was confirmed, Guimaraes told the club's official channels: “This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together.

“I fell in love with this place. I really mean that. From my first day, the supporters, my teammates, Eddie and the staff, and everyone connected with the club made me and my family feel at home.

“I thank PIF, our chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan and Jamie Reuben for everything they have done for me and for this football club. I also want to say thank you to David and Ross for the huge respect to me throughout this process. They did everything they could to keep me at Newcastle, and I am very grateful for our time together.

“This move is very tough because Newcastle means so much to me, but I wanted to experience something new in my life. I feel ready for a new challenge for myself and my family. I had a very positive conversation with Matthias Jaissle, and I leave knowing the club is in very good hands.

“To the supporters, thank you will never be enough, but I say it with all my heart. I will always be proud to have been part of this club’s journey. Thank you for everything.”

Meanwhile, Arsenal's sporting director said: “We are delighted to welcome Bruno Guimaraes to our club.

“Bruno is a player with a great mentality and great quality, who will bring strong leadership to our squad.

“With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.

“Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.”

Guimaraes sticks to 'special' tradition

Guimaraes has marked his long-awaited arrival in north London by selecting a rare shirt number for Arsenal.

He has stuck with the No.39 shirt, which he made famous at Newcastle and also wore for Lyon and Atletico Paranaense.

No senior Gunners player has worn the number since Hector Bellerin switched from 39 to 24 ahead of the 2015/16 season.

The digits are very meaningful for Guimaraes though, and to keep them at Arsenal will be a special moment for him.

3 Guimaraes wears the No.39 shirt to pay homage to his father and life back in Brazil Credit: Getty

He previously explained to The Players' Tribune: "The number tells a story more beautiful than words can say.

"39. I know people think it’s a weird number for a footballer. But for me 39 is special — no, it’s more than that. It's magical.

"The number 39 gave me everything in life. It got me here to Newcastle. It fed me, clothed me, and paid for three-hour bus rides to pursue my dream.

"#039 was the dispatch number of my father’s taxi in Rio de Janeiro."

What other Arsenal players have worn 39?

By taking the No.39, Guimaraes becomes just the eighth Arsenal player ever to wear that number on their shirt.

3 Guimaraes is the fourth most expensive midfielder to join a Premier League side this window

As mentioned, Bellerin was the most recent senior player to don the digits, doing so 11 years ago.

However, youth star Harrison Dudziak had the 39 kit last season, but he didn't end up playing a senior game for the club.

Dudziak's contract expired in July, so his number is now free.

Before Dudziak and Bellerin, youth player Zak Ansah had the shirt in 2012/13, with Francis Coquelin having it before that in 2011/12.

Rui Fonte in 2008/09, Mark Howard in 2005/06 and Sebastian Larsson in 2004/05 have also worn the 39 for the Gunners.

Sports.title: Chelsea could release entire XI good enough to challenge for Europe before window shuts
Sports.content:
Chelsea could release entire XI good enough to challenge for Europe before window shuts

With 24 days remaining until the transfer window slams shut, Chelsea still have plenty of work to do.

Their summer spending so far is in and around the £300million mark, with a large chunk of this coming via the £117m signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

6 Alonso has a number of players at his disposal as Chelsea boss Credit: Getty

Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha have joined in pre-agreed deals, with Marco Palestra, Maxence Lacroix, Danny Welbeck, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson also through the door.

However, the numerous additions mean that the Chelsea first team squad has only increased in size, with 46 players listed in the squad on their website.

It's an eye-opening number for a club void of European football this season, though many of those listed are academy talents who are on their pre-season tour such as Reggie Walsh and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli.

Xabi Alonso has not specified how big he wants his squad to be, but he is unlikely to want a bloated team that could risk squad harmony.

Various players currently on the books have been linked with exits, and talkSPORT.com has selected a hypothetical XI that, on paper, could contend for European qualification in the Premier League.

Filip Jorgensen

Having been the second-choice goalkeeper to Robert Sanchez for much of his Chelsea career, Jorgensen is closing in on a departure.

He left their pre-season tour amid transfer interest, with sister club Strasbourg understood to be an option for the 24-year-old, who was linked with a move in January.

Jorgensen is also a Denmark international who will likely be looking for more consistent minutes in between the sticks.

Axel Disasi

The first half of the 2025/26 season was quiet for Disasi, but he was back on the pitch at West Ham United with a winter loan move.

Although the Hammers were relegated from the Premier League, the French defender made a good impression in east London and is not short of interest as September 1 approaches.

6 Disasi did well on loan at West Ham despite their relegation Credit: Getty

AC Milan and Roma are understood to have shown interest in Disasi, and Crystal Palace is another speculated destination for the centre-back, who can also play as a right-back.

Tosin Adarabioyo

Another defender who could be heading out of Stamford Bridge is Tosin, who could have done better to deny Tottenham Hotspur the winning goal in their pre-season friendly last week.

His appearances last season were sporadic, and many of these came as a substitute amid competition from Wesley Fofana, Trevoh Chalobah and Jorrel Hato.

However, with 116 Premier League outings to his name, the 28-year-old would add a depth of experience to any back line should he leave.

Benoit Badiashile

Chelsea's FA Cup fifth round victory against Wrexham on March 7 is the most recent match that Badiashile has played for the club.

The defender has featured just 13 times over the past two seasons and dealt with various fitness issues that have kept him sidelined.

6 Gusto (right) and Neto (left) are among the targets for City Credit: Getty

Badiashile is only 25, though, and reports have linked him with Serie A runners-up Napoli, a move that could initially see him join on loan before a permanent switch.

Malo Gusto

It was always going to be difficult for Gusto to hold down the right-back spot when club captain Reece James returned to full fitness.

Premier League rivals Manchester City are understood to be keen on the French full-back, who mostly plays on the right-hand side but can feature at left-back if needed.

Chelsea are understood to value Gusto at £75m and, even though a sale is not being actively looked at, it is possible this summer.

Pedro Neto

Enzo Maresca is seemingly eyeing some Chelsea reunions as the new City boss, with Neto another player to be linked with a switch.

With Rogers and Quenda through the door, Cole Palmer hoping to hit the ground running and Estevao Willian remaining an exciting prospect, the competition for places out wide is strong.

Neto could cost City in the region of £70m, while Liverpool have also emerged as a speculated new club for the Portuguese international.

Enzo Fernandez

Completing the hat-trick of Chelsea to City transfer speculation is Fernandez, whose future in west London has been uncertain for a matter of months now.

6 Fernandez could follow Marc Cucurella as a big-name departure Credit: Getty

After fuelling rumours of a move to Real Madrid, they released a statement to shut down any perceived interest by saying they have 'no intention' of signing him.

City interest in 2022 World Cup winner Fernandez was reported by talkSPORT in April and, with Rodri looking set to leave for Barcelona, this could certainly open the door for a transfer.

Dario Essugo

A thigh injury meant Essugo made a limited number of appearances in his debut season at Chelsea.

The 21-year-old ex-Sporting midfielder is a player who would certainly benefit from consistent minutes away from the club with a loan spell which, as per the BBC, he is open to.

Essugo has featured in all three of their pre-season fixtures thus far but with Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, Fernandez and new man Barco all midfield options, a temporary exit may be wise.

Mykhailo Mudryk

The Football Association announced on July 31 that Mudryk can play for Chelsea once again after the resolution of his anti-doping disciplinary proceedings.

Mudryk's last competitive appearance came in November 2024 and, after months of work to maintain his fitness away from the club, he was a late substitute against Juventus earlier this week.

Coventry City, managed by Chelsea legend Frank Lampard, are among the clubs interested in the winger, who remains electric on the wing.

6 Mudryk is back and available for Chelsea, but may need a loan spell Credit: Getty

Liam Delap

Chelsea were unable to see the best of Delap in his first season after his move from Ipswich Town, where he had become an exciting prospect in English football.

He found the back of the net on just one occasion in the league over 28 appearances, with Joao Pedro being the more impressive striker.

Despite his poor campaign, Delap remained a handful for defenders, has a physical presence up front, and Premier League interest in his services.

Nicolas Jackson

Bayern Munich signed Jackson on loan for the 2025/26 season and he was part of their Bundesliga title triumph alongside Harry Kane, scoring 11 goals in 34 appearances throughout the campaign.

He could have joined them permanently for around £56m, but the conditions to activate the obligation to buy were not met and he is back at Chelsea.

Jackson is on the pre-season tour but has been linked with Villa and Spurs, and is under consideration for an exit.

6 Here is how the Chelsea XI could line up

On paper, this team looks as though it would have a real crack at pushing for European qualification if it played in the Premier League.

However, the Champions League would be a real challenge, so it may have more success in reaching the Europa League or Conference League, depending on the number of qualifying spots for each.

Sports.title: Phil Parkes dead aged 79: Wolves legend passes away as tributes pour in for record-breaking 'gentle giant' goalkeeper
Sports.content:
Phil Parkes dead aged 79: Wolves legend passes away as tributes pour in for record-breaking 'gentle giant' goalkeeper

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Wolves legend Phil Parkes has died at the age of 79, the club confirmed on Saturday.

The former goalkeeper, who chalked up 382 appearances for Wolves during his remarkable 18-year spell at the club, suffered a fall at his home in 2025 and remained under medical supervision until his death, a club statement revealed.

'Legendary Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes sadly passed away this morning at the age of 79,' the statement, posted to the club's website on Saturday, read.

'The Hall of Fame inductee, affectionately nicknamed 'Lofty' due to his 6'4' frame, spent 18 years at Wolves and is known as one of the greatest ever goalkeepers to represent the club.'

Parkes joined the Midlands club as a schoolboy in 1960 and made his senior debut six years later, saving a penalty in a 3-2 victory over Preston North End.

A highlight of his career was helping Wolves reach the UEFA Cup final in 1972, which they lost on aggregate to Tottenham.

Wolves legend Phil Parkes, who played 382 games for the club, has died at the age of 79

Parkes still holds the record for most consecutive league games played at Wolves (127 games)

Parkes still holds the record for most consecutive league games played at Wolves, tallying a remarkable 127 games in a row during the early 1970s.

Following his retirement in 1983, which came five years after his departure from Wolves, he went on to serve on the committee of Wolves' former players association.

His old team-mate John Richards told BBC Radio WM on Saturday: 'It's a sad day, I've had so many calls this morning from former players and friends of Phil just passing on their best wishes and thoughts and prayers to the family.

'You've got to bear in mind Phil has been part of the Wolves family for the best part of 70 years. He's going to be a big loss.

'He was one of the people who would have your back. He looked frightening but he was the opposite. He was a big gentle giant until one of his friends was in trouble and then he was there to protect everybody.

'He was known as Lofty or the big man and he lived up to it in a lot of ways. He had a big heart as well.'

Asked in 2024 how he'd like his Wolves career to be remembered, he said: 'I hope my Wolves career is remembered with joy. I loved playing for this football club, I had a great time, so I just hope all the supporters enjoyed it too.'

Sports.title: South Korea FA says sorry for providing 'sexual services' to foreign referees on multiple occasions
Sports.content:
South Korea FA says sorry for providing 'sexual services' to foreign referees on multiple occasions

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

South Korea's national football association apologised on Saturday after a media report alleged it had provided 'sexual services' to foreign referees when they were in the country for international matches more than a decade ago.

South Korean broadcaster JTBC reported on Thursday that the Korea Football Association (KFA) had provided such services to foreign referees on multiple occasions in 2011 and 2012, including when they were in the country for qualifying matches for the 2014 World Cup and the 2012 London Olympics.

'We deeply apologise for causing concern over various issues involving the association, which emerged from a parliamentary hearing and an unprecedented search and seizure, and from reports about events from more than a decade ago, that even many within the organisation were unaware of,' the KFA said in a statement.

In its news report, JTBC cited a 2016 sports ministry investigation that found the KFA had provided inappropriate entertainment to foreign referees on seven occasions between March 2011 and March 2012, including trips to massage parlours where the fees had included the costs of sexual services.

The KFA did not immediately respond to an email seeking further comment and details.

'The association makes clear that inappropriate conduct of this kind, or the use of corporate cards for such purposes, is absolutely not currently taking place,' the KFA said in its statement.

South Korea's early exit at the World Cup group stages caused consternation at home

The allegations add to scrutiny of the association over a separate issue involving the appointment of former national team coach Hong Myung-bo.

Seoul police raided the KFA's offices on Thursday as part of an investigation related to Hong's appointment, police told Reuters.

Hong returned as national team coach in 2024 after a previous spell in charge from 2013 to 2014. His appointment drew scrutiny after the KFA abandoned a months-long search involving foreign candidates and selected Hong following a brief meeting.

The controversy resurfaced after South Korea's disappointing World Cup campaign ended in a group-stage exit.

Sports.title: Jorge Messi dead at 68: Tributes pour in for father of Lionel after months of health woes
Sports.content:
Jorge Messi dead at 68: Tributes pour in for father of Lionel after months of health woes

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lionel Messi's father Jorge has died at the age of 68, two months on from the family revealing he had been rushed to hospital with an ongoing 'health situation'.

The news was first reported by local media in Argentina, and has since been confirmed by Messi's first team, Newell's Old Boys, in a statement.

Jorge reportedly died in a hospital in Rosario, close to the family home, at around 10pm local time on Friday August 7.

In the statement, Newell's Old Boys, wrote in Spanish: 'Club Atletico Newell's Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario.

'Recognized leproso fan, businessman, and father of the Argentine national team captain, Lionel Andrés Messi. Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.

'His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory. Thank you for teaching him to love these colors.

Lionel Messi's father Jorge, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, has died at the age of 68

Messi cried on the pitch at the World Cup amid his father's long battle with health problems

'The Board of Directors, members, athletes, and the entire leprosa family embrace with affection Celia, Lionel, Rodrigo, Matías, and María Sol, and all their loved ones and close ones in this difficult moment. Farewell forever, leproso.'

The Daily Mail has reached out to Inter Miami and the Messi family for a further statement, and no cause of death has yet been revealed.

In a post on X, CONMEBOL - the governing body of football in South America - added: 'CONMEBOL deeply regrets the passing of Jorge Messi, father of Argentine footballer Lionel Messi. We accompany Lionel, his family, friends, and loved ones with respect and affection in this moment of profound grief. May he rest in peace.'

Football legend Messi was extremely close to his father, who also operated as his agent and de facto business manager throughout his career, overseeing his son's multi-million dollar empire off the pitch.

In recent months, though, the patriarch of the family had been dealing with an as-yet-unconfirmed medical issue that had seen him taken to hospital in his home country.

His illness first came to light when Lionel, 39, cried on the pitch at the World Cup in a rare public display of emotion.

After scoring a hat-trick against Algeria in Argentina's opening group game in Kansas City, Messi was questioned by journalists and said: 'No, honestly it's something completely unrelated to sports. It's been a few difficult days, complicated.'

Just hours later, journalist Eduardo Feinmann explained the reason for the tears in an interview on Radio Mitre, one of the country's most listened-to stations.

'This has to do with his father. His father is not in good health,' he said. 'For quite some time now, several months, since last year.

'And this week there were some situations that slightly worsened his health, and Messi is going through this internal struggle. In other words, like any human being.'

It has since been reported that Jorge suffered a 'medical episode' at his home in January of this year, and he was hospitalized as a result.

Messi's childhood sweetheart Antonela Roccuzzo has supported him throughout his career

Messi stands in front of his family (including father Jorge (third left) in Rosario in October 2003

Jorge arrives at son Lionel's wedding in 2017 with his wife Celia (L) and daughter Maria (R)

In the aftermath, he was said to have undergone cardiovascular and neurological tests, but no official diagnosis was shared by the family, who sought to keep Jorge's health out of the media.

Jorge's health became headline news again in June, when a broadcaster in Argentina falsely claimed he had died - before later issuing an emotional apology and stepping down from her job.

Lionel is the third of four children of Jorge and his wife Celia Cuccittini, and the pair remained together until his death.

They married in 1978 and split their time between Rosario and Miami, where their footballing superstar son currently plays for David Beckham's Inter Miami in MLS.

Before becoming Lionel's agent, Jorge worked for a steel manufacturer in Villa Constitucion, meeting his wife as a young man in Rosario - where the family then grew up.

Messi has two older brothers, Rodrigo and Matias, and a younger sister, Maria Sol.

Jorge has been at Messi's side throughout his historic career, which began in Argentina with Newell's Old Boys, before he moved to Spain to join Barcelona's famed La Masia academy in 2000.

He became the greatest of all-time in an incredible 21 years in Barcelona, before stunning the world with a move to Paris Saint-Germain - orchestrated by Jorge - in 2021.

After two seasons in the French capital, he moved to MLS and Inter Miami, where he remains to this day at the age of 39.

Jorge remained with his wife, and Lionel's mother, Celia Cuccittini, until his death on Friday

Jorge was Lionel's business manager and was alongside him for the tax fraud case in 2016

Messi gives his father a hug in Fort Lauderdale in November 2025, as his mother watches on

While Lionel's career has been magical on the pitch, it has not been without controversy off it, with Jorge famously by his son's side throughout his tax fraud case in 2016.

The pair sat together in front of the court, with Jorge in his role as his son's business manager, with the prosecution alleging that Messi failed to properly pay tax on income from his image rights between 2007 and 2009.

Ultimately, both father and son were convicted of three tax offenses, initially each receiving suspended 21-month prison sentences.

Jorge's sentence was subsequently reduced to 15 months upon review in 2017 by Spain's Supreme Court, with the pair also hit with substantial fines.

Sports.title: Inside Enzo Maresca's Man City training: Using mannequins to mimic low blocks, the Pep Guardiola drill he's scrapped - and why Phil Foden and Josko Gvardiol are central to his plans
Sports.content:
Inside Enzo Maresca's Man City training: Using mannequins to mimic low blocks, the Pep Guardiola drill he's scrapped - and why Phil Foden and Josko Gvardiol are central to his plans

Enzo Maresca missed a trick if none of his staff thought to stick a GPS vest on him as he worked just south of the river in South Korea’s capital.

Forget putting Manchester City’s squad through their paces, nobody can have covered more ground during Saturday’s training session than the manager who undoubtedly has similar mannerisms and ideas to the guy who he has replaced.

Maresca drove this hour, planted right in the middle of the action for almost all of it. Acting as a tigerish opposing defender as a soft, and often dull, four-song playlist – Wonderwall, Hey Jude, Don’t Look Back in Anger and Blue Moon - looped endlessly for the few thousand local fans watching on.

There were key takeaways from this as to what Maresca’s City will look like in the coming months. ‘The willingness of the players has been very good,’ he said. ‘They have been very open-minded with a new manager arriving, changing some structures and patterns.’

Enzo Maresca is extremely hands-on in training sessions with his new Manchester City squad

City are acclamitising to life under Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola earlier this summer

PASS, PASS, PASS

Maresca stood by Phil Foden, directing traffic from the central areas to 11 players who appear to be starting the club’s third and final friendly of their pre-season tour against Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

City’s boss had chaired a brief huddle before the start of their first proper tactical drill, one that would last 15 minutes – long enough to hammer home the principles but not too long to allow minds to drift. Pep Guardiola’s always used to be around the same length.

Maresca managed to sweep through 16 attempts at building from the back, something he is insistent on perfecting before the Premier League campaign kicks off in a fortnight. Goalkeeping coach Michele De Bernardin fizzed crosses to Gianluigi Donnarumma and from there, City were told to play.

City largely built up slowly, using centre halves Ruben Dias and Vitor Reis, needing to keep their concentration while playing against nobody – basically walking through the process other than when Maresca pressed the ball. Four converged on an Antoine Semenyo cross, indicating the coach’s willingness to flood the box.

Those included Josko Gvardiol, who attacked the inside channel, seen as a key area of exploitation – the defender being talked through that by Maresca away from the group before they began the next stage of the session.

Phil Foden appears central to his plans after having frequent conversations with the Italian

Josko Gvardiol's underlapping runs through the inside channel are a key focus of his attack

PUT INTO PRACTICE

Two banks of mannequins were rooted into the grass, mimicking a 5-4-1 mid block – something City expect to face a great deal this term. Ten bibbed players, those slated for the bench against Atletico, acted as the opposition this time.

Again, Maresca reaffirmed Foden’s job with him. The chosen team were to replicate the last 15 minutes with more pace. White cones were placed across the width of the pitch, just inside the attacking half, to perhaps indicate how high Maresca intends his back four to stand when in possession.

First-team coach Danny Walker, formerly in City’s academy, brought energy to this, cajoling the fluorescent orange bibs – who would also then have the opportunity to play through a defensive opposition themselves to make sure all were giving practical experience of the messages.

This was again more about honing the patterns rather than anything overly competitive, the defensive 10 not really engaging across a shorter drill. Maresca clapped when moves were resurrected, like when Gvardiol took control of a situation when the ball bobbled in the box, rather than perfect goals.

He had another word with the Croatian before the third drill. Clearly, he is a key part of the plans.

Maresca has scrapped rondos from training sessions, a popular drill under Guardiola (above)

HIGHER STAKES

The longest part of the session, 16 minutes, was spent with just eight defensive bibs – seemingly mirroring City being able to beat an early press and bypassing two opponents.

They had an overload and this is where the expectation was to move possession with quick precision. Maresca volleyed a pass straight out to Savinho to restart play before the defence could rearrange themselves, designed to manufacture different bits of game play.

When Foden smashed one effort past reserve goalkeeper Marcus Bettinelli, Maresca span and demanded a new ball from coaches behind him, wanting quick repetition. There was some competitiveness in this and when the bibs attacked, it proved the only time throughout that Sunday’s first team did any defensive work whatsoever.

That suggests how Maresca envisages doing the majority of his work and so it is little wonder that the mood of players around the first two weeks has been encouraging. As the final section became more rudimentary – crossing wide and attacking, with Maresca wanting to utilise the wings – Donnarumma was undergoing more work on his 40-yard passing with goalkeeping coaches. A late shooting competition seemed optional. Maresca was still in amongst it all.

He was not early on though. The Italian missed the start, owing to a late arrival for media duties. Head of performance Chris Elderkin – one of very few still here from Guardiola’s reign - led the warm ups, devising team games that saw some players – Foden included – playfully arguing about the implementation of rules throughout.

There were no rondos, a past staple. But there was always a ball in play. While some things change, others remain the same. In keeping with the man in the middle.

Sports.title: Man United youngster wanted by Southampton, Ruggeri joining Villa could free up Romero switch, Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man United youngster wanted by Southampton, Ruggeri joining Villa could free up Romero switch, Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Loan star Ronald Araujo to check in at Liverpool

Ronald Araujo will have a medical at Liverpool on Sunday ahead of completing is loan with option to buy from Barcelona.

The fee on the option to buy for the 27-year-old defender is £47million.

Araujo is preparing to travel to link up with Liverpool ahead of signing his contract and meeting his new teammates tomorrow.

The Uruguay international gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at centre-back and right-back.

Araujo wanted to go because after talks with coach Hansi Flick it was apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts and he believes he will find greater opportunity to do so under Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

The Spanish champions are working to offload a number of players as they look to upgrade their squad. They are focused on signing Rodri from Manchester City and still want to strengthen their own centre-back options and at striker.

Araujo will say farewell to Barcelona teammates today prior to heading for Merseyside on Sunday.

Liverpool remain in talks for Paris Saint-Germain pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Full story

Saints eye Man United youngster Kamason

Manchester United full-back Jaydan Kamason is wanted by Southampton.

The Championship side would like the 19-year-old England youth international on a permanent transfer and he is also receiving enquiries from others wanting him on loan.

Preston North End, Blackburn Rovers, Bristol City and Sheffield Wednesday have shown interest in the right-back while there are clubs abroad keen to take him.

Kamason though has a lot of admirers at Old Trafford. He was one of the academy players who excelled in the opening games of United's pre-season, particularly in the 5-0 win over Rosenborg.

He was the first player to sign scholarship forms at United after coming through the club's Emerging Talent Programme, which he joined at 10, while playing for grassroots team Stockport Vikings.

United have yet to decide on plans for his development but he looks likely to stay around Michael Carrick's squad until January.

Goalkeeper Radek Vítek has completed his move to Middlesbrough on a permanent transfer from United in a deal worth up to £14m.

Jaydan Kamason has excelled in pre-season games for United and has plenty of admirers

Geronimo Rulli medical at Man City

Marseille goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli is due to undergo a medical at Manchester City on Monday after the clubs agreed a £1.75m deal.

Rulli, who is set to sign a two-year deal at the Etihad, joins as a replacement for James Trafford, who completed a club-record move to Leeds for £45m.

Rulli has been identified by City as the man to provide backup to Gianluigi Donnarumma next season.

Atletico's Ruggeri to join Villa for £16m

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri has agreed to join Aston Villa. The 24-year-old Italian will cost £16m plus add-ons.

His transfer will help pave the way for Atletico to bid for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

The Argentine centre-back is also among names being considered by Barcelona but Atletico coach Diego Simeone hopes to convince his compatriot if they can agree on terms.

Matteo Ruggeri's move should pave the way for Cristian Romero to join Atletico Madrid

Facundo Buonanotte leaves Brighton for Elche

Brighton midfielder Facundo Buonanotte has joined La Liga side Elche on a season-long loan.

The 21-year-old was on loan at two different Premier League clubs last season, spending the first half with Chelsea before joining Leeds in the second half of the campaign.

Sheffield Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is wanted on loan by Sheffield Wednesday.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff City and they are keen to take him back too.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and is attracting a number of enquiries but League One Wednesday, who play Bolton in the Carabao Cup today, are making a concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca will choose Man City captain himself and drops a hint about his preferred leadership style ahead of Atletico Madrid friendly
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca will choose his own Manchester City captain rather than put the decision to a team election and wants to inject some English influence into his leadership group.

City usually took votes among the squad to determine the captains under predecessor Pep Guardiola – but the Catalan changed that practice in his final year after a disastrous season with Kyle Walker leading the team.

Ruben Dias is the favourite to take the armband, linking back up with the squad last week following a post-World Cup break.

Maresca has Dias and Erling Haaland as certainties to retaining their positions of authority from last season but needs a new leader after Bernardo Silva sealed a free transfer to Real Madrid.

Dias was second in command, with Haaland fourth. Rodri was third but hopes to push through a move to Barcelona, with City having rejected an opening bid of nearly £40million for the midfielder.

Maresca would need two additional captains to step up if Rodri does depart, with Josko Gvardiol and Phil Foden already publicly putting their hands up for greater responsibility.

New Man City boss Enzo Maresca says he wants an English leadership group this season

Foden and Dias have captained City during their first two pre-season friendlies in Asia, with January signing Marc Guehi having led Crystal Palace before joining for £20m.

‘There is no pressure (on me), just a privilege,’ Maresca said ahead of Sunday’s friendly against Atletico Madrid.

‘In terms of expectations, this is a club that needs to win titles. We’re going to try to do exactly that.’

Sports.title: Arsenal sign Bruno Guimaraes: Gunners complete £75m deal for Brazilian midfielder as ANOTHER Newcastle star leaves St James' Park
Sports.content:
Arsenal have completed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle.

The Brazilian becomes their fourth arrival of the transfer window after they made Piero Hincapie's loan permanent and signed Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier.

Guimaraes has signed a four-year deal with the option of a further 12 months.

Guimaraes said: 'I feel good, I feel amazing. I'm glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta), I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

'Well I think, after playing two World Cups, I think I'm at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I'm in the right place to do it. I'm so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season, so the squad is going to be very, very important and I'm hopeful we can achieve our dreams.

'Big Gabi (Gabriel) was very excited. Every time he sent me the message, "We’ll wait for you, when will you come?" I'm so excited to join them, not only the Brazilians, we have an amazing squad here.

'(Declan) Rice sent me a message: "Come here and please no more fights, now we're friends". I was happy he messaged me, but the midfield we have here, in my point of view, is one of the best in Europe. Everyone is an amazing player, I'm so excited to start chatting and play, and know the players very, very well, but we have an amazing midfield.'

Arsenal have completed the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United

Mikel Arteta hugs his new arrival after the Premier League champions bolster their midfield

Sporting director Andrea Berta said: 'We are delighted to welcome Bruno Guimaraes to our club.

'Bruno is a player with a great mentality and great quality, who will bring strong leadership to our squad.

'With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team. As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.

'Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.'

His arrival at the Emirates takes their summer spend to around £145m as they look to build on last season's Premier League title and Champions League final.

But the move is another complication for Newcastle, who had already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this window before Eddie Howe stepped down as manager.

Guimaraes has been an important player for the Magpies ever since joining for £40m in 2022.

But the 28-year-old told them in July that he wants to join Arsenal.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on June 25 that the Magpies were braced for an offer from the Gunners after leading agents were instructed to explore the Brazilian's options.

The World Cup star had two years remaining on his contract at St James' Park, plus the option of an extra year, hence Newcastle were able to command a strong fee.

Mikel Arteta has been keen to strengthen his central midfield options despite already having Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Fabio Vieira.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes reveals private Declan Rice message after sealing Arsenal transfer
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes reveals private Declan Rice message after sealing Arsenal transfer

Arsenal have announced the £75million arrival of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, with the Brazilian midfielder going from opponent to team-mate of Declan Rice this summer

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes is now a team-mate of Declan Rice (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Declan Rice is more than happy to bury the hatchet with Bruno Guimaraes following his arrival at Arsenal, the Brazilian has revealed. Guimaraes was officially announced as a Gunner on Saturday after his £75million transfer from Newcastle.

‌



The 28-year-old has taken the No.39 shirt after signing a five-year contract. He is the third high-profile player to leave Newcastle this summer, following Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, after making it clear he only had eyes for Arsenal.

‌



He has become the defending Premier League champions' second-most expensive player of all time, behind only Rice, who arrived for £105m from West Ham in July 2023.

‌



Guimaraes is already well acquainted with Rice, having come up against the England star on the pitch on many occasions. And their fiery confrontation during Newcastle's 1-0 win over Arsenal at St James' Park in November 2023 has already come up between them.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gabriel Jesus' agent addresses Arsenal transfer exit after being spotted at rival club READ MORE :

Speaking to the club website, Guimaraes revealed: “Rice sent me a message: ‘Come here and please no more fights, now we’re friends!’ I was happy he messaged me."

‌



Guimaraes could play alongside Rice in Mikel Arteta's midfield, with the likes of Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Odegaard and Eberechi Eze also competing for places. “In my point of view, [the Arsenal midfield] is one of the best in Europe. Everyone is an amazing player," Guimaraes added.

“Every time when I play against [Arsenal] it was very tough. They keep the ball, they defend like one. I think that combination is the way I like to play as well, and of course, joining the winners of the league is always a big opportunity.”

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes and Declan Rice clashed back in November 2023 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Asked what he will bring to the table, he said: “I can pass the ball, run a lot and play like a warrior, I'll never give up. I will try to help the team, [I’m] good with the ball, composed, very calm, and sometimes I can score some goals and hope to make everyone very, very happy here.”

Rice isn't the only Arsenal player Guimaraes spoke to before making the move to north London, with fellow Brazilian midfielder Gilberto Silva another to reach out.

“Of course, Gilberto Silva. I love him as a player,” he said. “I had the opportunity before to talk to Gilberto Silva. I hope I can follow his history here and make myself one of the very good players at Arsenal in history.”

‌



Guimaraes spent four and a half seasons with Newcastle, where he helped win the Carabao Cup and become club captain. He says it was a difficult decision to leave behind the Magpies, but the right one for his career.

“I'm very excited,” he said. “I’m at the point of my life where I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I'm in the right place to do it. I'm so excited to start.”

Sports.title: Man Utd handed Lewis Hall update as Newcastle make training camp decision
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed Lewis Hall update as Newcastle make training camp decision

Newcastle United have a decision on Lewis Hall's pre-season involvement amid ongoing Man Utd transfer speculation

View 2 Images Manchester United have been linked with a summer transfer swoop for Lewis Hall. (Image: (Photo by Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

Newcastle United left-back Lewis Hall has been sent home from their warm-weather pre-season training camp in La Manga nursing a minor injury. The 21-year-old, who is a transfer target for Manchester United this summer, has returned to Tyneside, with the rest of his teammates set to take on Valencia this evening.

‌



The Magpies having already knocked back an initial approach from Michael Carrick's side and remain resolute that Hall will not be offloaded this summer. Newcastle have already lost Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon during the current window.

‌



Eddie Howe's exit from the club has only fuelled further conjecture surrounding Hall's future, though the club have stressed Hall won't be sold.

‌



The left-back is a key part of both the club and Matthias Jaissle's plans for this season, as the new German head coach plans his St. James' Park rebuild.

Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Chronicle Live reports that Hall and fellow defender Fabian Schar have been granted time away following the warm-weather camp in La Manga to recuperate from their respective injuries.

‌



The England international has been carrying out a separate training programme from his Newcastle teammates in Spain, concentrating on upper-body work.

Hall will play no part for new head coach Jaissle in his first match at the helm against Valencia this evening.

View 2 Images Man Utd are interested in signing Lewis Hall this summer. (Image: Iain Buist/Newcastle Chronicle)

‌



Man United are believed to be eager to bring in a new full-back this summer, with Carrick holding Hall in high regard.

Recent reports suggest the defender would welcome a move to Old Trafford if a fee could be agreed, though Newcastle have taken a firm stance following a turbulent summer of departures.

The Reds have also been connected with a potential swoop for Racing Santander defender Jorge Salinas.

‌



Nevertheless, the La Liga outfit have made it plain the 19 year old will only be offloaded if his £13.7million release clause is triggered.

Barcelona have also been associated with a move for the defender, having had an offer turned down earlier this summer.

Luke Shaw remains United's first-choice at left-back, with Carrick choosing to deploy Patrick Dorgu in a more attacking role and the club are eager to bolster that area of the defence.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
