World.title: Lionel Messi’s father Jorge dies aged 68
World.content:
Jorge Messi, the father and agent of Lionel Messi, has died aged 68, the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner’s childhood club Newell’s Old Boys announced on Saturday.

Argentinian media reported Jorge Messi had passed away on Friday in a hospital in Rosario.

“His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel,” Newell’s Old Boys said in a social media post.

Jorge Messi was his son’s first coach in Argentina and his sole companion when he first moved to Barcelona as a child, before later becoming his agent.

“My father helped me enormously. He is very critical of me. That made me always want to push myself further,” Lionel Messi told DirecTV Sports in 2022.

Messi’s family asked the media for “humanity” during the recent World Cup amid persistent rumours over Jorge’s health.

AFP

World.title: Hamas says still ready to go ahead with Gaza plan
World.content:
EDITORS NOTE: Graphic content / Mourners carry the body of 17-year-old Fadi al-Naasan during his funeral in the village of Al-Mughayyir, east of Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on July 18, 2026, after he died from wounds sustained about a week ago during clashes with Israeli forces. The occupied West Bank has been gripped by almost daily violence involving Israeli troops and settlers since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023. (Photo by JAAFAR ASHTIYEH / AFP)

Hamas said on Saturday it remained ready to proceed with a US-backed Gaza peace plan and urged pressure on Israel, which insists it did not agree to the latest part of the deal.

Hamas informed US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace that it stood by the latest stage of the plan, under which the militants would hand over weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing committee in the war-battered territory.

“Hamas and other factions have confirmed to mediators their readiness to begin implementing the agreement and move to the second phase, provided it receives Israeli approval and that Israel begins implementing the agreement,” a Hamas official told AFP.

“Hamas is urging the US administration to exert pressure on Israel to compel it to abide by the agreement and move to the second phase,” the official said on condition of anonymity.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces a tough reelection fight in October and wide opposition from his right-wing base to the Gaza deal, said on Tuesday that Israel had not agreed to the “draft” presented by the Board of Peace.

Trump last week had hailed as a breakthrough that Hamas had agreed to disarmament under the plan, with the Board of Peace saying Israel would in tandem carry out a phased withdrawal from much of Gaza.

Netanyahu met Monday with the Board of Peace’s high representative for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, who backtracked and said Israel would withdraw only after a full disarmament by Hamas.

Israel’s military also vowed to keep hitting Hamas, which carried out the deadliest attack ever against Israel on October 7, 2023.

But Israeli operations in Gaza, while ongoing, appear to have decreased in intensity in recent days. On Saturday, the Nasser hospital in Khan Yunis reported three people injured by Israeli army gunfire.

Israeli operations in Gaza have killed 1,257 Palestinians since October last year, when the two sides agreed to a ceasefire backed by Trump, according to the territory’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

The Israeli army has reported five deaths in its ranks during the same period.

AFP

World.title: Forensics cleared officers of Ibadan Poly graduate shooting – Police
World.content:
Nurudeen Azeez before (right) and after (left) the incident.

Oyo State Police Command has said that forensic evidence cleared its officers, Inspector Gbenga Ayodele and Sergeant Ayilaran Boluwaji, in the 2021 shooting of Nurudeen Azeez, an Ibadan Polytechnic graduate.

Both officers, attached to the Agodi Divisional Police Headquarters, had responded to a robbery alert.

In a statement on Saturday by the Command’s spokesman, DSP Ayanlade Olayinka, the Police stressed that an investigation concluded in 2021 exonerated the officers.

“Following its recent resurfacing in a viral video and newspaper publication, the Command considers it necessary to restate the findings of the investigation,” the statement noted.

The victim

The graduate of The Polytechnic, Ibadan, Azeez, aged 30, told newsmen recently that he is still battling the devastating effects of being shot five years after the incident.

Azeez, a native of Ibadan, said on August 16, 2021, he was hit by a bullet while riding on a commercial motorcycle from Iwo Road to his hostel in the Ijokodo area of the city.

He said there was traffic around Idi-Ape, which made the okadaman to take an alternative route.

“As soon as the motorcycle moved, I suddenly heard gunshots. A bullet struck my spinal cord, and I immediately collapsed on the motorcycle.

“A police officer came to where I had fallen and asked me to stand up. But I could not move. In the confusion, some passers-by who heard the gunshots rushed to the scene, and the officers fled,” he said.

Azeez said he was assured of assistance with his medical treatment, but that the support gradually diminished.

Police deny shooting

The Police statement denying involvement of its officers noted that “In the course of forensic sweep of the scene, a locally fabricated pistol was recovered.”

It added that during treatment, “15 pellets were removed. 13 were documented, while six were registered as exhibits.”

The two officers’ duty and firearm records were obtained during the investigation.

The statement read, “The records confirmed that they had signed out two AK-47 rifles for their assignment that night.

“The forensic examination established that neither AK-47 rifle had been fired in connection with the incident.

“In addition, the pellets extracted from the victim were not consistent with AK-47 ammunition.

“Unlike the two police-issued rifles, the pistol showed characteristics consistent with recent discharge. However, this finding alone could not establish who fired the weapon.

“Based on the totality of the evidence, the investigation concluded that the allegation that either of the two police officers shot Nurudeen Azeez was not substantiated.

“While the victim sustained a genuine gunshot injury, the evidence available did not establish the identity of the person responsible for the shooting.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Atletico Madrid won’t sell Alvarez – Simeone
World.content:
Atletico Madrid’s Argentine coach Diego Simeone attends a training session on the pitch at the Emirates Stadium in London on May 4, 2026, on the eve of their UEFA Champions League league semifinal, second-leg football match against Arsenal. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP)

Atletico Madrid will not allow forward Julian Alvarez to leave the club during the current transfer window despite interest from Barcelona, coach Diego Simeone said Saturday.

Last month, Atletico filed a complaint to FIFA over Barcelona allegedly tapping up Alvarez.

The Argentina international has also been linked with a possible move to Premier League champions Arsenal and was the subject of a rejected 150-million-euro ($173.4m) bid from Real Madrid in June.

“I think the situation is very clear. The club has made a decision that (CEO) Miguel Angel (Gil Marin) has explained very well,” Simeone told reporters ahead of a pre-season friendly against Manchester City in Seoul.

“From a sporting perspective, we’re very happy to have a footballer like Julian…

“We will help him continue to grow, continue to improve and continue delivering the best — which has been a tremendous amount — that he has given us over the last two years.”

Alvarez is due to rejoin the Atletico squad in two days’ time after taking a break following Argentina’s World Cup final loss to Spain.

While on World Cup duty, the 26-year-old said he “believed a transfer is best for everyone”, but did not confirm his preferred destination.

Alvarez has scored 49 goals for Atletico since signing from Manchester City two years ago.

“We don’t want to transfer him. We didn’t accept the 100-million-euro offer, nor will we accept one for 150 million or 200 million,” Gil Marin told the club’s in-house media channel.

“I have no doubt that Atletico is the right place for Julian and that Julian is the centre-forward for Atletico Madrid. We want to keep him.”

When asked about how Alvarez might be received by Atletico fans following the transfer speculation, Simeone pointed to Antoine Griezmann.

The Frenchman made a big-money move to Barcelona before returning to Atletico.

He was initially met with some hostility, but won the supporters back over and departed last season a club legend.

“We went through a period with Antoine in recent years where he had to leave, come back, and prove his quality and stature on the pitch,” said Simeone.

“I see no other path than focusing on the sporting side of things, doing our part and helping him (Alvarez), just as we have done over the last few years.”

Atletico get their La Liga campaign under way on August 19 with a home match against newly-promoted Malaga.

The capital club finished fourth last season, 25 points adrift of champions Barcelona.

AFP

World.title: ‘I want to make history,’ says Guimaraes after £75m Arsenal move
World.content:
Bruno Guimaraes said he wanted to “make history” at Arsenal after joining the Premier League champions from top-flight rivals Newcastle for a reported fee of £75 million ($101.2 million) on Saturday.

The Brazil midfielder spent four-and-a-half seasons with Newcastle and became captain of the Magpies.

Arsenal, who ended a 22-year wait for a top-flight English league title last season, did not disclose the exact length of Guimaraes’s “long-term” deal.

But British media reports said he had signed a four-year contract with a further one-year option.

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I’m glad for the opportunity,” Guimaraes told Arsenal’s media channels.

“We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I’m hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

The 28-year-old said he’d been enthused about joining Arsenal right from his initial contacts with sporting director Andrea Berta and manager Mikel Arteta.

“Since the first time I spoke to Berta and Mikel I was excited,” said Guimaraes. “I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I’m at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this.

“I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I’m in the right place to do it. I’m so excited to start.”

– ‘Strengthening the heart of our team’ –

Guimaraes is Arsenal’s most high-profile signing of the transfer window so far, joining fellow new arrivals Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis.

“With Bruno joining us, we are further strengthening the heart of our team,” said Berta.

“As we have all seen, Bruno can play as a defensive midfielder and as a box-to-box player. He combines quality with quantity, and has provided goals and assists for his team every year.

“Bruno will allow Mikel to further develop our playing style and will also increase our internal competitiveness, which is essential for maintaining the standards required when we are aiming to win major trophies.”

Guimaraes was also linked with Arsenal in January 2022, when he ended up leaving Lyon for Newcastle. But he has now joined the Gunners after scoring 31 goals in 195 appearances for the Magpies.

Under coach Eddie Howe, Guimaraes helped Newcastle end a 56-year major trophy drought when they won the 2025 League Cup and was also involved as they twice qualified for the Champions League.

Guimaraes is the third high-profile player to leave the northeast club ahead of the new season following the exits of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali.

“This is one of the toughest decisions of my life. When I arrived, the club was in a challenging position and I am incredibly proud of what we achieved together,” Guimaraes said in Newcastle’s statement.

“I fell in love with this place. I really mean that.”

Howe stepped down as Newcastle manager last week and has since been replaced by German Matthias Jaissle.

Guimaraes, who played for Brazil at the recent World Cup, will compete for a place in Arsenal’s midfield with Declan Rice, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino.

Arsenal kick off their season against Manchester City in the Community Shield next Sunday, before starting their title defence against newly-promoted Coventry five days later.

Newcastle get their campaign under way against Liverpool at St James’ Park on August 23.

AFP

World.title: NNPC welcomes public scrutiny, defends Ojulari’s performance
World.content:
Ojulari

By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has welcomed public scrutiny of its operations while defending the performance of its Group Chief Executive Officer, Engr. Bayo Ojulari, with the company citing increases in crude oil and gas production under his leadership.

NNPC said the clarification followed recent media reports attributed to the Oil and Gas Professionals Forum (OGPF), which questioned the performance of the company’s leadership in connection with the recently concluded oil licensing round conducted by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC).

In a statement issued on Saturday, the company’s Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, said NNPC remained committed to transparency and accountability and would continue to engage openly on its performance and operations.

Odeh, however, said it was necessary to clarify the company’s role in the licensing round, stressing that NNPC had no regulatory or allocative authority over the process.

According to him, the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 places the conduct of oil licensing rounds and allocation of oil blocks within the statutory mandate of the NUPRC.

“NNPC Limited, since its incorporation, has operated strictly as a commercial entity and holds no regulatory or allocative authority,” he said.

On production, NNPC said publicly available data showed a sustained improvement in crude oil output since April 2025.

The company said average crude oil production stood at 1.60 million barrels per day (mbpd), inclusive of condensate, in April 2025, before rising through the second half of the year and stabilising at 1.67mbpd by April 2026.

It said the increase of about 80,000 barrels per day represented a six per cent growth in output.

“These figures are documented in NNPC Limited’s Monthly Performance Report, which is available to the public,” Odeh said.

The company also reported growth in gas production during the period, saying output rose from an average of 7,354 million standard cubic feet per day (mmscfd) in April 2025 to 7,729mmscfd by April 2026.

NNPC said the 375mmscfd increase represented five per cent growth and was an indication of expanding gas output in support of domestic energy security and Nigeria’s export commitments.

The company said the production figures were also contained in its publicly available Monthly Performance Report.

NNPC said it remained open to scrutiny but warned that it would take necessary steps to protect its reputation and that of its leadership against what it described as false or unsubstantiated claims.

“We encourage industry commentators, analysts, and professional associations to verify information through the appropriate regulatory and corporate channels before publication,” Odeh said.

He added that greater reliance on verified information would ensure that public commentary remained factual, balanced and constructive to informed debate on Nigeria’s energy sector.

World.title: Our mother didn’t want Jude to manage P-Square – Henry, eldest brother
World.content:
Henry Okoye (Photo: YouTube|Nollyserve)

Henry Okoye, one of the brothers of the defunct music duo, P-Square, has said that their late mother Josephine Okoye, did not want Jude Okoye to manage the musicians.

In an interview with social commentator Jos Connection at the Okoye family residence in Plateau State on Friday, Henry said he was P-Square’s sponsor when the duo – Peter and Paul – did not find anyone to sponsor their music and that Jude was not involved at the time.

“When they started music, they were looking for sponsors. They didn’t see any. When I started sponsoring them, Jude was not there. When Benson & Hedges came to Jos looking for artistes, it was me that took them to the stadium for a performance; they came first. Jude was not there. We were travelling from state to state for music, sometimes they used my car (to distribute) flyers.

“We just took it as a family thing but we knew that it’s Peter and Paul that own it. We’re only supporting them. Sometimes we travelled to Abuja; my sister, the one we call Lilian, was the one who collected gate fee. As the elder brother I was the bodyguard.

“They started making money bit by bit. Jude came in and said he wanted to manage them. We allowed Jude, my mum disagreed,” he said.

Mrs Okoye died on July 11, 2012, in India following heart surgery.

Speaking further, Henry said Paul’s change in behaviour surprised him and added that he (Paul) used to be “the nicest person in the family”.

“They promised me 20 per cent when they start making money. Jude intervened and dismissed that. I challenged him that he wasn’t there when we started everything but now chasing everybody away from them,” Henry said.

He added that he would be happy if the brothers reunited but expressed doubts that such a reconciliation would happen.

“I will be happy for them to come back together but I don’t think it will happen. Paul was a very kind person,” he added.

Henry urged Jude to help restore the family to its former state by settling the disagreements among the siblings.

Henry, who is older than Jude, said their eldest brother Christopher does not want to be involved in the dispute as he is “born again”.

Peter and Paul effectively split in 2017. However, in 2021, they reunited but fell out again in 2024.

The rift resulted in the arraignment of Jude in 2025 by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission over allegations of fraud to the tune of N1.38bn, $1m and £34,537.59. He pleaded not guilty to the charges.

The case is still in court.

World.title: ‘He has no electoral value’ – Wike mocks Bode George
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA

Federal Capital Territory FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, has said he has no regret over stopping Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, former Deputy National Chairman, Chief Bode George, from becoming the party’s National Chairman, describing him as a failed politician who has not won any election for the PDP in Lagos State since 1999.

Read Also: Osun 2026: Strengths and weaknesses of Adeleke, Oyebamiji, Salaam as voters head to polls

In a statement on Saturday by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, the minister said Chief George’s political frustration has further been compounded by the emergence of Deji Doherty, a personality he does not want to see in charge of the party in Lagos State.

“His anger is because we didn’t allow him to be PDP National Chairman and no regret doing so,” Wike said.

He added that George “wanted to be PDP National Chairman, and was carrying on like the position was his birthright. We stopped him because it was the turn of the South-South. Since then, he has not stopped being angry.”

The minister recounted an incident in which he visited George’s residence in Maitama, Abuja, as a sitting governor, to appease him after the national convention. But was nearly turned away by George’s wife until former Ondo State governor, Olusegun Mimiko, intervened.

Wike described George as a politician who, despite all the privileges and power at his disposal, has failed to deliver electoral victories for the PDP in Lagos State.

“We have managed him even though we know that he has no value. But as it is, since he wants to keep dancing naked in the market place of politics, we can’t but allow him,” he said.

The minister argued that leadership of a political party is not determined by name, title or status as a founding father, but by the ability to win elections. He said on that score, Bode George is “a complete disaster.”

Citing specific electoral figures, Wike said George has never won even his own polling unit, Unit 001 in Ward E2, Evans Street, Lagos Island, for the PDP.

He noted that in the 2019 presidential election, the All Progressives Congress, APC, polled 84 votes at the unit against the PDP’s 40, while in 2023, after George transferred his voter’s card to Eti-Osa, the PDP recorded only four votes at his former polling unit.

Wike said that since Bode George appeared not to be busy, he would continue to make his associates busy by giving them reason to move from one television station to another.

Vanguard News

World.title: Idris Deserves Second Term, Says Zuru, Urges Voters To Support Gov For Continuity
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent

The Special Adviser to the Kebbi State Governor on Media Strategy and Communication, Abdullahi Zuru, has declared that Governor Nasir Idris has performed credibly well and deserves to be re-elected for a second term in 2027.

Zuru made the declaration yesterday while responding to questions from journalists who paid him a courtesy visit. He said the assessment was based on the governor’s record of delivery across key sectors since assuming office in 2023.

“Since the creation of Kebbi State, we have never had it this good,” Zuru said. “The governor has touched every sector and the impact is visible to the people.”

According to him, the Idris administration has prioritised the economy, infrastructural development, education, health, workers’ welfare, and human capital development. He noted that the interventions were designed to directly improve the lives of ordinary citizens.

On infrastructure, the media aide said the government has embarked on road projects, urban renewal, and rural development programmes aimed at opening up communities and boosting commerce across the 21 local government areas of the state.

“In education and health, we have seen massive investments in schools, primary healthcare centres, and the welfare of teachers and health workers,” he added. “Workers’ salaries are paid as and when due, and their welfare is receiving serious attention.”

Zuru further stated that the governor’s approach to governance has restored public confidence in government. He said the administration runs an open-door policy that allows citizens to feel the presence of government at all levels.

Calling on voters in the state, he urged them to rally behind the governor ahead of the next election. “I encourage the good people of Kebbi State to support Governor Nasir Idris and ensure he returns for a second term so that the good work can continue,” he said.

The Special Adviser also took a swipe at some politicians in the state, saying they lacked the pedigree to challenge the governor’s record.

“Some of them have held positions at state and federal levels before, yet they have no track record to show for it,” Zuru stated. “Leadership is about results, and the results are there for everyone to see.”

He noted that with the current momentum, Kebbi is on the path of sustainable development, and continuity under Governor Idris remains the best option for the people of the state.

World.title: Abia Leadership Academy, Strategic Institution For Training Future Leaders, Says Gov
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, says the Abia State Leadership Academy was established as a strategic institution where ethics, values, and practical leadership skills would be instilled in Abia youths.

He said the essence was to catch them young, adding “we are committed to getting it right with the younger generation. Otherwise, our wider development efforts will be in jeopardy.”

Governor Otti, represented by his Deputy, Engr. Ikechukwu Emetu, spoke while declaring open the 2026 Youth Leadership Bootcamp of the Abia State Leadership Academy. The batch has 1, 000 participants selected from 7, 000 applicants. The training holds every long vacation at Government College, Umuahia, since the Otti administration came to power.

The governor reaffirmed his commitment to developing young Abians as future leaders of the state and nation and charged the participants to learn with humility and participate actively in the programme.

“This year’s programme is particularly significant, with 1,000 participants selected from more than 7,000 applicants. That response tells us our young people are hungry for genuine transformation—and they trust this administration to deliver it.

“For 2026, we’ve partnered with the Enterprise Development Centre of Pan-Atlantic University—a global-standard institution with ties to the World Bank, Goldman Sachs, and MasterCard.

“To our young participants, your selection is only the beginning. I urge you to learn with humility, participate actively, build meaningful relationships and, most importantly, use what you learn to positively influence your schools, communities and State,” the Governor said.

Earlier, the facilitator of the programme and Chairman of Abia State Civil Service Commission, Pastor Mrs. Eno Jerry –Eze, represented by Rev. Mrs. Ifeoma Agu, said that the programme was an opportunity to for the youths to imbibe the ideals of civic responsibility and urged the participants to be determined to use the lessons of the bootcamp to better their lives as well as bring about the change they crave for.

Mrs. Jerry-Eze thanked the governor for placing the youths in the leadership map in Nigeria and for leaving a legacy that assures that the leadership he has introduced would be sustained.

Delivering a lecture on the theme of the training: ‘The Demands of Stewardship’, the Chief of Staff to the Governor, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, noted that the governor was investing in the lives of the teenagers and young leaders of the state through the academy.

Pastor Ajagba, while describing the initiative as a strategic investment in the future of the state and a lasting legacy that will shape the character, mindset and leadership capacity of generations yet unborn, disclosed that by intentionally preparing young people for responsible leadership, Governor Otti was laying a firm foundation for sustainable development and ensuring that the ideals of integrity, innovation and public service remain deeply rooted in Abia’s future.

He added that it was an honour for all those invited to share their perspectives in the noble vision of raising a generation of principled, disciplined and transformational leaders through the academy and applauded the exemplary life of vision, focus, sacrifice, discipline, competence, integrity of Governor Otti and assuring of the unwavering commitment of the Governor to good governance and purposeful leadership.

Also speaking on behalf of the Executive Director of the development partner – the Enterprise Development Centre (EDC), Pan-Athlantic University, Dr. Uche Egbuna, said the future of every society depends on the quality of leaders it intentionally develops, adding that leadership was about responsibility, integrity and service.

Dr. Egbuna stated that the boot camp was built on four key pillars: leadership and service, enterprise, impact and innovation, and encouraged participants to strive for meaningful impact by becoming problem-solvers and change-makers.

He described the partnership with the Abia State Leadership Academy as a shared commitment to developing ethical leaders, resilient entrepreneurs and innovative young people who will contribute to economic growth and social transformation.

President of Abia State Leadership Academy, Prof. Kenneth Kalu, disclosed that 7052 persons applied for the programme and about 1000 were qualified after the rigorous processes of selection.

Prof. Kalu enjoined the participants to remember that they were expected “to think, reflect and become” future leaders, emphasising that what was more important was not that they participated in the programme but what they become from the programme.

Responding on behalf of the participants, Chukwuemerie Obiorah and Treasure Ogbonna thanked the governor for the opportunity given them to become transformational leaders, assuring that they would not disappoint but make good use of the bootcamp to better citizens in the society.

The opening ceremony of the bootcamp being coordinated by the Programme Manager, Abia State Leadership Academy and Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Public Communication, Mr. Dodoh Okafor, was graced by Secretary to the State Government, Dr. Emmanuel Meribeole; Commissioner for Tertiary Education, Prof. Uche Emeh Uche; Principal Secretary and Chief Strategist Officer of the state, Mr. Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, among other government officials.

World.title: Just In: DSS Arrests Three More Suspects Over Kidnap of Nasarawa Varsity Professor
World.content:
Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) have arrested three more suspects linked to the kidnapping of the Dean of Agriculture at Nasarawa State University, Professor Samuel Avengbe Okunsebor.

The suspects were arrested on Friday night at a local brothel along the Mararraban Akunza axis of the Lafia–Makurdi highway.

A security source disclosed that the three suspects were members of the kidnapping gang responsible for the abduction of the university don.

Professor Okunsebor was kidnapped by gunmen in the early hours of Wednesday, July 15, 2026, at Mile Uku, a border community between Lafia and Nasarawa-Eggon Local Government Areas of Nasarawa State.

He was rescued two days later by DSS operatives. Two suspects, including a woman, were also arrested in connection with the incident at the time.

According to a security source, the newly arrested suspects were identified as 25-year-old Yakubu Abubakar, also known as Black or Starboy, a member of the Doemak tribe in Plateau State; 37-year-old Usman Abubakar Mairiga; and 27-year-old Sale Babauro Abubakar.

The source said Mairiga is Hausa, while Sale Babauro Abubakar is Fulani.

The three suspects are currently being held at the DSS State Command for further investigation.

The source added that their continued detention followed a warrant obtained from a magistrate’s court.

The latest arrests bring to five the number of suspects reportedly apprehended in connection with the kidnapping of Professor Okunsebor. Investigations into the incident are ongoing.

World.title: Bianca, Great Asset To Humanity, Says Gov Otti
World.content:
Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, has said that Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, is a huge asset not only to the Igbo nation but also to Nigeria, and humanity.

This was contained in a birthday message the governor sent to Nigerian former Ambassador to Spain, where he also enjoined her to continue to uphold the virtues and character that have distinguished her and made her an admirable amazon.

The governor’s birthday felicitations to the minister was endorsed by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma. The former Beauty Queen celebrated her birthday on August 5, 2026.

Governor Otti described Ambassador Ojukwu as an amazon who has distinguished herself in many facets of human endeavour, noting she deserves to be celebrated.

He recalled that the minister supported the struggle for Abia’s redemption, starting from when he first ran for governor on the platform of All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), adding that she is “an honest, just, and courageous Nigerian who has represented womanhood diligently and positively.”

“On a day like this, I feel excited to celebrate my sister and friend, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, on the occasion of her birthday. She is a woman of strong will and courage. An amazon from the East who has distinguished herself in many facets and continues to prove that, with courage and character, nothing is too big for any human being to accomplish,” the governor stated.

He noted that her appointment as Nigeria’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, “her commitment and accomplishments were already outstanding and commendable.”

The governor assured Ambassador Ojukwu that he would continue to support and stand by her at all times as she strives courageously to write more success stories in her eventful life and wished her a happy birthday, while praying that she would live long in good health to celebrate many more beautiful years ahead.

World.title: Adeleke Commends Monarch Residents  On Osun-Osogbo Festival
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

The world-famous Osun-Osogbo Festival was held yesterday with more than 500,000 participants from all over the world.

Osun-Osogbo Festival is celebrated in August every year at the Grove. The festival attracts thousands of Osun worshippers, spectators and tourists from across the globe.

The Osun-Osogbo Festival is a two-week celebration of culture, spirituality, and heritage held annually in Osogbo, South West Nigeria.

Speaking on this year festival, Osun State Governor, Senator Ademola Adeleke, commended Oba Jimoh Olanipekun Oyetunji, Larooye II, Ataoja of Osogbo, and all sons and daughters of Osogbo at home and in the diaspora on the celebration of the Osun-Osogbo Festival.

The governor described the annual festival as a priceless cultural and spiritual heritage that reflects the enduring bond between the people of Osogbo and the sacred River Osun, celebrating centuries of history and faith.

He noted that the festival remains one of Africa’s foremost traditional festivals and a proud symbol of Yoruba civilisation.

The governor stated that the sacred procession led by the Arugba, the royal presence of the Ataoja, the traditional rites at the Osun Sacred Grove, the prayers, chants, and cultural displays all represent our culture and preserved heritage across generations while projecting Osun State to the global stage.

Adeleke commended the monarch, Ataoja of Osogbo, the Osun Priestess (Iya Osun), the Arugba, traditional institutions, devotees, cultural custodians, and the entire people of Osogbo for sustaining a festival that has continued to attract visitors, researchers, and tourists from across the world.

“On behalf of the Government and the good people of Osun State, I heartily felicitate with Kabiyesi, His Imperial Majesty, Oba Jimoh Olanipekun Oyetunji, Larooye II, Ataoja of Osogbo, and the entire people of Osogbo on this year’s Osun-Osogbo Festival.

“As we celebrate this sacred tradition, may the blessings of Osun continue to bring peace, prosperity, and progress to our dear state.”

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to preserving Osun’s rich cultural heritage and protecting the Osun Sacred Grove as a globally treasured heritage site.

He added that the administration will continue to support initiatives that promote tourism, cultural diplomacy, and economic opportunities for the people accordingly.

World.title: Opata Defends Tinubu’s ‘All Is Fair in Politics’ Remark
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

A Professor of African Literature at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), Prof. Damian Opata, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s recent remark that “all is fair in politics,” arguing that the expression is neither new nor peculiar to Nigeria’s political history.

He urged Nigerians to consider the remarks within their historical and philosophical context.

Opata, who is also the National Chairman of the South East Movement for Tinubu 2027, said the expression derives from the popular saying, “All is fair in love and war,” which he traced to John Lyly’s Euphues: The Anatomy of Wit.

According to a statement issued on Thursday, he said he had no objection to the memorandum presented by the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria and read by its President, Bishop Matthew Ndagoso.

He said the bishops demanded free and fair elections, improved security and good governance for the common good, while also requesting the return of schools to their original proprietors and the extension of constitutional guarantees of freedom of religion. He noted that President Tinubu responded by highlighting improvements in the education and security sectors, explaining that the issue of returning schools rested with state governors and reaffirming that freedom of religion is guaranteed by the Constitution.

He added that the bishops applauded the President’s response by clapping at four achievements of his administration.

Opata said President Tinubu’s assertion that “all is fair in politics” reflected “his brutal courage in speaking and acting on truth and reality,” although he acknowledged that critics were justified in arguing that, as President, such an expression could send the wrong signal because he embodies the nation’s conscience and ethical standards.

He further argued that the bishops’ address should not have focused solely on the President and the All Progressives Congress, maintaining that all political parties share responsibility for ensuring free and fair elections.

According to him, the President’s remark is reducible to the Machiavellian principle that “the end justifies the means,” a doctrine rooted in political pragmatism that has found expression in institutions such as universities, churches, the police, the civil service and the business sector.

Commenting on reactions that followed the meeting, including an interview granted by Cardinal John Onaiyekan, Opata urged the media and the public to exercise restraint, saying attention should remain on the substantive issues rather than peripheral matters.

He concluded by calling on the ruling party, opposition parties and Nigerians to avoid conduct that reflects either “the end justifies the means” or “all is fair in politics” as the country prepares for the 2027 general election, expressing the hope that doing so would help guarantee free and fair polls.

World.title: EU, PLAC Charge Nigerian Youths to Demand Transparency, Accountability
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The European Union Delegation to Nigeria and the Policy and Legal Advocacy Centre (PLAC) have asked Nigerian youths to demand transparency and accountability from public institutions.

Speaking at a Model Legislative Assembly Session in Abuja, Programme Manager for Democracy, Rule of Law and Gender at the EU Delegation, Laolu Olawumi, said Nigeria’s democracy can only deepen when young people insist on accountable governance at all levels.

“This internship is not just about producing future politicians. It is about forming citizens who understand governance and how to engage it,” she said.

Olawumi told participants that democracy goes beyond elections to include lawmaking, oversight, citizen participation, and consensus building in a diverse country like Nigeria.

She urged them to use the knowledge gained to explain governance processes to their communities.

“You are now ambassadors of Nigeria and representatives of your communities. A second thing I want you to focus on is continuing to hold institutions accountable,” she added.

Executive Director of PLAC, Clement Nwankwo, said the internship exposed participants to the realities of lawmaking, representation, oversight, legislative research and the day-to-day operations of the National Assembly.

He noted that the programme would equip beneficiaries to interrogate those in leadership and contribute meaningfully to national development.

Also speaking, the Clerk of the National Assembly described the PLAC legislative internship as one of Nigeria’s foremost platforms for grooming young professionals with practical knowledge of legislative practice and democratic institutions.

The programme was organized by PLAC with support from the EU Support to Democratic Governance Programme.

World.title: Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji and Nigeria’s Historical Amnesia
World.content:
By Mobolaji Sanusi

“We live in a society of imposed forgetfulness, a society that depends on public amnesia.”

— Angela Yvonne Davis (1944 – present)

Sometime last week, news filtered in that the Sardauna of Sokoto, Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji, had passed away. He was a model bureaucrat whose three names begin with the letter ‘A’, hence his media-coined moniker during his heyday and throughout his lifetime as the man with the triple As, or simply Alhaji Alhaji. One of the ‘Alhajis’ in his name was included because, like his father, he was born on Sallah Day.

In every sense, he was royalty personified. A true scion of the Sokoto Caliphate and a proud descendant of the Islamic reformer, Uthman Dan Fodio. In an interview he granted in the late 1980s, he said the greatest inconvenience he ever suffered was having to trek home from school one day because his father did not arrive as scheduled. Despite his privileged upbringing, those who follow the socio-political and economic evolution of Nigeria cannot easily forget his hard work and governance exploits. From the 1980s to the mid-1990s, he played a prominent role in the nation’s political, economic and institutional history.

His expertise in political economy was honed at Bournemouth College of Commerce and later at the University of Reading in Berkshire, United Kingdom. He also attended the IMF Institute in Washington, D.C., and the Institute of Social Studies in The Hague, Netherlands. Unlike many blue-bloods and children of the nouveau riche today who detest hard labour but seek undeserved opportunities to become overnight multi-billionaires, Alhaji Alhaji opted to join the Nigerian Civil Service in 1964. He rose through the ranks in the Federal Ministries of Finance, Trade, and Budget and Planning to become Permanent Secretary. As Principal Assistant Secretary and later Permanent Secretary in the Federal Ministry of Trade (1975 to 1978) and subsequently as Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Finance, he acquitted himself admirably.

To further tap his wealth of experience, successive military governments appointed him to higher responsibilities. He served as Executive Secretary of the FESTAC ’77 International Secretariat, later as Minister of State for Budget and Planning in 1988, and then as Minister of Finance and Economic Development from 1990 to 1991. In 1990, he was turbaned as the Sardauna of Sokoto, succeeding Sir Ahmadu Bello. From 1992, he served as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, a position he held until his retirement from public service in the mid-1990s.

He served Nigeria with all his strength when he had the option of idling away in unearned opulence. In the course of his duties as a technocrat, he became a constant feature in global institutions, including the Interim Committee of the International Monetary Fund, the Advisory Committee of Experts on Third World Debt under the Non-Aligned Movement, the Commonwealth Secretary-General’s Drafting Committee on Third World Debt, the Board of Governors of the OPEC Fund in Vienna, and the African Institute for Economic Development and Planning in Dakar, Senegal, among others. He served without blemish.

Some critics might denigrate his achievements by attributing his rise to opportunism, simply because he was a northern prince from the Caliphate. What these critics cannot take away from him is his intentionality and resolute conviction to join and stay put in the civil service, despite its routine and often boring processes, at a time when more enticing options lay before him as a Sokoto prince.

The question is: how many of today’s privileged children are willing to endure the boring routine demands of the contemporary civil service? Those who attempt to join today often do so at undeservedly high grade levels and know little or nothing about service rules and procedures. They rise to the pinnacle in barely a decade, unfairly outpacing experienced, tested and brilliant officers, even when they lack the requisite knowledge, training and experience to lead. No wonder the civil service in most states is a shadow of its old self. The toils of the likes of Samuel Manuwa, Simeon Adebo, Allison Ayida, Philip Asiodu, and indeed Abubakar Alhaji have become forgotten ideals rather than standards of service.

Shockingly, despite Alhaji Alhaji’s exploits at the highest levels of governance, it is doubtful if most young Nigerians had heard his name before or after his death. That is not entirely their fault. History as a subject, for no sensible reason, was unreasonably banished from classrooms across the country for over two decades by the civilian administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration only recently reintroduced history as a subject in schools.

Alhaji Alhaji was a prince with a difference. Born into royalty and having the rare privilege of living within the precincts of Buckingham Palace as a student in the United Kingdom, he could have, upon completion of his studies, returned to start parading himself as a businessman living off his family’s vast connections and the nation’s often fleeced public coffers, as many privileged children of power do today. Instead, he embraced hard work and dedicated himself to the civil service and to national development.

The fact that his name and legacy are largely unknown to the younger generation highlights Nigeria’s more fundamental problem of historical amnesia, which goes far beyond its numerous current challenges. We are raising a generation with little or no sense of history, yet it is a cliché that a people without a sense of their history and heritage will be obliterated. It was through the deliberate demonisation and distortion of our history that Western colonialists alienated us from our deities, norms, values, beliefs, traditions and heroes. Today, they troop to our country in droves to study and appropriate their once condemned African culture and values.

It is worth recalling that many remarkable scientific contributions were made by Black men and women who were forcibly taken to America and Europe as slaves. They were made to change their names to erase all traces of their identity and origin, barred from speaking their own languages and compelled to adopt foreign ones. They were brutalised, raped and tortured. Meanwhile, what is often projected in popular Western narratives is an image of Africa as a jungle inhabited by primates.

Sadly, we have left our own educational system in shambles and take pride in sending our wards abroad to acquire Western education to the detriment of our rich cultural and resource endowments. The country is now shamefully at the mercy of Western values and standards. This generation prefers to ‘japa’ and never look back.

Under such a forgetful atmosphere, if the new generation does not know a relatively recent and notable figure like Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji, it is futile to expect them to know former institutional heavyweights like Dr. S. O. Wey, who was the indigenous Head of the Federal Civil Service from 1961 to 1966; Chief Simeon Adebo, Head of the Western Nigeria Civil Service; Chief Jerome Udoji, the famous technocrat who led the 1974 public service review commission; Alhaji Sule Katagum, pioneer Chairman of the Federal Civil Service Commission; Dr. Samuel Manuwa, the astute federal civil servant and revered medical doctor; and Mr. M. A. Ejueyitchie, who served as Head of Service and Secretary to Prime Minister Tafawa Balewa in 1960. Allison Ayida and Philip Asiodu are also outstanding Permanent Secretaries whose contributions future generations should not forget.

That is why, even as our leaders make deliberate efforts to address the nation’s socio-economic problems, a conscious effort must also be made to revive historical consciousness among young Nigerians.

Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji’s place in history is solidified by his commitment to national duty despite being a prince with numerous other options, including idling in unmerited opulence.

The fact that President Tinubu sent a high-powered delegation led by his deputy to his funeral underscored Alhaji Alhaji’s significance. In his tribute, the President described him as “an elder statesman, a first-class technocrat and one of the prominent figures in Nigeria’s democratic and parliamentary history.” What more is there to add? Nothing, as the President has said it all.

Yours sincerely believes that not only this Sokoto prince but also other tested bureaucrats who have passed on should forever be preserved in the country’s history books. Rest well in Al-Jannah Firdaus, Alhaji Abubakar Alhaji.

To Be Reasonable Is Tinubu’s Message to EFCC

Enough of this impunity, that is the message President Bola Tinubu has sent to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, and by extension to other law enforcement agencies in the country.

The Commission obtained a court order on August 5, 2026, freezing the accounts of the Osun State Government just days before its governorship election on August 15, 2026, leaving many mouths agape.

The public considers the order, even if circumstantial, a flagrant erosion of public confidence in the democratic process. To this, President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, has said no, by directing the Commission to immediately approach the court to seek a prompt vacation of the order in the overriding public interest.

The President was right when he said he felt “deeply embarrassed, not by the EFCC’s exercise of its mandate backed by a court order, but by the timing of the agency’s action.”

On the Osun governorship election, the President is saying: let the will of the people prevail, even if the heavens fall.

World.title: ‘As it was before COVID’: Pensioners push to have payment date reversed
World.content:
SASSA beneficiaries have renewed calls for the agency to shift grant payment dates back to the start of each month, with commenters arguing the current system leaves pensioners short-changed for longer than necessary.

In response to a The South African article, Nola Van Loggerenberg raised the payment date issue head-on, comparing the current system unfavourably with pre-pandemic practice.

“At least the pensioners don’t have to wait 33 days next month for SASSA to pay out. The date should be moved back to the first of every month as it was before COVID,” she wrote.



Money doesn’t stretch far enough

Beyond the date itself, beneficiaries say the money doesn’t last once it hits their accounts. Mary Coetzee summed up the financial squeeze many pensioners face in stark terms: “Yes, that money lasts just one day.” Caroline September agreed the strain begins immediately, adding “Not just one day..up..the moment you take it out”, suggesting that for many, the grant is spent before it even reaches their pockets properly.

Caregiver and disability grant frustrations surface

The thread also surfaced deeper concerns about how SASSA assesses grant applications. Daisy Moodley shared her own experience applying for a caregiver-related grant, describing what she felt was an unreasonable expectation from officials. “OMW, they don’t give the caregiver money, apparently they want to see you in a wheelchair, my doc said yesterday. I went to fill the form saying I look so fit, 76, yet I cannot walk without someone holding me, I have a misbalance, got pins and needles in my knee,” she wrote, a comment that drew sympathetic reactions from other users.

Meanwhile, Machiliza Nomthandazoe raised a separate practical concern, asking for guidance on updating banking details on behalf of an elderly relative: “Plz help what do they need at Sassa my granny want to change her banking details.”



Together, the comments paint a picture of beneficiaries juggling delayed payments, insufficient amounts, and confusing administrative processes, all while trying to make ends meet on a fixed monthly income.

Orlando Pirates team vs Milford FC at the Orlando Amstel Arena. Image: Orlando Pirates media

Orlando Pirates starting line up: Chaine, Sibisi (captain), Seema, Sebelebele, Ndaba, Mbatha, Dansin, Maswanganyi, Appollis, Moremi, Mbuthuma.

13:00: The team buses have arrived at the Orlando Amstel Arena.

14:00: Starting line ups to be confirmed

15:00: Match kick off.

MTN8 QUARTERFINAL: ORLANDO PIRATES VS DURBAN CITY

The Soweto giants enter the clash with history firmly in their sights as they chase a record-breaking fifth consecutive MTN8 title. Orlando Pirates began their remarkable run in 2022, defeating AmaZulu 1-0 in the final. Monnapule Saleng scored the decisive goal to secure the Buccaneers’ first trophy under former coach Jose Riveiro.

They successfully defended their crown in 2023, overcoming Mamelodi Sundowns on penalties after a goalless final. Goalkeeper Sipho Chaine proved to be the difference, producing three crucial saves in the shootout.

Orlando Pirates continued their dominance in 2024, defeating Stellenbosch FC 3-1 in the final to become the first club in the PSL era to win the MTN8 three seasons in succession.

The Buccaneers extended that remarkable record last season under Abdeslam Ouaddou. They defeated Stellenbosch FC 3-0 after extra time, with Tshepang Moremi scoring twice as Pirates secured their fourth consecutive crown and 14th MTN8 title overall.

DURBAN CITY EYE UPSET

Durban City head to Soweto determined to prevent another chapter being added to Pirates’ remarkable cup history. The Nedbank Cup holders have strengthened their squad under new coach Khalil Ben Youssef. They will believe they have enough quality to challenge the defending champions.

The Citizens also know they can frustrate the Buccaneers. They held Orlando Pirates to a goalless Betway Premiership draw when the sides last met.

Victory on Saturday would take Orlando Pirates one step closer to an unprecedented fifth straight MTN8 crown, while Durban City will be targeting a major quarter-final upset at the Orlando Amstel Arena.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs mourn tragic passing of former star Michael Nkambule
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have paid tribute to former star Michael Nkambule, who tragically passed away on Friday.

The 37-year-old former footballer was involved in a car accident approximately two weeks ago. The vehicle he was driving reportedly overturned, leaving him seriously injured.

After spending two weeks in hospital, the former Chiefs midfielder sadly succumbed to his injuries, as reported by Soccer Laduma.



On Saturday, his former club paid tribute to Nkambule, remembering him as a product of the Kaizer Chiefs academy.

“Kaizer Chiefs Football Club and the entire Kaizer Chiefs family deeply regret the passing of Michael Nkambule, a former academy graduate and player for the Kaizer Chiefs first team from 2007 to 2010,” the club said in a statement.

“A product of the Kaizer Chiefs academy, who earned a move to France in 2003 after impressing scouts with his performances for the Kaizer Chiefs U15 team at the Milk Cup tournament in Northern Ireland.”

Ex-Chiefs star Nkambule dies

“Kaizer Chiefs wishes to express its condolences and support to his family, friends, and former teammates. May his soul rest in peace.”

After leaving Chiefs, Nkambule went on to represent Black Leopards and SuperSport United. However, the midfielder’s professional career did not reach the heights expected of him, and he retired before turning 30.

Despite ending his professional career early, Nkambule remained deeply involved in football and regularly featured in legends’ matches.



Which match made you a fan of Nkambule?

World.title: Medication or rent? Pensioners reveal the impossible choices R2400 forces on them
World.content:
Frustration among South African pensioners is boiling over, with beneficiaries taking to Facebook to demand an urgent increase to the Older Persons Grant, insisting the current payout is nowhere near enough to cover the basics.

Commenting under a recent The South African article on SASSA payments, Annamarie Otto laid out the brutal arithmetic pensioners face every month.

“R5000 would help us so much. Some medication costs more than R1000. Then rent…food, and the rest follows. R2420 is not enough. How can we survive???” she wrote.



Her frustration was echoed by Vani Deevichand, who framed the grant shortfall as a matter of basic human dignity for older people.

“Really speaking, old age is literally saying… the last few years of their lives …make them happy and help them live comfortably, after 60 is bunsela years God gives grace …DO THE RIGHT THING, GOVERNMENT…. R5000 IS NOT A LOT…COST OF LIVING IS HIGH,” she said.

Calls for R5000 grow louder

The demand for a R5000 grant wasn’t an isolated complaint – it was a rallying cry repeated across the comment section. Mlungisi Donda put it simply: “We now demand R5000 grant for the older people.”

Nola Van Loggerenberg went further, tying the grant amount to broader dissatisfaction with SASSA’s payment schedule, arguing that pensioners deserve both consistency and a livable amount.

“Sassa old pensioners need a decent increase up to R5000. No one can survive on R2400 a month, everything is expensive in South Africa,” she wrote, adding that “Government should do the right thing and look after these old age pensioners.”

Patience wearing thin

Not everyone believes change is coming any time soon. Casper Janse van Rensberg was blunt about his scepticism, joking, “You will only receive that R5000 once the Donkeys are out and the Horses are back”, a comment that captured the weary cynicism running through the thread.



Whether government responds to the mounting pressure remains to be seen, but one thing is clear: pensioners are no longer prepared to suffer in silence over an amount they say simply isn’t keeping up with the cost of living.

World.title: Cameron Waldeck-Cooks appears carefree in video before ‘murder’
World.content:
Cameron Waldeck-Cooks in a video captured before her death. Images via TikTok

Cameron Waldeck-Cooks was seen dancing with a group of pals, just days before her death, in a video posted on TikTok. The St Stithian Grade 11 learner was allegedly killed in a murder-suicide involving former matriculant Ethan Coetzee.

The teens’ bodies were discovered in a Sabi game lodge in Mpumalanga on Monday, 3 August.

Police have confirmed that an initial inquest has been upgraded to a murder charge.



CAMERON WALDECK-COOKS LAST DAYS

In a tribute posted by a pal on TikTok, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks joyfully danced alongside a group of friends

The blonde teen appeared happy and carefree, blissfully unaware of what would transpire a few days later.

“Here’s to you, my Cam”, her pal captioned the clip.

In the comments section, another friend added: “To think this was just a week ago”.

Watch the video here.

According to a statement from her family, Cameron Waldeck-Cooks would spend the weekend with another family at a lodge in Sabie on a hiking adventure.



On Monday, 3 August, her body and that of her alleged boyfriend, Ethan Coetzee, were discovered by his father

An independent forensic pathologist’s preliminary findings indicated that Cameron died as a result of strangulation and suffocation. Police have stated that Ethan, who was 19-years old, may have died by suicide.

BRIGHT FUTURE AHEAD

Both Cameron Waldeck-Cooks and Ethan Coetzee’s lives were tragically cut short in the double tragedy,

Cameron, a St. Stithians Girls College Grade 11 student, was working towards the Gold level of The President’s Award for Youth Empowerment, which is part of the Duke of Edinburgh’s International Award.

She was also in the rowing and netball clubs and was described as a “natural leader” and a “big sister”.

Meanwhile, Ethan – who matriculated in 2025 – had been part of the first team rugby club, was a national champion in the equestrian sport of Eventing, and was a respected senior student at Penryn House.

World.title: ‘Chiefs will be eliminated by Arrows’ – Junior Khanye predicts
World.content:
Former Kaizer Chiefs winger Junior Khanye has backed Golden Arrows to knock Amakhosi out of the MTN8 in the quarter-finals.

Chiefs return to the competition after missing out on the previous two editions. They will host Arrows on Sunday afternoon, knowing that victory would take them one step closer to lifting the trophy they last won 12 years ago.

However, Khanye remains unconvinced by Chiefs despite their impressive 3-1 victory over Kruger United in their opening match of the season last weekend.



The outspoken analyst has predicted Chiefs to suffer a narrow defeat against Arrows and exit the competition.

“For me, Chiefs will be eliminated from the tournament,” Khanye said.

“The tournament for them is unfortunately eight teams. I don’t predict a heavy score, but there is also a possibility of extra-time in this game. I think Chiefs will be eliminated if we face reality.



“Arrows will beat Chiefs, but they will narrowly edge them. I predict Arrows to win this game, but it’s going to be a tough match,” he told iDiski TV.

Khanye has also backed defending champions Orlando Pirates to beat Durban City in Saturday’s other MTN8 quarter-final.

The former Chiefs star believes the Buccaneers have enough quality to retain the trophy, which they have won four consecutive times.



Chiefs to lose to Arrows, Pirates to retain trophy, says Khanye

“Pirates are favourites,” Khanye said ahead of the MTN8 clash with City.

“They haven’t changed their team a lot. Even though they lost their star player Relebohile Mofokeng, they beefed up their squad. I know Sundowns are a threat to any team, but there’s something we call momentum. Pirates started the season very well.

“I think, for me, Pirates will defend the MTN8. It’s straightforward,” he said.



Chiefs host Arrows on Sunday while Pirates and Durban City battle it out on Saturday afternoon in Soweto.

Will Amakhosi go through?

World.title: The side hustle turning women into millionaires
World.content:
South African women are hard-working and always willing to go the extra mile for their families.

On Women’s Day, and really every day, this is something to celebrate. But women rarely receive financial recognition for their labour.

There’s one side hustle where that is different.



Women dominate this side hustle and make more money than their male counterparts.

Self-Publishing is the Side Hustle for Women

Many people talk about writing a book. Self-publishing has made this easier to do than before.

Print-on-demand books and ebooks have allowed anyone with an internet connection the option to become a writer.



Written World Media reveals Kindle Direct Publishing (KDP) paid out $699 million (R11.4 billion) to its authors in 2025. As of June 2026, KDP has paid out $384 million (R6.3 billion), a 13% increase from the previous year.

The platform allows authors without an agent to publish directly to millions of readers worldwide. Then, if readers choose to read the book on their Kindle or buy a print-on-demand copy, the author gets a percentage of that sale.

It’s here where women dominate.

According to the National Bureau of Economic Research, although women only make up 43.6% of authors published on Kindle ebooks, they receive 58.5% of the revenue as of 2021.



From Self-Published Author to Millionaire

Many women make extra money through self-publishing, but a handful of authors have turned it into a lucrative business.

Authors like Tricia O’Malley, whose book The Stolen Dog made it onto the New York Times bestseller list, first self-published on KDP.

There’s also Amanda Hocking, who became a millionaire in 2011 selling $0.99 (R15.84) ebooks on KDP.



Colleen Hoover, who would become world-renowned, started as a self-published author in 2012.

More recently, thousands of authors have used social media to make money. On TikTok, for example, the BookTok tag has reached hundreds of billions of views.

Authors like Carissa Broadbent sold thousands of copies of her debut self-published novel thanks to TikTok.



The Genres Doing Well for Women

According to selfpublishing.com, Romance is the best performing genre for female authors. The genre, which accounts for 40% of the self-published on Amazon’s KDP, grossed more than $1 billion (R16 billion) in sales in 2025.

Female authors dominate this genre.

Romance is followed by the mystery, thriller, and suspense genre, and then young adult.



Becoming a self-published author is straightforward

There’s hardly any barrier to entry when self-publishing. South African women can get started with a laptop and a free Canva account.

Writing is the most demanding part.

The average ebook is roughly 30 000 words. This is months of unpaid work, where a writer will create the plot, write, edit, and proofread.



Then there’s the cover. A good cover captures a reader’s attention online or on social media.

Finally, it’s time to publish.

Free-to-use platforms like KDP provide guides on how to publish and format the document.



But publishing doesn’t lead to success.

Like any side hustle, there will be winners and losers.

It just so happens that with self-publishing, women win more than they lose.

World.title: DJ Warras murderer gets 25 years in jail
World.content:
One of the men accused of murdering radio personality and DJ Warrick "DJ Warras" Stock has been sentenced to 25 years in prison. Image via Instagram @gagasifm

One of the men accused of murdering radio personality and DJ Warrick “DJ Warras” Stock has been sentenced to 25 years in prison by the Johannesburg High Court.

Mozambican national Joaquim Armando Pacula pleaded guilty to murder, unlawful possession of a firearm, unlawful possession of ammunition and contravening the Immigration Act.

His conviction and sentence followed a plea and sentence agreement reached with the State.



Fatally shot

DJ Warras was fatally shot outside the Zambesi building in central Johannesburg in December 2025.

Pacula has now been sentenced to 25 years’ imprisonment for his role in the killing.

The case against his co-accused, Victor Majola, remains before the court.



According to the National Prosecuting Authority, Majola’s matter has been postponed to 17 August 2026 for the conclusion of the pre-trial conference.

The latest development means Pacula will serve his sentence while the legal proceedings against Majola continue.

World.title: Pitso Mosimane named as new Bafana coach
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pitso Mosimane is set for a return to the Bafana Bafana dugout.

The South African Football Association has approved his appointment as the new national team coach following the departure of Hugo Broos.

The decision was ratified at a Safa National Executive Committee meeting, with members backing Mosimane to take charge of the side that recently made history at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

South Africa reached the knockout rounds round for the first time, highlighted by a memorable victory over South Korea.

While SAFA said a few administrative details still need to be finalised, an official announcement is expected next week.

Mosimane was previously in charge of Bafana in a caretaker capacity in 2007 and from 2010 to 2012.

World.title: RFA flags enforcement gaps in freight sector
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Road Freight Association CEO Gavin Kelly said stronger enforcement is crucial to ease tensions over foreign driver employment in South Africa’s freight sector.

With truck driver associations threatening a freight shutdown, Kelly argued the issue begins with how companies are registered and monitored.

“We are not taking the right steps when we initially register companies. When we register companies, do we ask those companies who are their employees, before we allow the company to be registered?

“We need to ask questions like are you registered with the council that is applicable to your sector of business so that we have inspectors going to all the companies that are active in that sector.

“What happens now is that inspectors to companies they are aware of and that’s the real reason we have been struggling with this. Secondly, the deterrent has to meet this problem. It doesn’t help if you get rid of these foreign nationals and they reappear or the company just employs other foreigners because that destroys the operation of the sector in totality," Kelly said.

World.title: Coalition decisions will be crucial - Mnguni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The race is on for political parties to garner votes ahead of the November local government elections.

But the reality is many municipalities may end up with coalition governments.

Rise Mzansi said fixing Johannesburg starts with principled leadership, transparent coalition agreements and no deals with parties tainted by criminality.

City of Johannesburg mayoral candidate Lukhona Mnguni said they work based on principles and coalition agreements ought to be signed.

“I do think that people are exceedingly disappointed in how the ANC is governing this city.

The ANC will probably have a huge task to justify why it must be included in a coalition. But those are conversations that become more material when you see the actual results.

“But I think starting with principles, quality of leadership, coalition agreements, and ensuring that residents have a much more transparent path to coalition formation than we have had previously,” Mnguni said.

World.title: Recovering Marchand to skip medleys at European swim champs
World.content:
PARIS - Swimming star Leon Marchand has cut back on the events he will compete in at the European championships starting Monday because of a lingering thigh injury.

The French federation confirmed Saturday that Marchand will not compete in the 200m and 400m individual medley events in Paris.

The Frenchman had already ruled out the 200m breaststroke but remains entered in the 200m butterfly and 400m freestyle that place less strain on the adductor muscles.

He may also participate in one or two relays with the French team.

"The injury is healing well, and recovery is largely complete. However, since competing in the 200m and 400m individual medley carries a non-negligible risk of recurrence, and to safeguard the remainder of the competition, the decision was made not to enter these races," explained team doctor Sebastien Le Garrec.

The four-time Olympic champion injured his adductor during the 200m breaststroke heats at the French championships in June, subsequently withdrawing from the rest of the competition.

He suffered a setback during a training session in Marseille three weeks later.

Earlier this month, he had confirmed his participation in the European championships, though he was doubtful regarding the 400m individual medley.

Ultimately, he decided to withdraw from the shorter distance as well as a precautionary measure.

The withdrawal from his two signature events is a major setback for the 24-year-old, who had made these championships the primary goal of his season.

He had also stated he wanted to break his own world record in the 400m individual medley this season.

"It's something I want to do in the near future, and I imagine doing it in Paris at the European championships would be great," he had said.

World.title: MotoGP leader Martin speeds to British Grand Prix pole
World.content:
LONDON - MotoGP world championship leader Jorge Martin set a new lap record on his way to pole position for both Saturday's sprint race and Sunday's British Grand Prix.

Spanish rider Martin was not only the fastest in Saturday's midday qualifying session in perfect conditions at the Silverstone track, but also broke the all-time lap record with a time of 1min 56.160sec.

It was the second time in two days that the record fell after Martin's Aprilia teammate Marco Bezzecchi blitzed to 1min 56.280sec in practice on Friday despite fracturing a collarbone at the German MotoGP last time out.

Italian Bezzecchi will start fifth on the grid for Saturday's 10-lap sprint race and Sunday's 20-lap Grand Prix.

Behind Martin are compatriot Raul Fernandez, riding another Aprilia for the Trackhouse team, just 0.021sec behind, followed by Japan's Ai Ogura and Italian Fabio Di Giannantonio.

The Marquez brothers, Marc and Alex, round out the top seven.

Marc Marquez revived his title defence by winning in Germany and is only 18 points behind Martin in the standings, and four points adrift of second-placed Ogura.

The top five in the championship race, with Bezzecchi in fourth and Di Giannantonio fifth, are separated by just 24 points.

The sprint race takes place at 1500 GMT.

World.title: POPCRU demands firm response to Reiger Park cop killers
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Police and Prisons Civil Rights Union (POPCRU) has the brutal killing of two members of the South African Police Service’s Anti-Gang Unit in Reiger Park, Ekurhuleni, on Friday.

Reports indicate that Two civilians were Killed. The two officers, who were part of a crime-prevention operation, heard the gunfire and moved towards the source, where they were ambushed.

In a statement, POPCRU said an attack on a police officer is an attack on the authority of the democratic state and on the safety of every South African.

“Criminals cannot be allowed to reach a point where they believe they can ambush and kill police officers with impunity. When those tasked with protecting communities are hunted down while performing their duties, society must recognise that a dangerous line has been crossed,” the statement reads in part.

POPCRU said killing of the officers could not become another statistic followed by expressions of outrage before the country simply moves on.

“Government and SAPS management must confront police killings as a national priority. The Anti-Gang Unit operates on some of the most dangerous fronts in the battle against organised and violent crime.

“Its members confront criminal networks that terrorise communities and undermine the rule of law. Sending officers into these environments without sufficient intelligence, resources and operational support places their lives at unacceptable risk.”

The union has also urged community members to work with the authorities by providing information.

“Criminals survive when communities are intimidated into silence. They must find no sanctuary in our communities.”

World.title: Alleged CIT robbers killed in shootout with KZN police
World.content:
DURBAN - Three suspects who were wanted for various violent crimes in KwaZulu-Natal were in a shootout with police in Kranskop in the early hours of Saturday morning.

KwaZulu-Natal police spokesperson Colonel Robert Netshiunda said police acted on intelligence which uncovered the whereabout of the suspects and when they approached a residence at Mambulu area.

“A shootout ensued between police and an unknown number of suspects. Three suspects were shot and fatally wounded during the shootout and they were found in possession of firearms.

“The suspects are linked to a CIT robbery which happened in the Kranskop CBD on 13 April 2026 where suspects also fired shots at a police station,” he said.

One of the suspects was injured during the explosion of the CIT vehicle and was found dead inside an abandoned vehicle in Nkandla a day after the CIT robbery.

Netshiunda said a search is ongoing for more suspects who are believed to have evaded arrest and are armed, at least with a rifle.

World.title: ‘We sincerely apologise’ – COJ deputy mayor on uncollected refuse
World.content:
SOWETO – City of Johannesburg deputy mayor Loyiso Masuku has apologised to residents for the lack of service delivery as a result of strike at Pikitup.

“Let me start by sincerely apologising to the residents of the City of Johannesburg. Disruption is waste collection is an unfortunate situation,” she said.

Johannesburg authorities are racing to regain control of the City.

They are negotiating with striking Pikitup casual workers. Protesters have paused disruptions to waste collection.

They warn they will resume the strike if talks fail by Tuesday. Meanwhile, the City said it is working to clear the waste collection backlog.

Masuku said they have been trying to clear the backlog since Monday.

“As of today, we can confirm with you that 11 out of our 12 depot areas are actually functional. We are working throughout the weekend and the public holiday to clear the backlog so that when we resume our normal schedule at least the backlog has been cleared.

“We are an honest government. We are not in a position to absorb all 385 casual workers. Remember these casual workers are contracted to the service provider that actually has an SLA (Service Level Agreement) with the City.

“So they are not casual workers who work for the City of Joburg, they work for the company that is contracted. But we are honest that we are not in a position right now. However, the engagements that Pikitup management has been having with them is looking at different solutions gradually how the situation can be met,” she added.

World.title: Killing of Mt Elgon politician linked to planned controversial cleansing ritual
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Mt Elgon politician Nathan Wasama was shot on Thursday evening outside his house. [Courtesy]

The slain Mt Elgon politician Nathan Wasama was leading a cleansing ritual that involved cutting down two significant fig trees in Mt Elgon and Trans-Nzoia, which elders blamed for misfortune affecting the Sabaot and Bukusu communities.

The ceremony had faced strong opposition over the past year from a senior politician in Mt Elgon because of its perceived political significance.

Unknown assailants shot Wasama on Thursday evening outside his house as he stepped out of the bathroom at around 7pm.

Nothing was stolen during the shooting, heightening tensions in Bungoma and Trans-Nzoia counties.

Wasama, a former Chesikaki councillor, was among Laibon elders seeking security to fell the two fig trees, which their forefathers had guided them to cut down after 100 years of their existence.

The elders had criticised what they described as attempts by some leaders to frustrate the cleansing ritual.

"This is a crucial ceremony, but we are facing frustration and intimidation from some senior politicians that the cutting of the fig trees will have a negative political impact," Wasama told journalists in January this year in Kitale.

Some residents interviewed linked Wasama's killing to the planned ritual and his interest in the Mt Elgon parliamentary seat.

"The motive is clear: the planned ritual and politics. Unfortunately, those responsible for Wasama's death are shedding crocodile tears," confided a resident who declined to be named for security reasons.

Anger among residents was evident when they confronted Bungoma County Police Commander Anderson Njagi after a security team visited Wasama's home on Friday.

Despite Njagi's assurance that five people linked to the killing were being pursued, residents demanded the arrest of the alleged financier of the attack.

"Go for the financier of this killing. We know him, and he should be held accountable," shouted the residents.

Njagi attributed insecurity in the area to illegal guns allegedly possessed by elements of the Sabaot Land Defence Forces (SLDF).
