World.title: What Does New Pension Increase Mean for Defenders Who Worked After War?
World.content:
August the 7th, 2026 – There is set to be a new pension increase for Croatian defenders, but what will the situation be for those who did continue working after the war ended?

Index reports that the government has now presented a new model for increasing defenders’ pensions, which should apply from the 1st of January 2027 if the legislative amendments pass in Parliament. Among the beneficiaries covered by the changes are also defenders who returned to work after the war.

A defender who returned to work after the war and later retired under the old-age pension scheme basically receives a pension calculated in the same way as other workers, according to years of service and salaries. Then, as a defender, the pension is additionally increased depending on the time spent in the war, especially in the combat sector.

The position of these defenders was precisely one of the main reasons why Možemo demanded a change in the calculation method that would raise the pensions of the covered beneficiaries by up to 20 percent.

The Government today presented a different model under which the new supplement depends directly on the wartime service record. For every month spent in the combat sector the pension would be higher by three euros per month, and for a month in the non-combat sector by 50 cents.

Around 68,000 defenders are drawing pensions from the general system

In the refined proposal by Možemo, 68,561 beneficiaries are listed whose pensions are calculated primarily according to the rules of the general pension system, but with the application of defenders’ rights. On average they had around 31 years of service, and the average pension amounted to 668.37 euros.

The Ministry today presented a very similar current figure of 68,269 beneficiaries in that category.

Možemo intended its proposal primarily for defenders who returned to the labour market after the war and proposed an increase in the starting factor, which could raise their pensions by up to 20 percent. A higher factor would also apply when determining the lowest defenders’ pension.

The Government’s supplement is calculated completely differently. Its amount does not depend on the amount of the current pension, but on the number of months spent in the war and whether it was in the combat or non-combat sector.

what would an actual concrete example of that look like?

Let us take a simplified example of a defender who today receives 668.37 euros, which is the average pension of the mentioned group. If we assume that under the Možemo proposal he would achieve the full 20 percent increase, he would receive around 134 euros more per month, meaning his pension would rise to around 802 euros. Under the Croatian Government’s model, the increase would depend on the length of combat service.

In this concrete example the Government’s supplement would overtake the 20 percent increase after approximately three years and nine months spent in the combat sector.

This isn’t a universal threshold. For every defender, everything depends on their current pension and how large an increase that individual would achieve under the Možemo proposal. In this example, for simplicity, it was assumed that the person did not participate in the non-combat sector.

The length of participation in the war already today affects certain defenders’ pension rights. The Možemo proposal would not change that, but the new increase would not depend directly on whether someone spent one year or five years in the combat sector. Under the Government’s proposal that is precisely the main criterion for the new supplement. One year of combat service means 36 euros more per month, three years 108 euros, and five years 180 euros. The difference between the combat and non-combat sectors is also large. Five years in the non-combat sector would bring a monthly increase of 30 euros, while five years of combat service would bring 180 euros.

government proposals encompass a wider number of people

The Government’s increase isn’t intended only for defenders who continued working after the war. The Ministry announced today that the new supplement according to wartime service will be received by 104,560 defenders, while various proposed amendments would cover a total of 201,304 defenders and members of their families.

Defenders who continued working are thus included in the Government’s model, but they are not singled out as a special group. In other words, Možemo proposed an increase of up to 20 percent for a narrower circle of beneficiaries, while the Government proposes a supplement for a wider circle of defenders whose amount will depend directly on the number of months spent in the combat and non-combat sectors.

former pension reductions are also being scrapped

The Government also proposes the abolition of the pension reduction of 8 to 20 percent that is still applied to some retired soldiers, police officers and other authorised officials. This is a separate measure, distinct from the new supplement calculated according to the time spent in the Homeland War.

The abolition of the reduction should from 2027 cover around 34,000 beneficiaries, and the Ministry estimates that their pensions would as a result rise on average by around 70 euros per month. This measure is not limited only to defenders, but applies to all beneficiaries covered by that special pension regulation. The Government’s amendments have not yet been adopted. After public consultation they should be sent to the parliamentary procedure, and application is planned as of the 1st of January 2027.

World.title: Croatian Mountain Rescue Service Rescues Another Foreign National on Biokovo
World.content:
August the 7th, 2026 – The Croatian Mountain Rescue Service (HGSS) has had to rescue yet another foreign national stuck on Biokovo.

As Index reports, the Croatian Mountain Rescue Service (HGSS) has reported a night-time rescue of a foreign national who got lost last night in the area of Sutvid above Živogošće near Makarska, at around 1,050 metres above sea level on the southeastern part of Biokovo. HGSS received the call on Wednesday at around 18:30.

The man reported that due to high temperatures and lack of water he had become severely dehydrated, felt extreme weakness and was no longer able to safely continue moving or find the way. Four rescuers from the HGSS Makarska Station immediately set out into the field, and due to the demanding terrain they were soon joined by another four.

“After several hours of night ascent, the rescuers reached the injured person at 22:50. First aid was provided at the scene and after a rest and rehydration, accompanied by the rescuers, he began the descent towards the vehicle,” the HGSS Makarska Station announced.

The operation was successfully completed at 02:50. Photos published by HGSS show that the man had set out on the ascent in sandals. HGSS once again warns everyone not to go into the mountains without appropriate equipment and a sufficient amount of fluids.

“We’d once again like to appeal to all visitors to Biokovo to please, please carefully plan their trip before going into the mountains. During the summer months it is absolutely paramount that you bring a sufficient amount of water, avoid the hottest part of the day and use appropriate hiking footwear,” HGSS said.

World.title: This Croatian Island is Closer to Italy Than to the Mainland of its Own Country
World.content:
August the 7th, 2026 – There’s a far-flung Croatian island that is closer to neighbouring Italy than to the Croatian mainland. Only a lighthouse keeper lives there, and he’d be able to arrive on Italian shores much more quickly than he’d manage to arrive in Croatia.

Far out in the Adriatic Sea sits an isolated island from which, on a clear day, both shores of the Adriatic are clearly visible. Putni kofer writes that only a lighthouse keeper lives there, and day-trippers rarely stop by.

If you look at a map of the Adriatic and study the area from Split towards the shores of Italy, you will see the islands of Brač, then Hvar, then the more distant Vis and Korčula, followed by the open-sea island of Biševo… After that long stretch there is nothing, only deep blue emptiness, and then, almost in the middle of the open sea, another “little dot”. That’s Vela Palagruža, Croatia’s most remote island of all. It’s a narrow rocky islet barely a kilometre and a half long. From here to the Italian coast, you’ll cover just 68 kilometres, while to Split it is more than 120. In other words, this piece of Croatia is almost twice as close to foreign land as to its own.

this position made the island so important

It is precisely this position that for centuries gave Palagruža an importance out of all proportion to its size. It is the only point on the Adriatic from which, in clear weather, both the Italian and Croatian coasts can be made out, so for thousands of years the island served as a landmark and resting place on the long voyages between the Italian shore and Dalmatia.

Archaeologists have been confirming this for decades. At the Salamandrija site, on the plateau right next to the lighthouse, traces of human presence going deep into prehistory have been found, and in later periods the island became a sanctuary for seafarers. Finds of pottery inscribed with the name of Diomedes, the hero from the Iliad, confirmed that Palagruža was a place where sailors paid homage to him before setting out onto the open sea.

it remained under italian control until 1860

Until 1860, Palagruža was under Italian administration. When the Austrian authorities took it over, a lookout service was established on the island, and then in 1875 the lighthouse was built. Twenty years later a meteorological station was added. Since then Palagruža has never been without people.

The stone lighthouse stands in the middle of the island at 90 metres above sea level; with its lantern it rises to about 126 metres above the sea. A steep path about 700 metres long leads up to it – a real mountaineering stretch on which donkeys once helped the lighthouse keepers. About ten years ago they were replaced by a cable winch built specifically for this purpose.

the lighthouse keeper welcomes guests… but rarely

Today only the lighthouse keeper lives on Palagruža all year round; in the past entire lighthouse families – more than ten people – used to stay there. It is he who, during the summer, welcomes the guests who manage to reach this little piece of paradise.

And for those rare visitors that means exactly what it sounds like. There is no shop, restaurant, bar or pharmacy. There is not even the possibility of quickly buying something extra. Plovput looks after the lighthouse, and through them one can arrange summer accommodation in one of the two four-bed apartments, with a minimum stay of seven days. The building stands high on the island’s ridge, so a stay is not recommended for people in poorer health. What you get in return is hard to compare with anything else on the Adriatic: silence, the sea on all sides, and the feeling that you are on a planet of your own.

the highest number of endemic plants in all of southern dalmatia

Vela Palagruža is 1,400 metres long and only 300 metres wide, with gentler slopes on one side and vertical cliffs on the other. The climate is exceptionally mild and rainfall is scarce, so vegetation is lush in spring, autumn and winter, while in summer the coast is almost bare. Among the islands of southern Dalmatia, Palagruža has the most endemic plants. Here grow the Palagruža cabbage, Palagruža centaury, Palagruža horsetail, open-sea spurge and other species you will not find elsewhere. The archipelago around the main island also includes Mala Palagruža and a series of rocks and reefs. To the south-east lies the islet of Galijula, officially the southernmost land point of Croatia.

the former home of the richest fishing grounds in the entire adriatic

The waters around Palagruža were once one of the richest fishing grounds in the Adriatic. Today lobster and white fish are mainly caught here, and the area remains primarily a fishing zone. Visits have to be arranged with the lighthouse keepers or with one of the fishermen from Komiža; organised group excursions practically do not exist. For a place of this kind, that is probably not bad news.

World.title: Iraq oil exports drop 75% amid Hormuz closure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Oil Minister Hayan Abdul-Ghani announced on Saturday, August 8, 2026, that the nation’s crude oil exports have plummeted by 75% due to the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz and regional military escalations. The severe drop in oil revenues has triggered a liquidity squeeze across the federal government, causing widespread delays in state employee salary disbursements.

Speaking at a press conference in Baghdad, Abdul-Ghani revealed that Iraq is currently exporting only a quarter of its pre-war volumes, which stood at approximately 3.5 million barrels per day (bpd) prior to the outbreak of regional hostilities on February 28. He noted that while Baghdad has engaged in diplomatic talks with Iran to permit the passage of Iraqi oil shipments through the Gulf, no operational agreement has been activated.

Key financial and operational highlights

Export Collapse: Iraq’s crude exports have fallen to ~25% of pre-war capacity, cutting off the primary source of state revenue.

Fiscal Pressure & Salary Delays: Reduced export volumes and below-budget sale prices have caused acute liquidity shortages, delaying public sector payrolls.

Corporate Damage Compensation: Domestic Attacks: Baghdad has agreed to compensate foreign energy companies for damages resulting from attacks originating inside Iraqi territory. External Strikes: The government declared itself legally exempt from compensating firms for damages caused by foreign strikes or broader military actions beyond state control.

Alternative Export Bypasses: Baghdad is fast-tracking pipeline infrastructure projects bypassing the Persian Gulf, including routes south toward Turkey’s Ceyhan port, Syria’s Baniyas terminal, and Jordan’s Aqaba port.

To maintain minimal cash flows, Iraq is currently forced to sell its crude at deep price concessions below the baseline benchmark set in the national budget, compounding treasury deficits.

In response to the prolonged maritime chokehold in the Strait of Hormuz, the Ministry of Oil is accelerating infrastructure development along overland export routes.

Priority has been placed on expanding and constructing pipeline corridors connecting southern production hubs to the Mediterranean via Syria and Turkey, alongside long-term transit planning toward the Red Sea via Jordan.

World.title: Iraq activates Kirkuk oil field development contract with BP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Saturday, August 8, 2026, the official activation of its Kirkuk oilfield development contract with British energy giant BP. The project aims to elevate crude oil production from its current capacity of 320,000 barrels per day (bpd) to a peak target of 420,000 bpd.

Ministry of Oil Spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi stated that the contract—initially signed in September 2025—focuses on expanding crude extraction while capturing associated natural gas to eliminate routine flaring and feed domestic power generation infrastructure.

Key operational targets & metrics

Crude Oil Output: Increasing current production from 320,000 bpd to a peak target of 420,000 bpd.

Associated Gas Capture: Raising associated gas processing from 255 million standard cubic feet per day (scf/d) to a peak capacity of 400 million scf/d.

Facility Modernization: Upgrading and expanding infrastructure across North Oil Company fields and North Gas Company processing plants.

Power & Social Infrastructure: Constructing a dedicated 400-megawatt (MW) power plant, expanding local employment, funding community development initiatives, and upskilling North Oil and North Gas workforces.

Environmental Impact: Phasing out continuous gas flaring to redirect captured methane directly into national electricity generation.

The activation of the Kirkuk project represents a major component of Iraq’s broader energy strategy to achieve natural gas self-sufficiency and reduce reliance on imported fuel.

By upgrading processing facilities managed by the North Gas Company and constructing a dedicated 400 MW power generation facility, the initiative directly addresses regional electricity shortages while reducing environmental emissions.

The partnership also reinforces BP’s operational footprint in northern Iraq, complementing its long-standing management of the Southern Rumaila field and bolstering state-led efforts to modernize national energy infrastructure.

World.title: India’s Reliance pays record $25 million freight cost for Iraqi crude amid Hormuz crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — India’s Reliance Industries (RELI.NS), operator of the world’s largest refining complex in Gujarat, paid an unprecedented record charter fee of $23 million to $25 million for a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) to transport 2 million barrels of Basrah crude from Iraq, according to shipping sources cited by Reuters on Friday, August 7, 2026.

The extreme freight surge—marking a jump from a pre-war average of $2 million to 12 times the baseline global freight rate—highlights severe shipping chokepoints in the Strait of Hormuz caused by the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict. Daily vessel transits through the strategic waterway have plummeted from a pre-war average of 125–140 ships to a fraction of normal capacity as shipowners avoid military risks.

Key financial & logistics metrics

Soaring Freight Rates: Reliance chartered the VLCC from South Korea’s Sinokor at 1,200 points on the Worldscale freight index—12 times the reference benchmark—up from pre-war levels of 0.8 to 0.9 times ($2 million total).

Deep SOMO Discounts: To offset soaring shipping costs and attract buyers into the Gulf, the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) offered steep discounts of $25 to $30 per barrel below Dubai regional benchmarks.

Net Margin Offset: Despite the $25 million freight tag, energy analysts estimate Reliance will still save millions on the overall transaction due to Iraq’s heavy crude price reductions.

Limited Carrier Pool: Sinokor remains one of the few international maritime operators willing to navigate the Strait of Hormuz to load cargo at Iraq’s Basra Oil Terminal.

While Asian refiners—particularly across India and China—are actively seeking chartered tankers to capture Iraq’s discounted crude allocations, shipowner reluctance continues to limit available tonnage entering the Gulf.

By offering deep price concessions, Iraq’s oil marketing arm is successfully maintaining crude flow off the Basra coast despite soaring war-risk insurance premiums and maritime transport bottlenecks.

World.title: Kata’ib Sayyid Al Shuhada clarifies delay in retaliatory strikes against U.S.-Saudi targets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Abu Ala al-Walai, Secretary-General of Kata’ib Sayyid al-Shuhada, commented on Saturday, August 8, 2026, regarding the decision by the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” to pause planned military responses to recent joint U.S.-Saudi strikes.

Speaking via a statement on social media platform X, al-Walai confirmed that the delay was granted at the direct request of Coordination Framework leaders, led by Badr Organization chief Hadi al-Amiri, alongside several independent political figures. However, the paramilitary commander emphasized that options for retaliation—including the reassessment of its timing, scale, and nature—remain fully on the table. He urged state officials to utilize this temporary window to secure Iraq’s rights through diplomatic and legal channels.

Key developments in the escalation pause

The Deferred Response: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq announced on Friday, August 7, the postponement of retaliatory operations originally scheduled for the 23rd of Safar targeting Saudi Arabia and U.S. military bases.

Al-Amiri’s Appeal: Badr Organization leader Hadi al-Amiri issued an urgent video address early Friday urging armed factions to delay military action following American-Saudi strikes on Iraqi territory, prioritizing national stability while pursuing accountability for casualties via diplomatic means.

High Security Readiness: The political appeal followed a volatile night across Baghdad and multiple governorates, prompting high-level security alerts and military deployments across the capital.

Command Structure On Site: In response to directives from Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi to elevate combat readiness, senior commanders from Baghdad Operations Command were deployed on the ground to enforce military discipline and secure vital sectors.

The brief pause in military operations provides a critical window for Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s administration to manage state security, navigate delicate diplomatic channels with Washington and Riyadh, and prevent further regional escalation.

World.title: Iraq fish deaths: 7 alarming signs of a deepening water and pollution crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Recurring Iraq fish deaths are becoming an increasingly serious environmental and economic warning, with the Green Iraq Observatory describing the phenomenon as an annual pattern that reflects the accumulation of two interconnected crises: worsening water scarcity and persistent pollution.

Rather than representing isolated incidents caused by temporary changes in river conditions, the repeated deaths of large numbers of fish across Iraq’s rivers, canals and marshlands suggest that the country’s aquatic ecosystems are coming under sustained pressure from declining water flows, untreated wastewater, industrial pollution and weaknesses in water management.

The latest incidents, recorded in April and August 2026, have once again raised concerns about the condition of Iraq’s freshwater resources and the government’s ability to protect them. According to the observatory, more than 1,000 tonnes of fish died in the Tigris and Diyala rivers during April, with particularly heavy losses reported in Wasit province, while a separate incident occurred earlier this month in the Al-Amshan Canal in Maysan.

Although the two incidents were associated with different immediate circumstances, they demonstrate how vulnerable Iraq’s aquatic ecosystems have become when declining water levels interact with pollution and inadequate environmental controls.

Iraq fish deaths are becoming an annual warning sign

The Green Iraq Observatory argues that the recurrence of mass fish deaths should no longer be treated as a series of unrelated environmental emergencies. According to its assessment, similar incidents have occurred repeatedly across different parts of Iraq over the past several years, yet the underlying causes have not been addressed with sufficient consistency to prevent them from returning.

This pattern is particularly concerning because rivers and wetlands are not only ecological assets; they also support fisheries, agriculture and the livelihoods of communities that depend directly on healthy waterways.

The observatory said the April incident involved more than 1,000 tonnes of dead fish in the Tigris and Diyala rivers, with the largest losses concentrated in Wasit. It attributed the event to severe contamination caused by untreated sewage and industrial waste, while also pointing to increased water releases from Hamrin Dam that reportedly moved accumulated pollutants downstream toward the Tigris.

The organization further said that more than 20 people experienced poisoning or skin-related injuries and were taken to hospital, illustrating how deterioration in water quality can potentially extend beyond damage to aquatic life and become a broader public-health concern.

A second incident was reported at the beginning of August in the Al-Amshan Canal in Maysan. According to the observatory, the agriculture and water committee of the Maysan Provincial Council attributed the fish deaths to a sharp decline in the water releases allocated to the canal.

This episode is significant because it demonstrates that pollution is not necessarily the only immediate trigger for fish mortality; inadequate water flows can also create conditions in which fish become increasingly vulnerable to high temperatures, reduced oxygen levels and the concentration of pollutants already present in the water.

Water scarcity Is only part of the problem

Iraq’s water crisis is frequently discussed in terms of declining river flows, prolonged drought and reductions in water arriving from upstream countries. Those factors are undoubtedly important, but the recent fish deaths suggest that the country’s environmental problems cannot be explained simply by saying that Iraq does not have enough water. The quality, distribution and management of the water available can be just as important as its overall volume.

The Green Iraq Observatory highlighted this distinction by noting that the country’s total water storage had reportedly risen to around 34 billion cubic meters at the time of the latest incident.

From the organization’s perspective, the fact that fish mortality continued despite an increase in total reserves indicates that administrative decisions concerning water distribution may be contributing to the problem alongside genuine resource scarcity.

This does not mean that Iraq’s wider water shortage is unimportant. On the contrary, prolonged drought and declining inflows can weaken the natural ability of rivers and wetlands to dilute pollutants and maintain ecological balance. However, when available water is distributed unevenly or when polluted water is allowed to enter already stressed waterways, the consequences can become significantly more severe.

In other words, the crisis is not simply about how much water Iraq has, but also about where the water goes, what quality it has and how effectively it is managed.

Pollution can turn a water shortage into an ecological emergency

Untreated sewage and industrial waste are among the most serious threats facing Iraq’s waterways because they can fundamentally alter the chemical and biological conditions required for aquatic life. When large quantities of organic material enter a river or canal, microorganisms consume oxygen while breaking that material down, potentially reducing dissolved oxygen to levels that fish and other aquatic organisms cannot tolerate.

The situation can become even more complicated when water temperatures rise or when algae proliferate excessively. Some forms of harmful algae can contribute to oxygen depletion, particularly when large quantities of organic matter subsequently decompose.

At the same time, reduced water flows can prevent pollutants from being dispersed naturally, leaving them concentrated in particular sections of a river, canal or wetland.

This combination of factors helps explain why pollution and water scarcity should not be treated as completely separate problems. A waterway with strong flows may have a greater capacity to dilute certain pollutants, whereas a shallow and poorly circulated waterway can become significantly more vulnerable to contamination.

Consequently, environmental protection requires both adequate water releases and strict control over what is discharged into the country’s rivers.

Iraq has experienced similar fish mortality events for years

The latest incidents are not without precedent. The Green Iraq Observatory cited a long record of mass fish mortality events in Iraq, including a major incident in the Euphrates in Babylon in 2018, when tens of thousands of tonnes of fish were reportedly affected.

This was followed by the death of millions of fish at the Hindiya Barrage and another major incident in Al-Dalm Marsh in Diwaniyah in 2020.

Further incidents were reported in the Al-Ezz River in Maysan in 2023, while extensive fish deaths occurred in Ibn Najm Marsh in Najaf last year. Particularly worrying is the recurrence of fish mortality in the Maysan area where a similar incident had already been recorded, because repeated events in the same geographic location can indicate that the environmental conditions responsible for the original problem have not been adequately corrected.

The observatory argues that the repeated nature of these incidents is difficult to reconcile with a system that relies primarily on temporary investigative committees after environmental damage has already occurred. Investigations can establish causes and responsibility, but they cannot substitute for permanent monitoring mechanisms capable of identifying dangerous changes in water quality before they result in large-scale ecological losses.

Iraq’s Marshlands face particular risks

The Iraqi marshlands are especially sensitive to changes in water availability and quality because their ecological health depends on a delicate relationship between water flows, seasonal conditions and the surrounding environment. These wetlands provide habitat for fish and birds while supporting communities whose economic and cultural lives have developed around them over generations.

When water levels fall sharply, sections of the marshes can become isolated or excessively shallow, increasing temperatures and reducing oxygen circulation. If polluted water enters these already stressed environments, the damage can become significantly more difficult to reverse.

Protecting Iraq’s marshlands therefore requires a long-term approach that connects water policy with environmental policy. Maintaining adequate ecological flows, reducing pollution and establishing continuous monitoring systems would be far more effective than treating each fish mortality event as an isolated emergency.

What Iraq can do to prevent future fish deaths

The Green Iraq Observatory has called for several measures aimed at addressing the structural causes behind recurring fish mortality. Among its recommendations is the establishment of fair and sustainable water allocations for provinces and marshlands, rather than relying on short-term decisions that may leave some waterways dangerously depleted.

The observatory has also called for stronger environmental oversight of wastewater treatment facilities and industrial establishments located near rivers. Effective enforcement would require more than regulations on paper; authorities would need regular inspections, reliable water-quality testing and meaningful consequences for facilities that discharge untreated or inadequately treated waste.

Another important proposal is the creation of an early-warning system that monitors dissolved oxygen and pollution levels. Such a system could bring together government agencies, universities and civil-society organizations, allowing scientific data to be collected continuously and shared quickly when dangerous changes are detected.

Finally, rapid compensation for fish farmers affected by major environmental incidents could provide essential economic relief while investigations determine responsibility and long-term solutions.

No. Water scarcity is an important contributing factor, but pollution and poor water management can also play major roles. Even when overall water reserves increase, individual rivers, canals or marshes may experience insufficient flows or deteriorating water quality.

World.title: US Fed sends $500 million cash shipment to Iraq amid financial pressures
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The United States Federal Reserve has sent a new $500 million cash cargo to the Central Bank of Iraq, providing additional dollar liquidity as Baghdad grapples with rising financial pressures and disruptions to its oil-dependent economy.

The shipment was announced by Iraq’s national news agency, citing an official source who claimed the dollars will be used for permitted overseas transfers and transactions involving Iraqi citizens.

Further supplies are planned each month, with a government official estimating annual cash delivery of $8 billion to $10 billion.

These cash payments are part of Iraq’s peculiar financial relationship with the United States.

Proceeds from Iraqi oil exports are mostly placed in an account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, with Baghdad obtaining dollars via permitted transfers and cash shipments administered by the Central Bank of Iraq.

The new supply comes at a critical moment for Iraq’s budget.

The disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has increased pressure on a nation that relies significantly on oil exports to support government expenditures and get foreign currency.

Iraq’s enormous public-sector pay bill contributes to this vulnerability.

Millions of Iraqis rely directly or indirectly on government wages, pensions, and social benefits; therefore, stable oil income and liquidity are crucial to the national budget.

Baghdad has lately expressed increased worries about its capacity to fulfill expenditure obligations if oil earnings continue low, strengthening long-standing demands for Iraq to diversify government income and lessen its reliance on petroleum exports.

The most recent dollar cargo should offer further liquidity to Iraq’s banking system, but it also shows the country’s vulnerability to both oil-market shocks and its financial ties with Washington at a time of rising regional tensions.

World.title: Lise Klaveness, the Norwegian thorn in Infantino’s side
World.content:
Oslo – A rare woman in the top echelons of football, the head of Norway’s federation Lise Klaveness has been a thorn in FIFA’s side for years.

Now, some would gladly see her take over the leadership of football’s international governing body from Gianni Infantino.

The 45-year-old lawyer and former footballer who played 73 matches for Norway has been highly vocal about international football’s woes under Infantino.

The Swiss-Italian has been mired in controversy since his plan to open FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors was swiftly rejected last week.

On Friday she called for him to resign.

When he was elected FIFA president in 2016, “he was a candidate who had been elected on a reform programme focused on good governance,” she told AFP.

“Then things quickly deteriorated: from keeping a distance, we moved to giving up, and even backtracking, all against a backdrop of a lack of independence from heads of state and other influential figures, particularly from World Cup host countries,” she said.

She fired her first salvo at Infantino in 2022, just after she was appointed head of the Norwegian federation, about the conditions under which the World Cup was awarded to Qatar.

From Doha, she publicly lamented that “human rights, equality, democracy, the core interests of football, were not in the starting 11”.

The following year, Norway refused to back Infantino in his re-election bid, signalling its dissatisfaction with his leadership.

Klaveness “was in a way the first standard-bearer for much of this criticism that many others now share when it comes to the way Infantino runs FIFA,” said Mina Finsted Berg, a sports commentator for Norwegian channel TV2.

She “is very committed to ensuring that rules and decisions are respected,” she added.

– Trump, Balogun and investors –

The reasons for her outrage against Infantino have piled up in recent months: FIFA’s decision to award a “Peace Prize” to US President Donald Trump, with whom Infantino has a conspicuously close relationship; the lifting of the suspension of US player Folarin Balogun at the 2026 World Cup following an intervention by Trump; and the aborted plan to open FIFA to private investors.

The Norwegian federation has decided to bring all three issues before the Ethics Committee of the world football governing body.

Klaveness’s voice carries all the more weight after Norway, long absent from major international tournaments, enjoyed a strong run in this year’s World Cup before being knocked out in the quarter-finals by England.

Internationally, commentators have praised her “strong moral compass” and consider her a serious candidate to replace Infantino if he were to step down.

He is standing for re-election for a fourth and final term next March and is currently the only declared candidate.

“She was the only one who always took a clear stand and did not go along with the mainstream. And at FIFA, the time is right for a woman to take the lead,” former FIFA head Sepp Blatter — himself disgraced after a corruption scandal — wrote on social network X.

– Ballot box obstacles –

Klaveness herself has insisted that the crisis in world football should not be reduced to a simple “Game of Thrones” power struggle and has instead called for a renewed focus on good governance.

“For us, it has never been a personal issue against Gianni Infantino,” she told AFP. “The problems go beyond the person of the president.”

And while she “has registered” that her name is being tossed around as a possible successor, she brushed aside questions about whether she was a candidate: “We’re not there yet.”

Many obstacles remain.

“In addition to being seen as extremely radical in many places, especially outside Europe, she is a woman. That is also likely to count against her in many regions of the world,” Mina Finsted Berg said.

Even within Europe’s governing body UEFA, which one could presume would be most favourable to her, Klaveness failed to win election to the Executive Committee in 2023.

She only joined in 2025, when she was the sole candidate for the seat reserved for women.

“If she already has such a hard time getting elected in Europe, how could she convince Africans and South Americans?” asked Erik Thorstvedt, a former goalkeeper for the Norwegian national team turned commentator.

World.title: Clinton compares Trump’s White House to former Iraqi dictator Saddam’s palaces
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton has compared President Donald Trump’s White House renovations to former Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein’s palaces, remembering her own travels to Baghdad after his ouster.

Clinton, speaking on journalist Kara Swisher’s podcast, compared Trump’s White House decor to meetings she attended in Saddam Hussein’s former palaces while serving as a US senator.

“They were quite reminiscent of what we are seeing in our own White House,” she said.

Her remarks come amid wider criticism of Trump’s renovations and architectural decisions, such as heavy gold décor within the Oval Office, plans for a new White House ballroom, and a projected triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

Clinton called the improvements “tacky” and suggested that the president was focusing too much on cosmetic initiatives when the US confronts substantial foreign policy, economic, and technological issues.

She also criticized the process around Trump’s planned ballroom, stating that she was not opposed to the White House having such a facility but was concerned about the architecture and how the project had been handled.

Given Clinton’s past with Iraq, the connection to Saddam was especially relevant.

She was a member of the United States Senate during the 2003 war that deposed Saddam Hussein and subsequently became Secretary of State under President Barack Obama.

During his reign, Saddam was noted for building multiple extravagant presidential palaces around Iraq, many with elaborate interiors and significant use of marble, chandeliers, and gold-colored décor, despite the country’s international sanctions and economic difficulty.

Trump has defended his White House restoration plans, which are part of a larger push to renovate and enhance Washington’s important federal buildings and sites.

Clinton’s parallel brings Iraq and one of Saddam’s most recognizable emblems into the increasingly heated political argument over Trump’s White House moves.

World.title: Supriya Sule opposes FCRA Bill, urges Centre to withdraw it or send it to JPC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) working president

on Saturday opposed the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 in its present form, urging the Centre either to withdraw the proposed legislation or refer it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) for wider discussion.

Sule, the Lok Sabha MP from Baramati, said all political parties should be given an opportunity to examine the contentious legislation before Parliament takes it up for consideration. She cautioned the government against rushing the bill through Parliament, amid reports that it could be discussed and passed next week.

âWe reject and disagree with the present form of the FCRA bill. If the government is not ready to withdraw the bill, then it should send it to a JPC.

In a strong democracy, merely opposing something is not enough; we also have to sit together and discuss it,â she said.

The proposed legislation seeks to establish a designated authority for the vesting, supervision, management and disposal of foreign contributions and assets in cases involving cancellation, surrender or expiry of an organisationâs FCRA registration.

The bill also provides for provisional and permanent vesting of such assets.





Critics have argued that the proposed changes could give the government greater control over organisations receiving foreign contributions.

â Foreign funding cannot always be viewed with suspicionâ

Sule said foreign funding should not automatically be treated with suspicion, arguing that overseas contributions can support legitimate work in areas such as healthcare and education.

She said action should be taken if foreign funds are linked to illegal activities such as drug trafficking or terrorism, but questioned the rationale for viewing every foreign-funded organisation negatively.

âThere are organisations such as the Gates Foundation and USAID that have been doing good work for many years. Why should we look at every foreign-funded organisation with a bad eye?â she said.

She also compared foreign funding with money sent home by Indians living abroad, arguing that the source of money alone should not determine whether it is viewed negatively.

According to official figures, 13,520 entities received foreign remittances totalling Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.

As of July 15, 2026, there were 14,449 active FCRA registrations, while 22,498 registrations had been cancelled and 15,212 had expired.

The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable institutions, educational bodies, religious trusts and other organisations.

Sule backs youth protests, questions party symbol decisions

Sule also commented on the ongoing protests by students, saying young people should not face such treatment while seeking education.

âWhat happened at Jantar Mantar should not happen anywhere in the country. Our children want to study and this is happening to them. I read that ministers from Jharkhand have ordered an inquiry into it,â she said.

She also backed Uddhav Thackeray in the dispute over the Shiv Sena's name and election symbol, arguing that party organisations and constitutions should be considered while deciding control of political parties.

On the NCP dispute, Sule said the legal battle remained unresolved and alleged that her party had been waiting for a hearing.

âSharad Pawar is the founder president of the NCP and injustice has been done to him. We have been asking for a date for a long time, but why are we not getting a date?â she said.

Sule further said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had agreed to meet NCP (SP) MPs on Monday to discuss issues concerning their constituencies, amid the opposition's contention that Parliament was not functioning properly.

World.title: Explainer: What changes as Parliament passes Registration of Births and Deaths Bill
World.content:
The Parliament passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amid a wider logjam that has repeatedly disrupted the Monsoon Session. The Rajya Sabha cleared the legislation on Tuesday by voice vote days after the Lok Sabha passed it on July 31 amid opposition protests without a debate.

Both Houses witnessed repeated adjournments during the session, with several Bills being passed amid disruptions. The Monsoon Session began on July 20 and is scheduled to conclude on August 13.

The new legislation focuses on a seemingly routine but important part of government records like registering births and deaths. A birth certificate records a person's entry into the official system, while a death certificate formally records their departure.

Together, these documents help establish identity, maintain public records and provide proof for a range of legal and administrative purposes. The amendment seeks to tighten the process when such events are reported long after they occur.

What does the Bill change?

Under the existing system, delayed registration already requires additional verification. If information about a birth or death is submitted after one year but within two years, the amended law will require an order from a district magistrate, sub-divisional magistrate or an executive magistrate authorised by the district magistrate.





For cases reported more than two years after the event, the threshold becomes higher. The registration will require an order from a judicial magistrate of the First Class having jurisdiction over the place where the birth or death occurred.

The magistrate will have to verify the correctness of the information before permitting registration. A prescribed fee will also have to be paid, according to a document released by the government.

The amendment also updates the reference to an "Executive Magistrate" in the 1969 law to align it with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the earlier Code of Criminal Procedure.

The government says the primary objective is to ensure that births and deaths are registered promptly and that delayed registrations are subjected to stronger scrutiny.

The Registration of Births and Deaths Act makes registration mandatory.

According to the government's statement of objects and reasons, birth and death certificates provide legal identity and can be used as evidence of a person's birth or death.

The government argues that the integrity of these records is particularly important because birth certificates can be used for several official purposes, including processes involving identity and citizenship-related documentation.

Tighter scrutiny of delayed registrations, it says, can help prevent fraudulent or questionable entries and improve the reliability of official records.

BJP IT cell head Amit Malviya said, âThe objective is straightforward: encourage timely registration, prevent fraudulent or dubious entries, and preserve the credibility of birth and death certificates, the foundational documents that establish a personâs legal identity.â

The government has also pointed to a significant rise in registration rates over the past decade.

Union minister of state for home Nityanand Rai said birth registration increased from 86.6% in 2014 to 99.1% in 2024, while death registration rose from 72.5% to 99.4% during the same period.

He also said around 3.5 lakh registration centres have been established across the country.

The government's argument is that as registration coverage approaches universal levels, the focus must increasingly be on ensuring that the remaining delayed or questionable cases are properly verified.

What is the significance of a birth certificate?

A birth certificate is often the first formal document linking an individual to the state. It records details such as a person's date and place of birth and can be required for a range of official purposes, including education, employment, passports and other government documentation.

The government has also highlighted the role of birth records in establishing identity and in processes where proof of birth or citizenship-related documentation is required.

That makes the accuracy of the registration system important beyond population statistics.

A fraudulent birth certificate, for instance, could potentially affect records across several government systems. Similarly, failure to register deaths can leave outdated information in official databases.

The government has also linked accurate death registration with keeping records, including electoral rolls, updated.

What happened in the Parliament?

The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on July 31 by voice vote amid opposition protests. Several opposition MPs entered the Well of the House demanding the presence of Union home minister

, and the legislation was cleared without a debate.

Parliamentary affairs minister

criticised the opposition for not participating in the proceedings and said the government wanted a discussion on the "important Bill".

âIt is unfortunate. Please do not repeat this in the future. People who sent you to Parliament will seek answers from you,â Rijiju said, urging MPs to participate in debates rather than disrupt proceedings.

The legislation was passed amid continued sloganeering, with the opposition MPs demanding the presence of Union home minister Amit Shah and his response on the "police action" against student protesters on July 20 at Jantar Mantar.

The Rajya Sabha later took up the Bill amid similar disruptions.

Moving the Bill in the Rajya Sabha, Rai said the government wanted every birth and death to be properly recorded. He said, âThe country wants that anyone born in the country, it is important that he or she is registered. Anyone who has died, cannot continue to remain in the voter lists to benefit some parties.â

Rai also linked the legislation to concerns over people who have died continuing to appear on electoral rolls.

The country now wants to get rid of ghosts. There are govts in some states that look for an opportunity and welcome those (who were not born in India) and register their births who are not eligible to be registered here. Now, we will not allow this to happen. Union minister of state for home Nityanand Rai

He also cited the rise in registration rates as evidence of the government's efforts to improve the system.

Some NDA members supported the legislation. YSRCP member M R Reddy, AIADMK's M Thambidurai and BRS member Ravi Chandra Vaddiraju backed the Bill. BJP member Biswajit Sinha, meanwhile, accused the Congress of opposing the legislation because it did not want proper registration of births and deaths.

Sinha also referred to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in West Bengal, claiming that people who had died years earlier remained on voter lists.

He alleged that some parties were helping illegal Bangladeshi and Pakistani infiltrators obtain birth registrations and voter identities, and said the proposed changes would help prevent such practices.

Leader of opposition

said, âThe prime minister and the home minister should come. we want discussion.â

Despite the protests, the Bill was taken up for consideration and passage.

Why did the opposition say

Opposition members did not reject the need for accurate birth and death records but questioned the practical implications of requiring a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class to approve registrations delayed by more than two years.

UPPL member Pramod Boro said the objective of the Bill was important but questioned whether an administrative responsibility should be shifted to the judiciary.

He warned that the provision could add to the workload of courts, increase costs and make registration more difficult for migrants, homeless people, poor families and those living in remote areas.

BJD member Santrupt Misra also questioned why registrations are delayed in the first place.

He suggested that the government should identify the reasons behind late registration and consider dedicated registration offices, particularly in tribal areas, to improve access.

CPI(M) member V Sivadasan supported the need for proper registration but said the government should also focus on the circumstances surrounding deaths, including malnutrition and student deaths.

The passage came amid a wider logjam in the Monsoon Session, with repeated adjournments in both Houses and several Bills being cleared amid disruptions.

With Parliament having passed the Bill, the legislation will now go through the remaining constitutional process before coming into force. The Bill, therefore, seeks to strike a balance between two objectives: ensuring that births and deaths are recorded promptly, while subjecting unusually delayed registrations to greater scrutiny.

World.title: 21 of 57 TN MPs attend CM Vijay’s meet, reject Delimitation Bill; DMK, AIADMK stay away
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu MPs on Saturday "unanimously" decided to oppose Centre's Delimitation Bill after chief minister C Joseph Vijay chaired a meeting to discuss its likely impact on the state.Congress MP Karti Chidambaram said around 21 out of 57 Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha MPs attended the meeting and agreed to resist any alteration in Tamil Nadu's representation in Parliament."The chief minister of Tamil Nadu had called for a meeting for all the MPs from Tamil Nadu from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. About 21 of us attended the meeting, and there was absolute unanimity that Tamil Nadu's rights must be preserved. Our representation in Parliament can't be diminished. Any kind of alteration and delimitation, either on the basis of population or on a proportionate increase, will be resisted," Chidambaram said."We want Parliament to be frozen at 543, and the distribution among the states to be preserved as it is, which means Tamil Nadu will have 39 members in a House of 543. We are clear in our unanimous opinion that a larger Parliament will be an ineffective Parliament, and Tamil Nadu will not be well served by a larger Parliament.So we want Parliament to be preserved at 543 with the same representation of 39 Lok Sabha MPs for Tamil Nadu," he added.The meeting was boycotted by the DMK and AIADMK, which dismissed the deliberations as a "farce" and a "drama".The meeting was held at Kalaivanar Arangam, a government-owned auditorium near the Secretariat.Senior DMK leader A Raja told reporters in Perambalur that it was "a farce, a laughable exercise", arguing that the TVK government was deliberating on an issue about which it had no clarity.Meanwhile, AIADMK called the meeting a "hurriedly staged drama", pointing out that no new delimitation Bill had been introduced in Parliament and there had been no official announcement on the exercise.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed linking its implementation to the delimitation exercise. The opposition has demanded that women's reservation be delinked from delimitation.The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, was passed by both Houses of Parliament. However, its implementation has not moved forward after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill fell in the Lok Sabha on April 17, failing to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.The Bill linked the implementation of 33 percent women's reservation in legislatures to delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies.

World.title: India to recover 'Green Boots' climber's body from Everest after 30 years: Report
World.content:
The body of an Indian climber believed to have become the mountaineering worldâs infamous âGreen Bootsâ could finally be brought down from Mount Everest, three decades after he died while descending from the summit.

India is preparing a high-altitude recovery mission to retrieve the remains of Dorje Morup, an

(ITBP) personnel who died on Mount Everest in 1996, according to a detailed report by the BBC.

Morupâs body has remained frozen at about 8,500 metres on the northern side of Everest for nearly 30 years. The remains became known among climbers as âGreen Bootsâ because of the distinctive bright green mountaineering boots visible on the body.

The ITBP is now looking for a specialist team capable of undertaking the difficult recovery operation. The force hopes to bring the remains back to India by September, after which DNA testing would be carried out to establish Morupâs identity conclusively, the BBC reported.

If the identification is confirmed, his remains will be returned to his family in Ladakh.

The climber behind the â Green Boots â mystery

Morup was 48 when he joined a six-member ITBP expedition that attempted to climb Everest from the Chinese side in 1996.





The expedition was seeking to become the first Indian team to reach the summit from that route.

Three members of the expedition eventually turned back because of a snowstorm, while Morup and fellow climbers Tsewang Smanla and Tsewang Paljor continued towards the summit.

All three reached the top, but disaster struck as they attempted to descend.

A blizzard hit the mountain and killed the three climbers. Their bodies were left on Everest, as recovering bodies from the mountain is itself an extremely dangerous undertaking.

For years, the body now known as âGreen Bootsâ was assumed to belong to Paljor. However, surviving members of the 1996 expedition, along with information about the climbersâ final radio communications and the location of the body, have led authorities to believe that it was actually Morup.

An ITBP official told BBC that Morupâs clothing and climbing equipment had also helped authorities identify the remains in recent years.

The body has since become one of the most recognisable markers on the route to Everestâs summit, passed by climbers making their way through the mountainâs notorious âdeath zoneâ.

For Morupâs family in Ladakh, the operation could finally resolve a mystery that has lasted three decades.

His wife, Konchak Yangskit, told the BBC that she struggled to accept his death because she had never seen his body.

Morup had told her before leaving for the expedition that he would return home after making the country proud.

He had also asked her to look after their children and come to the airport to receive him when he returned.

His son, Punchok Dorjai, told the BBC that the family plans to hold a funeral near Martyrs Park in Leh if the remains are confirmed as his.

He also said the family intends to keep the green boots that gave Morup's remains their enduring identity on Everest.

A delegation of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) arrived in Ranchi on Saturday to extend support to students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the party stood in âcomplete solidarityâ with the protesting students and would provide them with all forms of support.âCJP stands in complete solidarity with the students of Jharkhand,â Ranka said in a post on X.He added that the delegation was travelling under the leadership of Mukallrounder and Akshay Shinde and would support the students during their ongoing agitation.Speaking to PTI, CJP national coordinator Mukesh said the party fully supports students protesting over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC examinations and repeated paper leaks. âWe stand with the students and will continue to support them,â he said, adding that the party would share its experience from the Jantar Mantar movement with the protesting students.âOur support may not be from the stage, but we are standing with them,â Mukesh said, asserting that the CJP would continue backing the students until there is transparency in recruitment examinations and paper leaks are stopped.âTill when will this continue to happen?â he asked.The protests in Jharkhand have intensified following allegations of irregularities in recruitment examinations. World.title: 'Which freedom fighter received most severe punishment?' Kerala orders probe into Savarkar quiz
World.content:
File photo: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar

Education department says quiz was not authorised

Pinarayi Vijayan accuses government of 'colluding' with RSS

Left groups, IUML leaders criticise question

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A political row has erupted in Kerala over a school quiz question that described Hindutva ideologue Vinayak Damodar Savarkar as the freedom fighter who received the "most severe punishment" from the British, prompting general education minister N Samsudheen to order an inquiry.The "Freedom Quiz" was conducted on August 6 for lower primary students in schools in the Kasaragod, Kumbla and Manjeshwar sub-districts, according to news agency PTI.The disputed question asked: "Who is the freedom fighter that received the most severe punishment from the British?" Savarkar was given as the answer.The minister's office said Samsudheen has directed the director of general education to establish who prepared and conducted the quiz and take stringent action against those responsible.According to the minister's office, the quiz was not included in the activity calendar of either the Social Science Club or the General Education Department. Neither had authorised anyone to independently prepare the questions or conduct the competition."The person who included the historically incorrect question holds a prejudiced view," the minister's office said, adding that the Education Director had been instructed to identify those responsible and take strict action.As per PTI, teachers associated with the Social Science Club had prepared the questionnaire.The controversy has since drawn criticism from the CPI(M) and Left-affiliated student and youth organisations, which accused the Congress-led UDF government of allowing what they described as a "Sangh Parivar agenda" to enter the education system.CPI(M) veteran and former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan accused the UDF government of "colluding" with the RSS and alleged that efforts were being made to conceal Savarkar's history and glorify him.Addressing a press conference in Kannur, Vijayan alleged that the Centre and the RSS were attempting to "rewrite history". He also linked the controversy to the Centre's efforts to implement its new education policy in Kerala.Former general education minister V Sivankutty also criticised the question, alleging that it was part of an attempt to "saffronise" Kerala's general education sector and distort the history of India's freedom struggle.Sivankutty demanded a comprehensive inquiry, strict action against those responsible and the withdrawal of the disputed question and answer. He also sought an apology from the General Education Department.SFI state secretary P S Sanjeev alleged that the quiz sought to portray Savarkar as a freedom fighter. In a social media post, he criticised the UDF government and alleged that the general education portfolio was being used to create space for the Sangh Parivar.DYFI state secretary K Sanoj also criticised the government, saying there was no justification for a school quiz to contain a question that allegedly glorified Savarkar.Senior Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leader and former minister M K Muneer said portraying Savarkar as a patriot was part of the RSS-BJP agenda.Muneer, however, said that if the question had indeed been included in the quiz, the matter should be seriously examined and those responsible identified, adding that it should not be treated lightly.

World.title: 'Army safeguarding territory': Arunachal CM Pema Khandu rejects Chinese encroachment
World.content:
Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu on Saturday rejected reports of Chinese military encroachment in the state and said that the Army was effectively patrolling and safeguarding the territory.Speaking to reporters, Khandu said, "No signs of encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh; Indian Army effectively patrolling and safeguarding the territory."Khandu's remarks came a day after the Centre identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on the official map of the country, amid China's repeated attempts to rename places in the border state.The government said the exercise was aimed at ensuring the correct identification of the locations and improving public awareness of their geographical and historical significance."Identifying them formally on the Survey of India map of Arunachal Pradesh is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large," an official statement said.New Delhi has consistently rejected Beijing's practice of assigning Chinese names to places in Arunachal Pradesh, calling the move "vain and preposterous".India has maintained that such actions do not alter the "undeniable" fact that Arunachal Pradesh "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of the country.Several of the locations newly marked on the official map hold strategic importance because of their proximity to the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and their role in past India-China military confrontations.Among them is Long Ju, one of the earliest flashpoints between the two countries. Chinese troops entered the area in 1959, three years before the 1962 India-China war.The official map also includes Maja village in Upper Subansiri district near Long Ju, Bisa village and the strategically significant mountain passes of Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La.Another key location is Thag La, the high-altitude pass where one of the opening battles of the 1962 India-China war took place.Jairampur in Changlang district has also been formally identified. The town serves as an important logistics hub for the movement of security forces towards eastern Arunachal Pradesh and the Myanmar border.Other locations added to the map include the high-altitude lake Sambho Sarovar, Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun, Dhan Bari, Pritnagar, Teritnagar, Ramnagar, Jaswant Garh, Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar, Baisakhi, Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, Chhota Ropuk, Bara Ropuk, Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura, Kamlang Nagar and Buddhamandir.India has repeatedly dismissed China's attempts to assign what it calls "fictitious names" to places in Arunachal Pradesh, saying such efforts seek to create "baseless narratives" and cannot alter the "undeniable" reality on the ground. New Delhi has also warned that such actions could undermine efforts to improve bilateral ties.China first issued a list of six standardised names for places in what it calls Zangnan in 2017. It followed this with a second list covering 15 locations in 2021 and another naming 11 places in 2023. Beijing uses the term Zangnan to refer to Arunachal Pradesh, a claim India has consistently rejected.

World.title: Supreme Court directs MEA to trace Indian seafarer missing after Black Sea drone attack
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) asked the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to use its diplomatic channel and trace a seafarer missing after his cargo ship was struck by drones on July 25 in the Black Sea.

Also read: Indian seafarer killed in attack on ship in Black Sea

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to seek instruction from the Indian Embassy in Ukraine and Embassy of India, Bucharest, Romania and enquire about the whereabouts of Deepak Kumar Gupta, who was onboard cargo ship, MV AGN Ragnar.

The matter is listed for hearing on Friday (August 7, 2026).

The Supreme Court was hearing a plea by Sandeep Kumar Gupta, elder brother of the missing seafarer, seeking directions to the MEA to coordinate with Indian embassies in Ukraine and Romania to undertake search and rescue operations.

The plea was filed by Mr. Sandeep Kumar Gupta after his family’s persistent requests to the Union of India and Indian embassies in the two countries went unheard.

The plea contended that the family wrote to the MEA and the Indian embassies in the two countries between July 26 and July 30 but the representations did not evoke any response or any positive assurance.

The 22-year-old seafarer went missing after a merchant vessel carrying Indian crew members came under attack near Ukraine’s Odesa port.

Comment | Should Indian seafarers stop serving on sanctioned ships?

According to family members, Mr. Deepak Kumar Gupta, a resident of Bharataul village in Bareilly district, was working as a crew member aboard the merchant vessel MV AGN Ragnar.

Mr. Deepak Kumar Gupta’s family originally hails from Siwan district in Bihar but has been residing in Bharataul village in Bareilly for several years.

World.title: Sanjay Raut slams RSS over CJP protest ‘anti-constitutional’ remark
World.content:
Shiv Sena(UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Monday (August 3, 2026) responded to a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leader’s comment calling the protest at Jantar Mantar ‘anti-national’. “How can a protest be anti-constitutional? No protest can be anti-constitutional,” he said.

“The history of the RSS is their ideology. They do not respect the Indian Constitution. They do not respect the tricolour. They do not respect India’s independence. They have never hoisted the tricolour over their office for the last 52 years. They want to create an independent constitution. That’s why they have created a group of 50 MP’s to destroy the Constitution,” Mr. Raut said.

Questioning the protests that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has held over the years, Mr. Raut said, “To call a protest anti-national is an insult to Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar’s Constitution. Then the protests carried out by the Bharatiya Janata Party over the last many years fit under which Constitution? The protest by Jayaprakash Narayan in 1975 within which Constitution’s framework? A respected leader of the RSS should tell the country that we, and the BJP, are not ready to respect the Constitution while running this country,” he said.

“The country’s youth gathered at Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of a corrupt Education Minister, due to whom 20 students took their lives. If anyone thinks that asking for his resignation is not normal, then this Sangh person’s mentality should be checked,” Mr. Raut said.

“My challenge to the RSS leaders is that they should say whether the agitation at Jantar Mantar was unconstitutional or not, because the statement should be understood,” he added.

RSS leader Atul Limaye had said that the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar should be viewed as a weapon against the Constitution. He said this while addressing activists of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, earlier this week.

“If we want to become a developed nation, as Bharat Ji said in his speech, we need a significant contribution from our youth. But what kind of youth do we need? What values should they have? What dreams should they pursue? These are questions we must decide very carefully and thoughtfully,” Mr. Limaye said.

“This protest should not be viewed merely from a political perspective or simply as anti-BJP. It should be seen as a protest that has been used as a weapon against the Constitution. It should also be viewed as a protest raised against the nation, against India. We need to understand this force from that perspective,” Mr. Limaye added.

World.title: Home Minister Shah must explain in Parliament lathicharge-pellet gun action on students: Kharge
World.content:
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Monday (August 3, 2026) demanded that Home Minister Amit Shah should come to Parliament and explain the lathicharge-pellet gun action on protesting students.

The Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha also demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi should answer how the donations to the Ram temple were stolen.

"Modi government will have to answer INDIA. Home Minister should come to Parliament and explain the lathicharge-pellet gun action on students.

"Prime Minister should answer how the 'chhanda-chdhawa' donated to Shri Ram Mandir, was stolen, even as the Trust was under PM's oversight," Mr. Kharge said on X after a meeting of INDIA bloc party floor leaders at his chamber in Parliament House complex.

The Opposition has been seeking a statement from the Home Minister on the police action against protesting students on July 20, including use of pellet guns, and have also demanded his resignation over the issue.

Besides Mr. Kharge, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress general secretaries Jairam Ramesh and K.C. Vebugopal, SP's Dharmendra Yadav, TMC's Mahua Moitra and Sagarika Ghose, NCP (SP)'s Supriya Sule, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Sanjay Raut and Arvind Sawant, JMM's Mahua Maji, CPI(M)'s John Brittas and CPI's P Santhosh Kumar, RSP's N.K. Premchandran, among others, participated in the meeting.

The INDIA bloc has vowed to corner the government on issues of alleged donation theft and the use of "brutal force" against students during their protests over the NEET paper leak.

World.title: Madras High Court refuses to quash FIR against former DMK MLA L. Idhayavarman
World.content:
The Madras High Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) refused to quash a First Information Report (FIR) registered by the Mamallapuram police against former DMK MLA and incumbent Thiruporur Panchayat Union Chairman L. Idhayavarman for having allegedly caused damage to public property at the Nemmeli seawater desalination plant just before Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s visit on July 6, 2026.

Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan dismissed the FIR quash plea and directed the police to complete the investigation and file the final report within four weeks. The orders were passed after watching a video clip submitted by State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan of the former MLA causing damage to the green safety nets put up by the Chennai Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (CMWSSB).

The SPP claimed the video clip was shared by the DMK IT wing on social media. He said that it showed the entire incident, right from the moment when the former MLA stepped out of his car and went on a rampage ripping the nets put around a culvert, which was under repair because of the damage caused due to its proximity to the main road and consequent heavy vehicular vibrations.

CMWSSB Assistant Engineer V. Malarselvam had lodged a complaint with the police on July 7, 2026, alleging that the former MLA had come to the desalination plant, along with two others, at around 9.30 p.m. on July 5, 2026, and ripped the safety nets, causing a loss of ₹10,000 to the public exchequer. The complainant had urged the court to register a FIR and initiate appropriate criminal action against the offenders.

Former MLA’s plea

On the other hand, the former MLA, in his FIR quash plea, said he had visited the desalination plant on July 5, 2026, only on receipt of information that the CMWSSB officials had removed a plaque containing the name of his party leader and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin who had inaugurated the plant in 2024 and had used green safety nets to cover the plaque during the visit of the incumbent Chief Minister.

Denying the charge of having caused damage to public property, the petitioner claimed the case had been registered due to political motives. He added that the media had covered extensively as to how the officials had used green nets to cover the name of the former Chief Minister.

World.title: Sparsha Darshan at Srisailam only at night on Saturdays, Sundays and Mondays
World.content:
Srisailam temple Executive Officer M. Srinivasa Rao has said changes have been made to the protocol Sparsha Darshan for the convenience of general devotees.

According to Mr. Srinivasa Rao, Sparsha Darshan will be provided only during specific night-time slots on three days of the week, Saturday, Sunday and Monday. There will be no Sparsha Darshan during the morning and afternoon hours on these three days.

On the remaining days, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, Sparsha Darshan will be provided three times a day at the scheduled times, as usual. However, during the coming month of Sravana, it will not be available during the morning and afternoon hours on Fridays either.

The temple administration has asked dignitaries visiting the temple to give their visit details at least two days in advance. The Executive Officer asked that recommendation letters for accommodation and darshan be submitted to the Devasthanam on official letterheads at least two days before the visit.

The letters may be sent to protocol@srisailadevasthanam.org, or on WhatsApp to 9160016215.

World.title: Kharge attacks RSS over freedom struggle, says Congress has the ‘real patriots’
World.content:
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday (August 8, 2026) stepped up his attack on the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), questioning its contribution to the freedom struggle and accusing the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its ideological mentor of “lecturing” the Congress on patriotism despite having played no role in the fight against British rule.

Also Read | RSS helped the British while Congress fought for freedom: Rahul Gandhi

Addressing a rally in Haldwani, Mr. Kharge sounded the poll bugle for the Uttarakhand Assembly election, which is scheduled in 2027. Invoking Mahatma Gandhi’s call to ‘do or die’ on August 8, 1942, the Congress chief said the Quit India Movement had united Indians against British rule and ultimately led to their departure from the country.

“It is an auspicious day today and we have sounded the conch shell for victory from here. This will usher in change and the Congress will form the government here,” Mr. Kharge said, linking the historic occasion to the Congress rally.

The Congress chief said no genuine BJP or Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) member had gone to jail during the freedom struggle. “The BJP and the RSS have done nothing for the country’s freedom struggle. The truth is, we are the real patriots. They are the deserters,” he said.

Mr. Kharge also accused the BJP and RSS of “looting in the name of religion”, referring to alleged irregularities involving temple donations. He named Kedarnath, Badrinath, and the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, alleging that those accused of taking devotees’ offerings were now branding their political opponents as being against God. “When I stand up to speak on this in Parliament, BJP MPs start creating a ruckus,” the Congress leader said.

Taking aim at the BJP government in Uttarakhand, Mr. Kharge questioned its ‘double-engine’ governance model and alleged that ₹1,000 crore was being spent annually on publicity and propaganda. “Whose money is this?
